Straight line winds knocked a tree down onto a house in Bay. Power lines were also knocked down in the area.
Heavy rain flooded Walnut Street in Blytheville causing the street to be impassable.
Straight line winds blew several trees and power lines down in the Horseshoe Lake area. Approximately, 700 people were without power during the peak outage.
Straight line winds knocked down several tree limbs at two residences northwest of Sharon. In addition, trees were knocked down on Travis Chapel Road, southwest of Dresden.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in the town of Coahoma.
Straight line winds blew a large tree down on a house on Brown Street in Arlington.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the Bartlett-East Memphis area. Interstate 240 at Walnut Grove was flooded. In addition, Walnut Grove at Farm Road was flooded. Flooding also occurred at Mullins Station Road and Sycamore View.
Straight line winds knocked trees down onto Highway 72 near Slayden.
Straight line winds blew several large tree limbs down southwest of Leach. Winds were estimated at 60 mph when the storm moved through Hollow Rock.
Straight line winds blew trees down near Glendale. Several trees fell onto roads some of which were Glendale Road, Clarks Creek Road and Jones Road.
Straight line winds knocked trees down in and around Lexington.
Winds were measured at 58 mph just west of Parsons.
Penny size hail reported near the Coahoma County - Bolivar County line.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Sabino.

Straight line winds knocked down power lines on U.S. Highway 61 near Dundee. Trees were also knocked down on Old U.S. 61 along with 10-15 power poles and power lines on Casino Strip. Winds were measured at 61 mph at the Tunica AWOS. An aircraft hangar was damaged as well. Power outages were reported on the north side of the county.
Quarter size hail fell in Western and Central DeSoto County.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in Ellistown.
Half dollar to golf ball size hail fell in Southhaven. The hail was reported in the Snowden Grove area of Southaven and at the intersection of Goodman and Getwell Roads as well.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in Olive Branch.
A privacy fence was blown down on Leslie Lane in Olive Branch. In addition, a large 6 ft. in diameter tree was knocked down at the Olive Branch Middle School. An awning was knocked down as well.

A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of County Road 127 and County Road 128, approximately 3 miles east of New Albany. Several large trees were uprooted and one fell onto a house and caused major damage. One additional home received major damage with 24 homes receiving minor damage. A mobile home sustained partial roof loss while 10 mobile homes received minor damage.

A tornado briefly touched down west of County Road 305, approximately 3 miles southeast of Manila. The tornado tracked north-northeast for about 2 miles and moved across Mallard Lake. The tornado track was within Big Lake Wildlife Management Area. A few trees were snapped as a result of the tornado.

A tornado touched down just south of Hamilton Road along Highway 45 in New Hamilton. The tornado tracked northeast for seven miles and lifted near Bartahatchie Road, approximately one mile east of the intersection of Bartahatchie Road and Grubb Springs Road. Numerous trees were uprooted along the track. Traffic lights were severely damaged at the intersection of Highway 45 and Hamilton Road. One house near the beginning of the track suffered structural damage losing a garage and utility room. Several homes also sustained roof damage. A few vehicles also received damage from falling trees or other debris. One person was injured when a tree fell onto a vehicle. A small steel outbuilding was also destroyed with debris from the outbuilding being wrapped in amongst surrounding trees. A support on a built in carport was destroyed allowing a portion of the home roof to collapse. Several power lines were also knocked down along Hamilton and Grubbs Springs Road. In total, 9 homes sustained major damage from the tornado with 35 homes receiving minor damage. In addition, 3 mobile homes sustained major damage and 7 received minor damage. One business was destroyed, one business sustained major damage and 3 received minor damage. Several vehicles were damaged as well. Timber damage alone from the tornado was reported to be around 92 thousand dollars.

A tornado touched down on Bible Hill Road, approximately 2 miles north-northwest of Parsons. The tornado traveled east-northeast for about 11 miles crossing the Tennessee River and continuing into Perry County, Tennessee.  Significant tree damage occurred along the track, especially on Brodie's Landing Road. Although minor damage occurred to most structures hit directly from the tornado, significant property damage occurred from falling trees. In total, 15 homes sustained damage. Three of these homes were completely destroyed. Seven homes received major damage while five had minor damage. One business had a roof blown off while one barn was completely destroyed.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell in Hickory Hill.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in the Cordova area. Golf ball size hail was reported at the National Weather Service Office.
Penny to golf ball size hail fell in Piperton.
Nickel to golf ball size hail fell in the Germantown area.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell in the Collierville area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Downtown Olive Branch.
Golf ball size hail fell in Arlington.
Straight line winds knocked down trees just west of McNairy.
Straight line winds blew a roof off of a mobile home in Sweet Lips.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down just north of Madison.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Corinth. An underpass on a major road was flooded and closed as a result. Cass Street was covered with water as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Eastern Union County.
Straight line winds destroyed a shed in Clarksdale.
Quarter size hail fell in the Monroe County portion of Nettleton.

Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down in the Berclair and Raleigh areas. A tree was knocked down onto a vehicle at the intersection of North Graham Street and Macon Road. In addition, a large tree fell onto a house on Victor Drive. A tree knocked down power lines on Jewell Road.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Midtown Memphis. Several of these trees fell near the intersection of Hawthorne Street and Galloway Avenue.
Winds were measured at 63 mph at the intersection of Interstate 69 and Highway 61.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the Midtown to East Memphis area. The viaduct at Union Avenue and Poplar Avenue was flooded as well as Poplar Avenue near the  intersection of Highland Street.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Memphis International Airport. Water depth reached the wheel wells of several cars at the intersection of Winchester Road and Plough Road. One person was injured when their vehicle hydroplaned into a power pole.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Germantown. Southbound Kimbrough Road between Wolf River Boulevard and Farmington Boulevard was flooded with 1 foot of water. Farmington Boulevard near Germantown Road was flooded with water higher than the curb.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Cordova. Streets inside the Countrywood Subdivision were flooded. Dexter Road was covered with 6-8 inches of water between Appling Road and Germantown Parkway.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Arlington. Hayes Road was covered with 6-8 inches as a result.

Straight line winds produced damage between Ellendale and Arlington. Limbs with the diameter of a baseball were knocked down at the intersection of Summer Avenue and Appling Road. A tree was uprooted and a greenhouse structure was destroyed in Arlington. Power poles were knocked down in Arlington as well.
Straight line winds blew a roof off of a house and damaged a chimney on another house in Belmont.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 59 near Highway 70.
Straight line winds blew a roof off of a car dealership in Humboldt. Several trees were knocked down in the area as well.
Straight line winds blew trees down along Wolfe Road and Vernon Road near the Alabama State Line.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power poles near Cottage Grove and Puryear.
Golf ball size hail fell between Cades and Milan.
Quarter to softball size hail fell in the Henderson area.
Golf ball size hail fell in New Hamilton.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Highway 100 east of Henderson.
Penny size hail fell in Parker's Crossroads.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Highway 70 in Huntingdon. Additional trees and power lines were knocked down near Trezevant, Atwood, Hollow Rock and Westport.
Straight line winds produced widespread tree damage across Henderson County.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell east and south of Lexington including the Pine Lake area.
Heavy rain flooded a low water crossing 3 miles east of Lexington. A subdivision road and several yards were flooded as a result.
Quarter size hail fell 2 miles west of Pickwick Dam.
Straight line winds severely damaged two camper trailers when winds blew one into the other near Pocahontas.
Straight line winds produced damage near the intersection of U.S. Highway 49 and Punkin Center Road. One building collapsed while power lines and small trees were knocked down as well.
Heavy rain produced widespread flooding in College City. Numerous streets were flooded.
Straight line winds damaged trees from U.S. Highway 135 to the Mississippi County line near County Road 884, south of Caraway. In addition, a tree fell on a house off County Road 885.

Straight line winds blew a shed down and knocked power lines down near Manila. An awning was blown off of a gas station on Main Street in Manila. Several limbs and a large tree was knocked down as well. Fifteen power poles were broken and thrown about a 100 feet into a field between Milligan Ridge and Manila. In addition, tree tops were damaged in the area.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in McKenzie. Several trees fell onto homes causing structural damage. Power lines were also knocked down in the area.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Milan. A couple of trees fell onto a vehicle and a house causing damage.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near the Lauderdale-Haywood County line, east of Henning. Significant property damage occurred to homes in the area from fallen trees.
Straight line winds knocked down 20 trees across Weakley County stretching from Dresden to the Henry/Carroll County line.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding northeast of Paris. A culvert was washed out on Somerset Drive as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Paris.
Lightning struck a detached garage on Boswell Road near Summer Avenue near Memphis. The garage caught fire as a result.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Jonesboro. The intersection of Matthews Avenue and Madison Street was flooded as well as Aggie Road and Azalea Lane. In addition, Burke Avenue and Culberhouse Street was flooded.
Heavy rain produced widespread flooding in College City. Numerous streets were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked a few tree limbs and power lines down near Martin. Winds were estimated at 72 mph.

Very heavy rain produced widespread flooding in portions of Mississippi County especially the Osceola area where at least 35 homes were affected by flood waters. At any one point homes had anywhere from two inches to up to a foot of water inside. The most concentrated area of flooded homes occurred near the Osceola Country Club. In Wilson, flooding forced the closure of Hampson Archaeological Museum State Park, which had 4 feet on its grounds and seepage occurred inside the museum building. In Lepanto, several homes were flooded. In total, 70 homes were affected by flood waters in Mississippi County where eight inches of rain fell in less than a 24 hour period.

Very heavy rain fell during the day across Madison County. As much as 11 to 16 inches fell across the county. Forty roads and bridges were closed due to the flooding. Vehicles had water up to the steering wheels in some locations. Power outages occurred as a result of the flooding. Houses were inundated with water(as much as 5 feet) especially in South Jackson, the Herron Grove area of Jackson, McGee Loop area of Northeast Jackson, and Bemis. In total, 120 to 140 homes across Madison County sustained damage from the flooding. As many as 85 businesses in Jackson received damage. The flash flooding event transitioned into a flood event as rivers rose quickly from the rainfall and overflowed their banks. Some roads remained closed for days making travel difficult. Shelters were opened in Jackson due to the flooding.

Very heavy rains produced a flash flooding event in Madison County. As much as 11 to 16 inches of rain fell across Madison County. The flash flooding event transitioned to a flood event by late afternoon of May 1st. The South Fork Forked Deer River in Jackson rose quickly above flood stage. Many homes and roads were affected by the high water.

As much as 11 to 16 inches of rain fell near Spring Creek. The heavy rains caused Spring Creek to rise rapidly. This caused lake levels in the Springbrook Lake to also rise.  A levee failed as a result of the high water spilling water into Springbrook Lake Estates. Many homes and roads were flooded as a result.

Very heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding across Tipton County. Up to 20 inches of rain fell causing devastating damage to homes, businesses, roads and bridges. In fact, 40 roads were impassable in Tipton County due to the flooding. Twenty-one of those roads and 14 bridges were washed out as a result of the flooding. Other roads received damage just from the heavy rain. Damage was particularly bad in Atoka and Mason. Numerous vehicles were completely submerged in water. Two apartment complexes in Covington sustained major damage. In total, 309 homes received damage from the flooding. Of those, 96 homes were completely destroyed. As many as 93 businesses were flooded and of those 21 were completely destroyed. Nineteen mobile homes were flooded with 14 being destroyed. Many other structures or buildings were flooded as well. One fatality occurred in Mason. The flash flooding event transitioned into a flood event as rivers rose rapidly and overflowed their banks.

Very heavy rain produced devastating flash flooding across Northwestern Shelby County. Up to 16 inches of rain fell causing widespread flooding. Millington was the hardest hit area where a levee holding back water from Big Creek was topped. As many as 200-300 homes in base housing at the Naval Support Activity Base were flooded. Numerous people had to be rescued. Four to five feet of water covered the navy base. Some locations around Millington were covered by as much as 8 feet of water. All roads in Millington were closed. Power outages occurred due to the flood waters.  Raleigh, Frayser and Bartlett also received widespread flooding where water was as deep as vehicles windshields. One fatality occurred in Raleigh as a vehicle became stranded in flood waters.  Water covered some streets in Downtown Memphis with water as high as vehicles wheel wells. In total, 576 homes received some kind of flood damage. Of those, 77 were completely destroyed. Eight businesses were damaged and 403 mobile homes were completely destroyed. Several other buildings including apartment complexes were damaged as well. The flash flooding event transitioned into a flood event where rivers rose rapidly spilling over their banks.

Flash flooding transitioned into a flood event across Northern Shelby County as a result of up to 16 inches of rain. The Loosahatchie River rose rapidly spilling over its banks flooding numerous homes and businesses from Millington to Arlington. Many roads were underwater as well. The river crested at a record level in Arlington on May 2nd.

Very heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding in Gibson County. Rainfall amounts were estimated between 10 to 15 inches. As many as 16 roads were flooded or washed out. Highway 79 between Milan and the Carroll County line was covered by as much as 8 feet of water. In total, 137 homes sustained some kind of flood damage in Gibson County. Of those homes, six were completely destroyed. Eighty-seven businesses received damage with two businesses being completely destroyed. A few apartment complexes, mobile homes and other public buildings sustained damage as well. One fatality occurred as the waters quickly rose and swept one person off their feet. The flash flood event transitioned into a flood event as the heavy rain caused the North Fork Forked Deer and the Middle Fork Forked Deer River to overflow their banks.

Heavy rainfall in excess of 10-15 inches produced flash flooding which later transitioned to a flood event across Gibson County. The North Fork Forked Deer quickly rose to record levels. Water spilled out of its banks and flooded areas near Trenton and Milan. Numerous homes and businesses were flooded as a result.

Very heavy rain as much as 20 inches fell across Haywood County producing widespread flash flooding. As many as 21 roads were flooded or washed out from the heavy rain. In total, 168 homes sustained some kind of flooding damage. Three businesses received damage as well. Vehicles were stranded in flood waters. At least one flood rescue occurred. The flash flooding event transitioned to a flood event as the heavy rain allowed rivers to rise rapidly overflowing their banks.

Very heavy rain up to 20 inches produced devastating flooding across Crockett County. As many as 25 roads and bridges were flooded or washed out. At the peak of the flooding, most of the county roads were closed. Some rescues occurred from the flood waters. In total, 49 houses sustained some kind of flood damage. Of those, thirteen were completely destroyed. Three businesses were damaged as well. A few apartment complexes, farm buildings and other structures were affected by the flood waters. The flash flood event transitioned into a flood event by late in the afternoon as heavy rain allowed rivers to rapidly rise and overflow their banks.

Very heavy rain up to 20 inches produced widespread flooding in Henderson County. Numerous roads and bridges were flooded or washed out. At least 35 culverts were washed out from the heavy rain. As many as 43 homes sustained damage from the flood waters. Numerous rescues from homes and vehicles stranded in flood waters had to be made. The flash flood event transitioned to a flood event by late in the afternoon as heavy rain allowed rivers to overflow their banks.

Very heavy rain up to 20 inches fell across Carroll County producing widespread flash flooding. Small streams and creeks overflowed their banks. At least 25 roads were flooded or washed out as a result. In total, eleven homes sustained damage from the flooding. Three of those were totally destroyed. Thirty-six businesses also sustained damage with nine being totally destroyed. Several other buildings including apartment complexes, farm buildings, and mobile homes also received damage. One fatality occurred when a vehicle was washed off the roadway as the driver tried to drive through flood waters. Water swept more than 20 used cars off of a car lot in downtown Huntingdon. Railroad tracks across the county sustained damage as well. The flash flooding event transitioned into a flood event as the heavy rain allowed rivers to rise rapidly and overflow their banks.
Straight line winds produced roof and structural damage to about seven homes near the Fair Oaks Golf Course just north of Oakland. Large trees were uprooted as well.

Very heavy rain fell across McNairy County producing widespread flash flooding. The city park in Selmer was flooded. Numerous roads and bridges were flooded or washed out. The flash flooding transitioned to flooding as the heavy rain caused rivers to rapidly rise and overflow their banks.

Very heavy rain, up to 10 inches, fell across Fayette County. Small streams and creeks quickly overflowed causing numerous roads to be flooded or washed out. In total, about 20 homes and three businesses received flood damage across the county. The hardest hit area was the North Woods Subdivision in Oakland. However, the cities of Rossville, Hickory Withe, and Somerville also had homes or businesses flooded. Several vehicles were stranded in flood waters as well.

A tornado touched down near Highway 15 southeast of Cotton Plant and traveled northeast into Tippah County. An outbuilding suffered minor damage near the touchdown point and minor tree damaged occurred along the path.

A tornado moved northeast into Tippah County from Union County. The tornado remained on the ground for roughly 8 miles in Tippah County lifting near County Road 602 northeast of Dumas. Six homes sustained minor to moderate damage. The hardest hit area was located on County Road 701. In addition, a roof was peeled off of a mobile home. A barn was also damaged. A few vehicles were damaged as well. Many trees were knocked down along the path. A church suffered minor damage just before the tornado lifted.

A tornado moved northeast into Cross County from Woodruff County, Arkansas near Primrose, east of Highway 49. The tornado first tracked across open farm land. The tornado then damaged three homes and several outbuildings on US Highway 64. One home sustained major damage and a two-story barn was completely collapsed. The other two homes had minor damage. Several very large trees were also knocked down. Five power poles were also snapped along US Highway 64. The tornado then continued northeast across open farm land before snapping power lines along County Road 165 before lifting.

A tornado touched down southwest of Weona near Hogg Road. The tornado moved a tractor disc and then moved northeast across open farm land damaging several transmission lines near Highway 373. Four power poles were also snapped. The tornado continued northeast destroying an office trailer at a crop duster hangar off Highway 14 in Weona. The crop duster hangar was also damaged. The tornado then tracked across open farm land damaging trees and power poles. The tornado crossed Henderson Lane and damaged one home. A barn was also destroyed. The tornado then tracked across more open farm land snapping three more transmission lines as it crossed Maple Grove Lane. The tornado damaged more trees between farm fields before lifting near County Road 204.

An eyewitness took photos of a tornado briefly touching down in the St. Francis Sunken Lands State Wildlife Refuge Area. The extent of the tree damage from the tornado is unknown due to the track across a marsh land.

A tornado briefly touched down on Micro Road in Millington, just west of Highway 51. The tornado tracked northeast to Highway 51 before lifting. A couple of wooden poles and several trees were blown down and twisted.
Dime to golf ball size hail fell near Como.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Paris. Fairgrounds Road just east of Paris was flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Milan. The intersection of North 1st Street and Highway 79 was flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Brooksy Thompson Road to the southwest of Decaturville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Decatur County. Several low water crossing were flooded across the county.
Hail to quarter size hail fell in Decaturville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Scotts Hill. Hughes Road was flooded just east of town.
Nickel size hail fell at the intersection of Tchulahoma Road and Winchester Avenue.
Dime to nickel size hail fell near the intersection of Interstate 240 and Getwell Road.
Golf ball size hail fell at the University of Memphis campus.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Memphis. The left lane of Interstate 40 was flooded near the Interstate 55 interchange.
Quarter size hail fell at the Best Western Hotel in Robinsonville.
Quarter size hail fell at Interstate 40 and Highway 385.
Golf ball size hail fell at Highway 70 and Airline Road.
Penny size hail fell at the National Weather Service Office.
Quarter size hail fell at the National Weather Service Office.
Half dollar size hail covered the ground in Arlington.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Highway 222 between Interstate 40 and Somerville and on Akin Road in Northern Fayette County.
Ping Pong to Golf ball size hail fell along Highway 222 near Interstate 40 and along Akin Road in Northern Fayette County.
Quarter size hail fell at the Weakley County Sheriff's office.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell near Trezevant.
Quarter size hail fell near the St. John Baptist Church northeast of Trezevant.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a car near Lynn and also knocked down some power lines.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Eastern Shelby County. Several roads were flooded including Houston Levee Road at Plum Creek Road near Lakeland. The intersection of Dexter Road and Lenow Road was flooded in Cordova. The intersection of Kirby Whitten and Century Center Parkway in Memphis was flooded along with Sycamore View Road and Interstate 40.
Straight line winds knocked down power poles along Highway 20 just west of Elaine.
Straight line winds destroyed a tool shed on County Road 721 to the southeast of Kennett.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Coahoma.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in the south part of Crenshaw.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 315 east of Water Valley.
Very heavy rain produced flash flooding in Oxford. Many roads were covered with 3 to 4 feet of water throughout Oxford. Flooding damaged 21 homes, 7 apartments, 10 businesses and 25 cars.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Dyer. Highway 77 and the Old Dyer-Trenton Road were flooded. The road in front of 184 West College Street collapsed and washed away.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Samburg. Highway 21/22 was flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees, power poles and fences in Ridgely. Five utility poles were snapped along State Route 78.  A pickup truck was crushed by a toppled tree.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Fisher.
Straight line winds blew away a metal car port and knocked down large tree limbs at Locust Grove Road and Highway 211 to the northeast of Newbern.
A thunderstorm wind gust was estimated at 60 mph near just southeast of Yorkville.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous large trees in Dyer.
Straight line winds knocked down light poles across the city of Marked Tree.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous large trees and power lines across Trenton. The Lake Hayes area was also hit hard with several homes damaged and a car crushed by a tree. Extensive tree and power line damage was also reported in the Concord, Cades and Union Central areas. Several homes were hit by trees along Concord-Cades Road.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Milan. Several homes suffered shingle damage and a railroad crossing gate was snapped off.  Four trees fell on a house on Mayo Cook Road north of Milan. Hundreds of giant trees were knocked down along Gann Road, Salem Road and Park Avenue. A couple of cars were also crushed by toppled trees.
Golf ball size hail fell in Milan and across a large part of the surrounding area.
Straight line winds knocked trees on to homes and cars on Cades-Atwood Road between the towns of Cades and Atwood.
Straight line winds knocked down trees south of McLemoresville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Lawrence County. Various back roads were flooded across the county.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding east of Malden. A 2 mile stretch of Highway H was flooded just south of the Stoddard County line.
A 64 mph wind gust was recorded at the Tupelo Airport. The hospital helicopter hangar was damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines blocking Highway 348 and the Birmingham Ridge Road. A trampoline was also blown across the road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Pontotoc County. Sword Lane off of County Road 215 was washed out.
Heavy rain producing flash flooding in Pontotoc. Several roads were flooded and the retaining wall along 8th street was damaged.

Very heavy rain produced flash flooding the the Tupelo area. In Verona two rescue events were reported involving stranded cars.  Twelve to eighteen inches of water covered roads in the Palmetto area. Several houses were flooded in Tupleo.
Heavy rain producing flash flooding near Bruce. Highway 32 east was flooded with 8 to 10 inches of water over the roadway.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Monroe County. The Amory area was especially hard hit with several roads and homes flooded. The communities of Hatley and Smithville also had roads flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Clarksburg. Highway 220 was flooded just west of town.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the Holly Springs National Forest. A temporary bridge was washed away about 6 miles south of Hickory Flat.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in downtown Martin. A building partially collapsed as well.
A trained spotter reported a 59 mph gust just east of Union City. Several trees were knocked down by straight line winds in the Union City area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Martin. Several streets were flooded.
Public reported golf ball size hail at Germantown Parkway and Trinity Road in Cordova.
Public reported quarter size hail at Germantown Parkway and Cordova Road in Cordova.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Northern Shelby County.  Fite Road at Highway 51 was flooded.
Nickel size hail fell on Goodlett Farms Parkway between Whitten Road and Appling Road.
Nicked size hail fell at the National Weather Service office at the Agricenter International complex near Walnut Grove Road and Germantown Parkway.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Shelby County.  The intersection of Raleigh Lagrange and Dexter Road was flooded. The parking lots and breezeways were flooded at the Greenbrook Apartments on Macon Road. Street flooding also occurred on Appling Road near the Bellevue Baptist Church.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding just south of Millington. Greenlawn Cove was flooded and garbage cans were floating in the street.
Penny size hail fell near the Carriage Crossing shopping center just west of Collierville.
Large amounts of quarter size hail fell on Interstate 40 near Steele.
Straight line winds blew a 18 wheel truck off Interstate 155 just west of Dyersburg. Large highway signs were also blown over between mile markers 2 and 3.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines and damaged a mobile home just west of Wynne.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding just south of Bartlett. The intersection of Whitten Road and Hillshire Circle was flooded and completely closed.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Northern Marshall County. Flooding occurred near the Mike's Stop gas station on U.S. Highway 72 near the Tennessee and Mississippi border.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on the north side of Tunica. The winds also stripped away part of the North Tunica Fire Department's facade.
Golf ball size hail fell in Tunica.

A 60 mph wind gust was measured at the Savannah AWOS. Trees and power lines were knocked down across Hardin County including Savannah, Pickwick, Walkertown, Childers Hill and Olivehill. Minor shingle damage was also reported throughout the county. A tree fell on a house on Country Club Road.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines just south of Jonestown.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Henderson.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Chester County. Numerous roads were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Clarksdale. Several roads were flooded on the  west side of town.
Straight line winds estimated at 60 mph knocked down power lines on Highway 147 and destroyed an outbuilding to the southwest of West Memphis. Several trees were also uprooted.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees, power poles and power lines in Lexington.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Thrashers.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in the vicinity of Grand Junction.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Corinth and along County Roads 630 and 505 between Corinth and Kossuth.
Dime to quarter size hail fell in Dumas and lasted several minutes.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of large trees at campgrounds on Sardis Lake. A few awnings were blown off campers at the Oak Grove Campground.

A weak tornado touched down just north of Interstate 69 near Tulane Road and traveled northeast for about 1 mile before lifting near the Nesbit Road. Several very large trees were knocked down and a couple of them were snapped off. Some shingle damage was noted as well.

A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of Eureka and Hubbard Roads about 4 miles east-northeast of Pope in Panola County. The tornado snapped trees and bolted down playground equipment was thrown. A dumpster was turned over and power lines were also downed.
A weak tornado touched down briefly near Gadsden snapping off many pine trees 10 to 20 feet above the ground.

A tornado touched down on the south side of Humboldt and several houses received roof, siding and garage door damage. One home in Humboldt received partial roof loss and garage damage while the storage shed and wooden swing set were completely destroyed. Several power poles were knocked down before a winery received tree and vine damage. Some tiles were stripped off the business home at the winery. One rural home suffered more extensive damage near the end of the track with partial roof loss, porch removal and brick veneer ripped off the northeast corner of the home. Windows were also blown out on the home with a large well built brick supported carport completely destroyed. A well built 40 foot by 40 foot wood and metal shed on the property was completely destroyed with the wood support beams snapped off one foot above the concrete slab. A tour bus nearby was lifted and turned 180 degrees. A semi trailer on the property was also flipped over. Numerous large trees along the path were either uprooted or damaged. A few smaller trees were snapped off one to two feet above the ground. Several power lines were also knocked down before the tornado lifted near Pleasant Hill Road.

A tornado touched down near Highway 5 approximately 2 miles south of Ashland. The tornado traveled northeast crossing into Tippah County. Eleven homes and mobile homes were destroyed with six receiving major damage. Twenty-three homes sustained minor damage. Numerous trees were snapped and debarked along the path. Power lines were also knocked down. A free standing transmission tower collapsed and was severely twisted as well. Two deaths and one critical injury occurred when a double wide mobile home was destroyed just east of Ashland. Four additional injuries, three of them critical, occurred when a mobile home was picked up by the tornado.

A tornado tracked northeast into Tippah County from Benton County. The tornado continued northeast crossing into Hardeman County, Tennessee. Numerous homes were damaged along County Road 301 near the intersection of County Road 303, along Highway 72 east of Walnut and near Brownfield. In total 5 homes were destroyed. Trees and power lines were knocked down in the area as well.

A tornado crossed into Hardeman County from Tippah County, Mississippi. The tornado tracked northeast hitting Pocahontas before moving into McNairy County. One fatality occurred in Pocahontas when a single wide trailer was destroyed. Two injuries also occurred. In total, one home was completely destroyed. Thirteen homes sustained major damage with another five receiving very minor damage. Two mobile homes were destroyed with another two receiving minor damage. Numerous trees were snapped and debarked in the area. In addition, power lines were knocked down as well.

A tornado crossed into McNairy County from Hardeman County. The tornado briefly traveled northeast before lifting near Highway 57. Several trees and power lines were knocked down in the area. This storm would later spawn a couple of tornadoes further northeast in McNairy County.

A tornado briefly touched down near Dan Head Road, west of Ramer. Several trees were knocked down in the area. Minor roof damage occurred to a mobile home. This tornado was spawned by the same cell that produced damage from near Ashland Mississippi to near Pocahontas, Tennessee. This same cell would go onto produce damage near Selmer.

A tornado touched down near the intersection of Sulphur Springs Road and Steadman Road, southwest of Selmer, and tracked northeast. This tornado was spawned from the same cell that produced a tornado from near Ashland, Mississippi to near Pocahontas, Tennessee and just west of Ramer, Tennessee in McNairy County. Tree and minor roof damage was noted at the beginning of the track.  The tornado tracked further to the northeast and hit northern parts of Selmer. A carport failed due to fallen trees at the Christmas Tree Farm. A large home was moved off the foundation as well as a double wide mobile home. A single wide trailer was destroyed and wrapped around a tree. Total collapse of a few buildings occurred as well. Large trees were knocked down and minor roof damage was noted. The tornado then tracked further to the northeast and hit Bethesda and Purdy. Two churches were destroyed. A brick home sustained major roof damage while a horse barn was completely destroyed. The tornado tracked further to the northeast and hit the town of Good Hope. Two homes were destroyed. The tornado continued to the northeast crossing into Hardin County just to the southwest Milledgeville. At least ten injuries occurred in McNairy County from the tornado. In total, 22 homes were completely destroyed with 59 homes sustaining major damage. At least minor damage occurred to 219 homes. Fifteen mobile homes were destroyed and eleven sustained major damage. Twenty mobile homes received minor damage. Several other buildings and outbuildings were damaged or destroyed as well.

A tornado tracked northeast into Hardin County from McNairy County and hit the town of Milledgeville. One house sustained major damage while another sustained roof damage. Minor damage occurred to a shed. Several trees were knocked down in the area. Two injuries occurred from the tornado. This storm went on to produce a tornado in Henderson and Decatur Counties.

A tornado touched down along Old Reagan Road, southwest of Scotts Hill and tracked northeast. This storm cell had previously produced tornadoes in McNairy and Hardin Counties. A building and outbuilding sustained roof damage at the beginning of the track. The tornado continued northeast and hit Scotts Hill before crossing into Decatur County. Several trees were knocked down along the path. In total, five homes were damaged from the tornado.
A tornado tracked northeast into Decatur County from Henderson County. Several trees were knocked down along the path.

A tornado touched down just southwest of Abbeville and tracked northeast hitting the south side of Abbeville. The tornado lifted along County Road 215. One fatality occurred when a single family home was destroyed. A double wide mobile home was also destroyed. Three other homes sustained major damage. Numerous trees were also uprooted along the path.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across mainly Northwest Chickasaw County where many roads were flooded. A few motorists became stranded in the flood waters. Streets in Woodland and Houston were flooded as well.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Ripley and Falkner. Numerous roads were flooded as a result. In total, nine roads and two bridges were destroyed with eight roads receiving major damage. Two roads sustained minor damage. Numerous homes were flooded sustaining major and minor damage. One building and one utility company received major damage as well from the flooding.
Heavy rain occurred in New Albany. One fatality occurred when a vehicle lost control on Highway 78 near New Albany during the heavy rain and hit a guardrail.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding across Alcorn County. Numerous roads were flooded or washed out as a result. One fatality occurred when the vehicle lost control and went into a ditch off of Shiloh Road near Shiloh Ridge Golf Course. The vehicle became fully submerged and the driver drowned as a result. Numerous additional water rescues were made as a result of the flooding. Portions of Highway 72 in Downtown Corinth were flooded. Flood waters went into at least 40 businesses including K-Mart and Kroger. At least 8 homes were destroyed from flood waters. In addition, seventy homes sustained major damage with two receiving minor damage. An apartment complex containing 40 units also sustained major flood damage.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Lee County. Several roads and bridges were flooded or washed out. Of these, six roads and one bridge sustained damage. One home sustained minor flood damage. One fatality occurred when a vehicle hydroplaned on Highway 45 between Eason Boulevard and Main Street exits in Tupelo as a result of the heavy rain and hit another vehicle.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Lakeland. One tree fell down on Monroe Road blocking the road.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Horn Lake and Nesbit. Vehicles were stranded in flood water up to headlights at the intersection of Highway 302 and Highway 51. Motorists had to be rescued. The roads were closed as a result. In addition, a teenager had to be rescued from a flooded ditch off of Tulane Road near Nesbit. At the peak of the storm, one home in off of Dean Road had nearly three feet of water inside.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding around Tunica. The intersection of White Oaks Road and Josephine Road was flooded near the Tunica Airport. Several streets in town was flooded as well.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Corinth. Numerous streets were flooded as a result.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Panola County. A home was flooded off of Seven Road as a result. Flood waters entered into Smith Cleaners in Downtown Batesville as well. In addition, four additional homes were flooded and as many as twenty-four roads were closed or received damage due to the flooding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Union County. Twenty-eight roads and one bridge sustained major damage. Fifteen businesses and one public building received damage from flooding as well. In addition, fourteen homes and six mobile homes sustained minor damage.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Tishomingo County. Nine roads were destroyed and six roads sustained major damage. Sixteen roads received minor damage. One church and two other buildings on the church's property sustained damage. Nine homes and one mobile home sustained major damage. Five culverts were destroyed.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Marshall County. Ten roads sustained major damage. Seventeen roads received minor damage. Twenty-one homes and mobile homes sustained minor damage.

Heavy rain of 10 to 20 inches produced record breaking flooding along the North Fork Forked Deer River in Dyer County. South Dyersburg was hit extremely hard with numerous homes and businesses sustaining major damage. At one point portions of South Dyersburg was underneath as much as 4 feet of water. In total, at least 600 structures received damage from the flooding.

Very heavy rain up to 20 inches produced devastating flooding across Lauderdale County. Twenty homes sustained at least minor damage. Twenty mobile homes and few businesses sustained damage as well. Five roads sustained major damage and fifteen roads received minor damage. The flash flood event transitioned into a flood event by late in the afternoon as heavy rain allowed rivers to rapidly rise and overflow their banks.

Very heavy rains produced a flash flooding event in Lauderdale County. As much as 20 inches of rain fell across Lauderdale County. The flash flooding event transitioned to a flood event by late afternoon of May 1st. The South Fork Forked Deer River in Halls rose quickly above flood stage. Many homes and roads were affected by the high water.

A microburst produced damaging winds in Southeast Memphis. A semi-trailer was blown over as well as several trees and light poles. Roof damage occurred to a warehouse as air conditioners were ripped off of the roof.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and power lines in Lexington.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Sledge. One tree fell on top of a fence causing damage.

Straight line winds knocked down two 20 ft. tall aluminum flag poles and several trees between Watson and Warsaw. Shingles were also blown off of a couple of homes. Lawn furniture was tossed around as well.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Holmes Road and Autumn Forrest Drive. Water was as high as the fenders of school buses.
A student was struck by lightning and injured near Southwind High School in Southeast Memphis.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding in Midtown Memphis. Numerous streets were closed as a result including major intersections such as Cooper Street and Central Avenue, Walnut Grove Road and Highland Street, and Sam Cooper Boulevard and Collins Street.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Whitehaven. MillBranch Road was flooded just north of Shelby Drive.
Straight line winds knocked numerous large trees down across Gibson County. Several homes sustained roof damage along South College Street in Trenton as well.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and tree limbs as well as a pizza restaurant sign in Bruceton.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Doskie.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding across Tippah County. County Road 200 and County Road 240 near Falkner were flooded as a result. In addition, County Road 237 was flooded along with several streets in Walnut. Several culverts were washed out in Tiplersville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 72 near the Union Center Fire Department.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Decaturville. Concord Road was closed as a result.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding in Hardin County. Several roads in Savannah were closed as a result including Highway 64 which was covered by at least six inches of water. At least 5 homes along Hwy 64 in Olive Hill sustained flood damage. Numerous roads and bridges sustained damage from the flooding. One man was rescued from his vehicle after being trapped from flood waters on Lonesome Pine Road. One other motorist had to be rescued as well. Roads were also closed northeast of Savannah where water was as high as two feet on some roads.

Straight line winds knocked several trees and power lines down along Highway 51 in Ripley. A mobile home sustained roof damage and had the underpinning blown out in Henning. A tree and swing set was also blown over as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines at the intersection of Armour Road and Millington-Arlington Road in Millington.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down along Highway 315 in Pleasant Grove.
Straight line winds uprooted several trees near Enid Lake in Panola County.
A man was struck by lightning while standing out on a balcony in Joiner. The lightning first struck a nearby tree and then jumped to the balcony striking and injuring the man.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees and a pavilion in Savannah.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees across portions of Crockett County.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees across portions of Haywood County. Minor roof damage occurred as well. One shed was destroyed near Brownsville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Alamo that eventually led to a bridge being partially washed out.
Lightning struck a house on Carmack Road, north of Ripley. A fire started as a result causing a complete loss of the home.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and caused roof damage to a few homes near the Corinth Airport. One home had the roof and porch ripped off while another home had a carport damaged.

Straight line winds knocked down several large trees east of Savannah. Damage occurred to some outbuildings as well.
Ping-pong size hail fell on Highway 315 near the Panola, Lafayette, and Yalobusha County lines.

Straight line winds knocked down trees near Darracot Road, south of Aberdeen.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Lawrence County. County Road 210 near Black Rock was closed due to flooding. Several roads were flooded in Walnut Ridge including the south end of Pocahontas Road, Free Street, North Carolina Street, Alabama Street and Tennessee Street.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Dunklin County. Roads flooded included Highway Y between Kennett and Caruth, Highway 164 in Hornersville and Highway P in Senath.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Maynard. Several low water crossings were flooded.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Sedgwick. Several county roads were flooded near Highway 228 and Highway 63. Sections of pavement were swept away on Eighth Street in Black Rock. Highway 412 near Walnut Ridge was closed due to flooding. All low water crossings across Lawrence County were flooded. Bridge and culverts throughout the county have been damaged.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Northwest Greene County. County Road 138 was closed due to flooding along with all the low water crossings across Northwest Greene County.  The Evening Star community on County Roads 223 and 229 was completely flooded. The Stanford community had some flooding on County Road 203 while County Road 215 was flooded near Beech Groove.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Wheatley.
Straight line winds propelled tree branches through the roof of a home in Forrest City and another home in Madison. Power poles were knocked down in Forrest City as well.
Straight line winds propelled tree branches through the roof of a home in Caldwell.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Corning.  Flooding closed 3rd Street, Laurel Street and Crafton Street. Some sandbagging was necessary to keep water out of homes.

Damaging straight line winds moved through Eastern Poinsett County. McCormick was the first town to receive damage at around 605 PM CST. Fifteen to twenty power poles were knocked down along Highway 214 just east of McCormick. Isolated tree damage was found at various spots along the path of this storms through Eastern Poinsett County. A roof was taken off of a building in Marked Tree. Power lines and a tree were knocked on to a house near Lepanto. An 18 wheeler was blown on to its side on Highway 63 near Tulot. Damaging winds then moved into Western Mississippi County.

Damaging straight line winds moved from Eastern Poinsett County into portions of Western Mississippi County. The worst damage was found near West Ridge. Power poles were knocked down, a few trees were snapped and a cinder block garage was destroyed with the metal roofing blown over 200 yards from the building. In addition, a storage building received damage to the siding and a barn lost some shingles. Well pivots were turned over about 5 miles north of West Ridge. Power lines were knocked down in Etowah.
Straight line winds knocked over a tractor trailer on Interstate 55 at mile marker 24 near Turrell.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Glass Road and South Bluff Road. Trees were also knocked down in the town of Glass.

Damaging straight line winds moved through Eastern Crittenden County. The path of damage began near the town of Crawfordsville. Several trees were down or suffered limb damage. Shingles or metal roofing was ripped off several structures. Several pickup trucks and large tractors for farming had broken windows. Winds in this area were estimated at around 80 to 85 mph. Wind damage was also found at the Delta Acres subdivision about 5 miles north of Marion along Highway 77. Several trees and fences were broken or down in this area. Siding and shingles were off almost all in the houses in this subdivision. Winds at this location were estimated at 70 to 80 mph. A roof was torn off a gas station in Marion. The storm continued to move east and crossed the Mississippi River.

Damaging straight line winds moved from Crittenden County across the Mississippi River into Shelby County. The damage path continued near Meeman-Shelby Forest State Park where power lines were knocked down. Power poles and several trees were knocked down in the Cornell Street and Frayser Boulevard area in Frayser. Trees and a metal shed were also damaged. A small plane was flipped over at the Charles W Baker Airport and a nearby Fire Department sustained some roof damage. Wind speeds in this area were estimated at 70 mph. The storm entered Millington at around 6:55 pm CST resulting in tree and shingle damaged across the city. Trees and power lines were snapped along Navy Road and Singleton Road on the naval base. A tree was knocked on to a mobile home in the Shady Oaks subdivision. Wind speeds in Millington were estimated at 85 to 95 mph. A tree was knocked on to a car near the intersection of Mudville Road and Rosemark Road east of Millington. Shingle and fence damage was also noted across Bartlett where wind speeds were estimated at 60 to 70 mph. Power lines were also knocked down and a street light was bent at Highway 64 and Highway 70.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 61 and on Highway 140 near Osceola. A 62 mph gust was measured on a hand held anemometer.
Straight line winds knocked over a chimney at a house in Hickory Hill. The stoplight was damaged at Poplar Avenue and Germantown Road in Germantown.

Damaging straight line winds moved through East Central and Northeast Lauderdale County. This is the same storm that produced damaged across Poinsett and Mississippi Counties in Arkansas. Trees were knocked down in the town of Ripley. The town of Gates received damage as the storm continued northeast. Damage to trees and fences was found in Gates. Power poles were snapped and power lines were knocked down along Highway 209 between Halls and Gates. A shop was destroyed and a home was damaged along Lawrence Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Kennett. St. Francis Street at South Jackson Street was closed due to 2 feet of water on the road.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and power lines north of Somerville. A shed was destroyed on Newcastle Drive near Armour Drive.
Straight line wind knocked down trees and power lines across Crockett County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Northern Pemiscot county. Water surrounded homes in the community of Homestown.
Three power poles were bent at a 45 degree angle near Highway 70 and Airline Road in Arlington.
Portion of a metal roof of a barn was peeled up near Cloverdale.
Power poles were knocked down along Highway 70 and Highway 50 in Crawfordsville. In addition, a few trees and power lines were knocked down in Marion.
A roof of a church and a business were blown off in Osceola.

Straight line winds knocked down trees across Gibson County. Trees fell into a couple of homes in Trenton. A construction trailer at Peabody High School was overturned. Large tree branches were downed south of Bradford.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and power lines north of Somerville. A shed was destroyed on NewCastle Drive near Armour Drive.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Cordova. Chimney Rock Boulevard was flooded near the St. Francis Church.

Straight line winds knocked a large oak tree on to a carport and a portion of a house on Westmoreland Place. The carport and the car inside were destroyed. The house suffered slight roof and siding damage. A wooden fence was also damaged. A business had a sign destroyed.
A wind gust of 64 mph was recorded at McKellar-Sipes Regional Airport east of Jackson.
Penny size hail was reported in Trenton.
Straight line winds knocked trees down near Chickasaw State Park. Trees were also knocked down on Sand Road and Wilson Road.
Penny size hail fell in Jacks Creek.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in the Henderson area. Power lines were also knocked down on the Tate Loop Road southwest of Henderson.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Henderson. Water covered the intersection of Main Street and Church Street to the depth of 8 inches.

Rain amounts of 4 to 5 1/2 inches produced flash flooding in Obion County. Streets were flooded in Union City and portions of Highway 21 between Hornbeak and the junction of Highway 21 and Highway 22 were closed.

Straight line winds knocked down trees on Corinth Road northwest of Darden. A carport was caved in damaging a pickup truck and a shed was destroyed. A tree landed on a house and a rood was blown off a barn.

Damaging straight line winds moved through extreme Northeast Henry County. Tree damage was found along East Antioch Road and in the Russwood Shores area near Kentucky Lake. One tree fell on to a home causing substantial damage. Other homes received minor damage from debris and straight line wind. Estimated wind speeds were between 70 and 75 mph.

A tornado moved from Carroll County into Decatur County and continued northeast. Major damage was sustained to a mobile home in the Five Forks area. A large grain bin was tossed 50 yards and destroyed and there was minor damage to homes and trees in the Bible Hill area. Several tombstones were also overturned and damaged in Bible Hill. The most significant damage occurred on Blue Bird Circle at the Lick Creek Inlet. Eight homes sustained enough damage to render them uninhabitable along with damage to private boat docks and pontoon boats. A roof to a floating boat dock was lifted off of its foundation and tossed approximately one half mile across the inlet and destroyed. Damage to homes and businesses were estimated at 1.285 million dollars.
Straight line winds knocked down several large trees in New Harmony and Blue Springs. A few trees landed on vehicles.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Pontotoc County.  A roof was peeled back on a business near Pontotoc.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 341 and County Road 102.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Saltillo.
A 59 mph gust was report at the Tupelo Airport.
Straight line winds knocked trees down in New Wren and Smithville. Three mobile homes had some damage.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down in Belmont.
Straight line winds knocked down limbs and mailboxes near Beaver Lake. A car was blown off the road near Beaver Lake.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines on US Highway 72 near the Mississippi and Alabama state lines.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines at South Highland and Perry Switch Road and at South Highland and Highway 18.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Henry County. Several roads around the county were flooded and suffered some damage.

Penny size hail was reported at the intersection of Dexter Road and Chimney Rock Boulevard.
Heavy rain flooded a low water crossing on Highway 59 near the town of Braden with more than six inches of water.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Ballentine Road and River Road between Sardis and Batesville.
Straight line winds blew numerous trees down across St. Francis County. A few sheds were damaged as well.
Winds were measured at 62 mph at the Blytheville Airport ASOS. The straight line winds damaged a camper and knocked down large tree limbs in East Blytheville.
Dime to nickel size hail covered the ground in Dyersburg.
Quarter size hail fell on Antioch Road and Caleb Lake Road near Independence.
Quarter size hail fell in Wall Doxey State Park.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell on Highway 15 just north of New Albany.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell in Tula.
Dime to nickel size hail fell northeast of Saltillo.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell along the Lee County and Prentiss County line.
Penny size hail fell at the intersection of County Road 202 and County Road 229.
Penny size hail covered the ground in Trezevant.
Quarter size hail covered the ground in Nettleton.
Quarter size hail covered the ground lightly in Evergreen.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell south of Water Valley.
Nickel to quarter size hail near New Salem.
An elderly man drove his truck into flood waters when he lost control of the vehicle in the current causing the cab to fill with water. The passenger of the vehicle died as a result.

Straight line winds knocked down trees all across Greene County. The most concentrated area stretched from near Stanford to Center Hill. Two shop buildings were blown over on County Road 217. A barn was damaged on County Road 615 and a tree fell onto a house on County Road 626.
Penny to golf ball size hail fell in Kennett to 4 miles south of Kennett.
Straight line winds knocked down power poles on Independence Street in Kennett.
Damaging straight line winds caused minor roof damage to two businesses and one house within the town of Rivervale. One telephone pole was also knocked down.
Damaging straight line winds took a roof off of a barn on Bluebird Hill Road to the northeast of the city of Ripley.
Damaging straight line winds tore the roof off of a barn and scattered the pieces across a field. Some large tree limbs were also knocked down in the area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Dyersburg. Several streets and county roads were covered by water and two vehicles were flooded.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down a few trees in the square of the town of Pontotoc. One tree fell on a car.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down a few trees in the town of Friendship.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in the town of Gadsden.
Straight line winds overturned two tractor trailers on Interstate 55 near mile marker 26 and mile marker 27, east of Wardell.
Straight line winds knocked down three large trees and power poles along Highway 21 in Tiptonville. A tractor barn was partially destroyed and a trailer was overturned on Highway 22 as well.
Quarter size hail fell in Fort Pillow State Park.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding along Highway H, north of Campbell. Six to eight inches of water covered the road as a result.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines across county roads near Marvell. Approximately, one hundred people were without power in Marvell immediately after the storm. One mobile home sustained minor damage on County Road 113, outside of Marvell.

Straight line winds knocked down trees on Cherry Street and power poles on North Forrest Street in Helena-West Helena. A building was partially blown on to North Forrest Street. Power poles were also knocked down on Highway 242 in the city. Numerous trees were knocked down on county roads outside of Helena-West Helena. A house received minor damage near the intersection of County Road 300 and Highway 85 near Barton.

Straight line winds damaged two businesses along Main Street in Marianna. In addition, a structure at the Witten Elementary School sustained major damage. Multiple trees and power lines blocked Highway 1 South as well as numerous city streets. As a result of the storm, 5000 people were without power and one injury occurred. Multiple trees were also knocked down along county roads outside Marianna including County Road 415.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees on multiple county roads near Horseshoe Lake. A steeple was blown off a church as well.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs in Roger Springs.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and tree limbs in Atoka.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Highway 87 in Henning. In addition, telephone poles were knocked down on Highway 209.

Straight line winds blew a roof off of a farm building and knocked several trailers off of their foundations in Robinsonville. Several power lines were knocked down and trees uprooted as well. Eight irrigation pivots sustained damage as well.

Straight line winds blew up to 40 power poles down along Highway 61 across Tunica County. Numerous trees were also blown down and minor roof damage occurred on several homes. The back wall of the North Tunica Fire Department was blown in resulting in one damaged vehicle.

Straight line winds produced major roof damage to three buildings near Horn Lake. One roof was torn off of a house. Minor shingle damage occurred to several other homes. A fence was blown over, west of Olive Branch. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in the area.
Penny size hail fell 5 miles west of Ripley on Highway 4.
Straight line winds destroyed one mobile home while another mobile home sustained minor damage in Quitman County.
Straight line winds destroyed a tractor shed and knocked down several trees in Byhalia.
Straight line winds produced minor damage to two homes in Senatobia. Several trees were knocked down from Senatobia to near Independence.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Germantown. Homes and automobiles were damaged as a result of the fallen trees.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage across much of the middle corridor of Shelby County, mainly from Memphis International Airport to East Memphis to Cordova. Damage occurred to the one of the Fed Ex hangars at Memphis International Airport. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down causing minor damage to homes and automobiles. Windows were blown out of the Clark Tower and St. Francis Hospital in East Memphis. Several traffic lights were inoperable due to wind damage and an awning was blown off a hotel. One death occurred when a person encountered a fallen power line.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Joe Vaughn Road, west of Maury City.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down in Alamo.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage between Oakland and Macon. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. A sheet metal barn was severely damaged in Oakland. A church sustained roof and steeple damage and a flag pole was blown over.
Straight line winds produced widespread damage between Somerville and Williston. Numerous trees and tree limbs were knocked down. A house near Somerville received damage from a fallen tree.

Straight line winds produced some damage to homes near Ina Road and Eastside Drive near the Fayette/Hardeman County border. A roof was blown off a barn near Laconia. Multiple trees were down in the area.
Nickel size hail fell 5 miles west of Ripley.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees across Benton County.
Straight line winds produced damage from Jackson to Bemis to Pinson. Numerous trees and power poles were knocked down in the area. Minor structural damage occurred to homes from fallen trees.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in and around Huntingdon.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in the Henderson area.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell just southeast of Oxford.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple trees down east of Ripley. Power lines were knocked down on County Road 611 near the WKRZ tower.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power poles down across McNairy County. Two homes were damaged from fallen trees, 2 miles east of Highway 45 along Highway 199.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in and around Lexington. Minor shingle damage occurred to a few homes in the area. A flag pole was also bent by the winds. Winds were estimated to be around 71 mph in the Beech Lake area.

Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down all across Decatur County. Roads were blocked as a result. At least, ten homes sustained some minor structural damage. A roof was blown off of the Parsons city truck garage.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down all across Hardin County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines just west of New Albany near the intersection of County Road 86 and Highway 30.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines on County Road 1390, County Road 1490 and County Road 3490 in Prentiss County.

Straight line winds overturned a tractor trailer between Guntown and Tupelo. A small trailer attached to a pick-up truck also overturned near Baldwyn. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down between Baldwyn and Tupelo. A few homes sustained damage from fallen trees.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines from near Tishomingo to Belmont.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near Fulton. The campus of Itawamba Community College has several trees and large branches knocked down.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding outside of Campbell. Highway H was covered with water as a result.
Quarter size hail fell on the south side of Portageville.

Heavy rain from numerous rounds of severe storms brought the Black River at Pocahontas to record levels during late April which continued through the end of May. The crest surpassed the Flood of 1915. Two levees broke sending water further away from its normal banks. Much of the area around Pocahontas was flooded as a result. U.S. Highway 67 was flooded between Pocahontas and Walnut Ridge. The Current River was also extremely high in Eastern Randolph County. Numerous homes and businesses were flooded. Roads and bridges were flooded and/or damaged. Evacuations occurred in Pocahontas and East Pocahontas.

Heavy rain brought the Black River in Black Rock to just under record levels in late April that continued into mid May. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Homes and businesses sustained minor damage from the flooding. Evacuations of Black Rock and Portia, but Portia was spared from any damage.  Many roads and bridges were also flooded and/or damaged. Portions of Black Rock and Powhatan Courthouse State Parks. Several thousand acres of cropland was flooded as well.

Heavy rain brought the Black River near Corning to record levels in late April that continued into the beginning of May. The record crest surpassed the Flood of 1945. Shallow flooding extended for several miles away from the river. Several homes and businesses sustained minor damage from the flooding. Many roads and bridges were closed and/or damaged including Highway 62, Highway 67 and Highway 155. The Clay County Airport was flooded as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on County Road 628, west of Oak Grove.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in portions of Randolph County. Highway 328 and Highway 90 were closed as a result of the flooding.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Belle Trees Drive in Cordova.

Straight line winds produced damage along the Highway 64 corridor in Cross County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down from Fair Oaks to near Parkin. Two businesses sustained roof damage near Wynne.

Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down from near Vanndale to Cherry Valley. A volunteer fire truck was blown off the road due to the winds. The Farmers Co-op and the post office in Cherry Valley sustained minor damage.
Straight line winds damaged two homes on Highway 54 between Johnson Grove Road and Highway 88, southwest of Alamo. Numerous trees were knocked down in the area as well.
Straight line winds blew over road signs along Highway 135, north of Caraway.
Straight line winds blew two tractor trailers over into the median on Interstate 55, east of Keiser.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage between Tunica and Dundee. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in the area. Three homes sustained major damage and one mobile home was destroyed near the Maud Community. A few vehicles were damaged in that community as well.
Straight line winds knocked down several privacy fences in the Southaven area.
Straight line winds blew down a fence over at the corner of Raines and Kirby across from Kirby High School in Southeast Memphis.
The Blytheville ASOS reported a 58 mph wind gust.
Straight line winds knocked a tree down onto a house causing roof and structural damage.
A large tree was knocked down on Highway 196 near Piperton.
Straight line winds tore a wooden porch from a house as well as some shingles.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down on Interstate 40 between mile markers 41 and 63.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree across both lanes of Highway 309, a quarter mile north of the Coldwater River.
Straight line winds knocked down two large poplar trees and several limbs in Gadsden.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage from the Crockett County line to the Jackson area. Numerous trees and power poles were knocked down. At least two houses sustained damage from fallen tree. A steeple was blown off a church. In Jackson, a nursing home sustained damage from fallen trees. Numerous trees and power lines were also knocked down in the city of Jackson. A fence door was also broken at the hinge by the wind.
Straight line winds damaged a municipal building and ripped off the roof. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. A mobile home was destroyed. A few power poles were snapped.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Trenton blocking several roads including Old Jackson Road and Highway 104.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines between Sharon, Martin, Dresden and Mount Pelia. At least 100 power poles were snapped. Several homes received damage from fallen trees. One injury occurred as a result. In addition, A tree fell on a vehicle in transit injuring the driver. A couple of sheds were destroyed.

A tornado touched down near Pierce Road, northeast of Martin and traveled northeast across Ralston Road. Many trees sustained damage or were uprooted. The tornado moved along Simpson Road, knocking over more trees. Near the intersection of Simpson Road and Whispering Hills Road, more trees were uprooted. Further to the northeast, additional trees were uprooted and large branches were knocked down along Chestnut Glade Road. An open hay barn was partially destroyed near the intersection of Chestnut Glade Road and Morrison Road. Farther north, more trees were uprooted at the intersection of Mansfield Road and Morrison Road. Additional tree limbs were knocked down along Wall Road and Wall Loop Road. The tornado continued northeast and produced minor damage to a house along Roberts Road. More trees were knocked down as well. Continuing northeast, the tornado crossed into Kentucky along State Line Road and continued moving to the northeast.

A weak tornado touched down near Holmes Road in Henderson County and traveled northeast towards Wildersville. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. One home sustained roof damage and one storage shed was destroyed. The tornado continued northeast out of Wildersville and crossed into Carroll County.
A weak tornado traveled northeast out of Henderson County and knocked down trees along Highway 114 in the Natchez Trace State Park. The tornado lifted near Pecan Tree Road.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage across Carroll County between McLemoresville and Vale. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Several homes sustained damage from fallen trees. One home between Huntingdon and McLemoresville was destroyed.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage in Henry County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down all across the county including in the city of Paris. Power poles were knocked down as well. Two mobile homes were damaged from fallen trees in Henry. One injury occurred as a result. Several homes sustained minor damage also from fallen trees.

Straight line winds knocked several large trees and power lines down across portions of Western Union County from near Cornersville to County Road 18. An irrigation pivot was blown over southwest of Cornersville.
Quarter size hail fell at Shelby Drive and Highway 78 in Southeast Memphis.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in the Bartlett and Ellendale area.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage across much of Crittenden County including the Crawfordsville, Marion and West Memphis areas. Trees and power lines were knocked down in Crawfordsville and Marion. Two tractor trailers were overturned on Interstate 40 in Marion from the winds. Portions of the roof of a hospital in West Memphis was torn off. Several businesses and homes were also damaged in West Memphis including a car dealership that had the front of the main building destroyed.

A weak tornado touched down one mile north of Elaine on Highway 44 and traveled east-northeast. Trees and power lines were knocked down. A few road signs were also blown over. The tornado continued east-northeast and crossed into Coahoma County, Mississippi.

A weak tornado moved east-northeast from Coahoma County, Mississippi back into Phillips County. Several trees were knocked down. The tornado continued to move east-northeast and crossed back into Coahoma County, Mississippi.

A weak tornado moved east-northeast out of Phillips County, Arkansas into Coahoma County. Several trees and power lines were knocked down. The tornado continued to move east-northeast and moved back into Phillips County, Arkansas.

A weak tornado moved east-northeast out of Phillips County, Arkansas into the Friars Point area. Several homes sustained roof damage and one home was moved off of the block foundation. A commercial metal storage building had a large section of roof peeled off. The tornado continued east-northeast near Coahoma and Lula. A church a few miles south of Lula sustained roof damage. At least two homes in Coahoma sustained damage. Trees and power lines were knocked down all along the path. A few telephone poles were knocked down as well as a few road signs. The tornado continued east-northeast into Tunica County, Mississippi.

A weak tornado traveled east-northeast out of Coahoma County, Mississippi into Southern Tunica County. Several trees and power lines were knocked down. An irrigation pivot was turned over as well. The tornado lifted near 6 Mile Lake Road.

A violent thunderstorm with downburst winds estimated at 70 to 80 mph lifted and rolled a double wide home on County Road 267 about 3 miles west of Caldwell. The mobile home traveled 70 feet where it finally landed on its roof. The mobile home was completely destroyed. A couple of vehicles were also heavily damaged. The downburst also removed a large part of the roofing material from the Country Hearth Inn near the interchange of Interstate 40 and Highway 1B in Forrest City.

Damaging straight line winds knocked down power lines on U.S. Highway 63 and Commerce Drive about 3 miles southeast of Jonesboro. Trees were also knocked on to homes and vehicles about 5 miles south of Jonesboro. A camping trailer was overturned at this location as well. The damaging winds spread toward Bay knocking down power lines at the intersection of Main Street and Central Avenue. Power lines were knocked down and a shed was damaged in town of Lunsford along Highway 158 east of Bay.
