Damaging straight line winds struck the Lakeshore Community in Marion. One trailer was completely destroyed and three others suffered minor damage. Trees were knocked down on cars and power lines were also knocked down.

Damaging straight line winds uprooted numerous large trees and tore away metal roof parts from several outbuildings in the southeast corner of Desoto County. A large metal carport awning was picked up and carried 25 to 30 yards. Damage was mostly in an area about one half mile long and up to 100 yards wide. Isolated trees were also downed to the east for another one half mile.
Damaging straight line winds downed multiple trees and large tree limbs about 5 miles east of Dyersburg. A few cars were damaged.

Damaging straight line winds tore the front roof off of a home on Shook Road in the Paynes Community. A carport was flipped and destroyed while an outbuilding was damaged. Trees and power lines were also knocked down.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Coffeeville.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down trees in the western part of Henderson County. Trees were also knocked down and covered roads in Scotts Hill.
Damaging straight line winds destroyed a porch and lifted it over a mobile home in Randolph. Several trees were knocked down across southern portions of Pontotoc County.

Damaging straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Van Vleet near the Post Office. A roof was blown off a mobile home. A porch was lifted and blown over a home. A large tree also fell on a home and a butane storage tank.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the Hamilton and Strong areas in southern Monroe County. Many roads were flooded including Rye Bottom Road and Valley Chapel Road among others. Some roads were covered with three feet of water.
Quarter size hail reported at the intersection of Mulberry Road and Old Highway 45.
Quarter size hail reported at the intersection of Rinda Road and Meridian Road.

A weak tornado touched down near Ferguson on Highway 44 and traveled northeast toward the Mississippi River. Some trees were knocked down. The tornado continued northeast crossing into Coahoma County, Mississippi.

A weak tornado traveled northeast out of Phillips County, Arkansas into Coahoma County. The tornado continued northeast toward the city of Coahoma where it eventually lifted. A church sustained roof damage, 3 miles southwest of Coahoma. Numerous trees were either uprooted or snapped. Scattered telephone poles were knocked down. A few road or advertisement signs were damaged as well. A few pivot irrigation systems were also toppled over.
Penny to golf ball size hail fell in Arlington.
Nickel size hail fell one mile south of Interstate 40 near Hickory Withe.
Golf ball size hail fell at the Helena Bridge.
Straight line winds overturned multiple irrigation pivots near Dubbs.
Golf ball to baseball size hail fell between Farrell to just north of Clarksdale.
Nickel size hail fell along Highway 51 near the Southern DeSoto County line.

Heavy rain produced widespread street flooding all across DeSoto County. Drainage ditches were overflowing and sewer covers were lifted off due to the abundant run-off water moving through the sewers. In Olive Branch, water rose high enough to flood a few homes on the southeast side of town. Numerous roads were closed throughout the county.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell one mile south of Coldwater along Highway 51.
Straight line winds overturned aluminum carports.
Golf ball to baseball size hail fell near the Como area.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across much of north and eastern portions of Shelby County. The intersection of Pisgah Road and Houston Levee Road in Cordova was covered by six to eight inches of water. Jenkins Road and Macon Road was flooded in Cordova as well. In addition, the intersection of Airline Road and Highway 70 in Arlington was closed due to flood waters. North of Collierville, Highway 205 South and Raleigh-LaGrange Road was flooded. In Millington, roads near Raleigh-Millington Road were flooded. One car was stranded in flood waters.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Marion and West Memphis. Numerous streets were flooded with water.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Marianna. Creeks and ditches that run into the L'Anguille River were overflowing between Highway 1 and the river, northwest of Marianna.
Straight line winds damaged a few homes in Smithville.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 205 South and Raleigh LaGrange Road, north of Collierville.
Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding around Tunica County. Numerous roads were closed as a result including School Street, Josephine Road, Dulaney Road, and Robin Cove.

A tornado touched down near Money Road outside of Philip and moved northeast. Many trees were snapped or uprooted. A fence was also blown over. The tornado continued northeast and crossed into Leflore County, Mississippi.

A tornado continued northeast out of Leflore County, Mississippi into Tallahatchie County. Several homes sustained shingle damage. A portion of a roof was ripped off a mobile home and building. Many trees were snapped or uprooted. The tornado lifted near Mudline Road, northwest of Oakland.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees along County Road 9 and County Road 10 near Tillatoba. One mobile home was destroyed by fallen trees.

Straight line winds produced damage north and west of Oxford. A roof was partially taken off of a house and a machine shop. Numerous homes sustained minor roof damage. Numerous trees and power lines were also knocked down. One person was killed when his 18-wheeler struck a fallen tree on Highway 30.

Straight line winds knocked several trees down from the Union County/Marshall County line northeast toward Myrtle. A few homes were damaged from fallen trees. One home was damaged from fallen trees near the intersection of Highway 349 and County Road 18. An injury occured as a result.

Heavy rain caused the Wolf River at Rossville to go above flood stage. Numeous roads were flooded and a few bridges were washed out in Southern Fayette County from Piperton to LaGrange including portions of Highway 194, Laconia Road, Highway 196, LaGrange Road and Highway 220. Two houses in Rossville were flooded as well.

An EF-3 tornado moved northeast out of Clay County, Mississippi into Chickasaw County just south of Trebloc. The tornado weakened to an EF-1 as it moved into Chickasaw County. One home was destroyed which resulted in two injuries. Several other homes sustained minor damage from fallen trees. A barn was damaged and trees were uprooted near Highway 8 and Highway 47. Numerous trees were knocked down along the path. The tornado continued northeast into Monroe County, Mississippi.

An EF-1 tornado moved northeast out of Chickasaw County into Monroe County. At least 31 homes and businesses sustained minor damage. Three injuries occurred in the Wren and New Wren area. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped along the path. Power lines were also knocked down as well.

A weak tornado touched down southwest of Jacks Creek and traveled northeast lifting just northeast of Jacks Creek. Numerous tree tops were broken off and many large trees were knocked down along the path. On Sweet Lips Road, a mobile home was damaged from a fallen tree. A couple of structures sustained roof damage. On Highway 100, trees and power lines were knocked down.
Straight line winds caused roof damage to a home and a workshop along Highway 228 West near Minturn. The workshop roof was partially blown off.

A weak tornado briefly touched down on Hill House Road near the Cloverport area and traveled northeast lifting just north of Toone. A tin roof on a home was peeled back. Numerous trees were knocked down in the area.
Damaging straight line winds knocked down a transmission line and damaged some buildings at the Fairgrounds in Jonesboro. There was a measured gust of 62 mph at the Jonesboro airport at 9:04 PM CST.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Paragould and caused roof damage at the Greene County Technical High School.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in the Tupelo area.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines at the intersection of Highway 278 and Highway 8 in Greenwood Springs.

Straight line winds caused minor roof damage to houses in Fisher, Harrisburg and Truman. A carport was knocked down near Fisher and a few signs were blown down in Trumann. Trees and power lines were knocked down throughout the county.

A tornado touched down along County Road 864 in extreme Southern Tishomingo County and traveled northeast toward Belmont. Thirty homes and a few apartments were damaged or destroyed in Belmont. Two businesses were destroyed and the town's maintenance yard was severely damaged. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. One tree fell on a vehicle and trapped the driver. The tornado lifted northeast of Belmont near County Road 993.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Burnsville. A barn and an outdoor shed were also damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Strickland and Glen. Trees and power lines were also knocked down on County Road 356.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Crawfordsville. A few of the trees fell on vacant houses. Two tractor trailers were blown over on Interstate 55 near Marion. A roof of a business was blown off and there were many trees and power lines knocked down near Marion.
Straight line winds knocked trees down near Horseshoe Lake.
Straight line winds ripped a mobile home in half near Lehi, close to the intersection of Highway 70 and Interstate 40. A tractor trailer was also blown over in the vicinity.

Straight line winds knocked down storage buildings. A gas station awning was blown off and two gas pumps at another gas station were blown over. A hotel and several homes in the area suffered roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs from Walls to Horn Lake.
Straight line winds caused damage from Atoka to Brighton. Six houses, four mobile homes, three businesses and eight farm buildings were destroyed. Many trees and signs were also knocked down.

Straight line winds created a swath of damage across Northern Shelby County. Damage in the Frayser and Raleigh areas consisted of broken shingles along with downed fences and trees. In the Millington area, a tree was knocked down destroying a couple of fences and power lines were knocked down across Cuba Millington Road. In the Bolton area, near the high school, roofs and buildings were damaged and many trees were knocked down. There was also minor fence damage southwest of Arlington. Across Shelby County there were 22 homes with minor damage, 13 homes with major damage and 5 homes were destroyed.
Straight line winds knocked trees down in Germantown and Cordova and briefly trapped one person in a house.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs in Cooter.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines throughout Lauderdale County.
Straight line winds damaged a mini storage building on Highway 1 south of Lawson Street to the south of Jonesboro. Several 50 foot transmission poles were also broken in the area.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees all across Prentiss County. Three houses sustained roof damage.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding all across Tate County. Numerous roads were flooded as a result. A school bus accident occurred as a result of the flooding which resulted in seven injuries.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across Dyer County from the Mississippi River through Dyersburg and into Newbern. Forty-four houses, twenty-nine mobile homes, six businesses and nineteen farm buildings were destroyed. Thirty-eight houses, six mobile homes and eight farm buildings suffered major damage. Many trees were also knocked down.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across Gibson County. Sixteen homes, fourteen mobile homes and one public building were destroyed. Sixteen homes, one public building and three businesses suffered major damage. Forty-five homes and seven businesses suffered minor damage. Many trees, power lines and signs were also knocked down.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Union City.
Heavy rain produced extensive flash flooding all across Benton County. Many roads were flooded as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down some small to medium trees on Highway 371 and Donavon Road near Mantachie. A roof was partially blown off a church in Mantachie as well.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across Weakley County. Five buildings were destroyed. Four homes suffered major damage. Three homes, two mobile homes and one business suffered minor damage. There were also numerous trees and power lines knocked down.
Straight line winds knocked trees down north of Tupelo.
Penny size hail reported in Saltillo and Baldwyn.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across parts of Carroll County including Huntingdon. Two mobile homes, two businesses and two farm buildings were destroyed. Twenty-eight homes and one public building suffered minor or major damage. Many trees were knocked down as well.
Heavy rain produced excessive flooding across all of LaFayette County. Numerous roads were closed and a water rescue occurred in Oxford.
Penny to golf ball size hail fell from Downtown Memphis, through Midtown Memphis and Bartlett, all the way to the Ellendale area. A windshield of a car was broken in Downtown Memphis.

Straight line winds caused considerable damage across Henry County. Forty to fifty homes received minor to moderate damage while several barns and outbuildings were destroyed. One mobile home on Jones Bend Road was destroyed when a large tree fell across one of the bedrooms. Many trees and power lines were also knocked down.
Straight line winds damaged a roof near the intersection of Wheeler Road and Highway 51 in the southern part of De Soto County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and large limbs partially blocking Orr Road in Fayette County.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs in Decaturville.
Penny size hail fell in the south part of Clarksdale.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Morris Chapel.
Straight line winds destroyed two mobile homes and damaged two others in Crockett County. A house also suffered minor damage.
Straight line winds destroyed three homes in Madison County and caused minor or major damage to six others.
Straight line winds caused considerable damage to six houses and six mobile homes across Henderson County. One business and seven farm buildings were also damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 9 near Sarepta.
A wind gauge on the roof of a house measured sustained winds at 65 mph with gusts to 89 mph.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of large trees across Beech Springs Street near the WTVA TV Station in Tupelo.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and power lines along County Road 451 and County Road 460 near the town of Vardaman.
Straight line winds caused damage throughout Northern Monroe County. Many trees were knocked down. Several homes in Nettleton and Amory suffered damage from fallen trees.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near the town of Woodland.
Heavy rain resulted in the flooding of the Highway 278 underpass in Amory.
Golf ball size hail fell near College Hill.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell on a mobile home along Highway 348.
Nickel size hail fell just north of Guntown.
Quarter size hail fell in the Shady Acres Development just south of the airport.
Quarter size hail fell on Pea Vine Road between Middleton and Bolivar.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Helena-West Helena. A block and a half of Highway 49 was flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down trees north of Batesville.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell across the city of Oxford including the University of Mississippi campus and downtown.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree that hit a gas meter and caused a gas leak behind the Post Office.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Clarksdale. Several streets were flooded.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Calhoun City. Trees and power lines were also knocked down in Vardaman and a couple of homes were damaged as well. A tree was uprooted on Highway 8 which pulled up a gas line.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Chickasaw County. One tree fell on a home in Houston resulting in minor injuries to a child.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across the southern end of Lee County.
Straight line winds knocked down many trees across the northern part of Monroe County.
Heavy rain caused areas of flash flooding in Baldwyn. Several streets were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked several large tree limbs down on Cotton Gin Road near the Alabama border. In addition, a tin roof was torn off a porch near Fairview.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding throughout Henderson County. At least six inches of water was covering many roads near Lexington.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding all across Gibson County. North College Street in Trenton had up to a foot of water covering the road. Central Street was also closed.  North of Milan, Cades Atwood Road was closed due to flooding. Middle Road in Milan was also closed. South of Bradford, Highway 45 was closed due to high water covering the road. Highway 152 near Humboldt was also closed due to flooding.  Numerous other roads around the county were closed as well.
Heavy rain flooded Highway 178, Highway 23, and Briar Ridge Road near Tremont. Numerous other roads throughout Itawamba County were closed due to flood waters as well.
Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding all across Union County. Numerous roads were closed with up to three feet of water covering some of the roads.
Half dollar to baseball size hail fell in Pocahontas.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Chester County. Highway 45 near Henderson was closed as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding all across Hardeman County. Numerous roads were closed as a result. A mudslide occurred on Highway 121 which knocked down power poles.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding all across Tunica County. Most of the roads were closed due to water covering them. Some roads had up to 3 feet of water covering them. Old Highway 61 was washed out between Dundee and Mayplace.

Heavy rain caused extensive flash flooding all across Marshall County. Numerous roads had culverts washed out. Several motorists had to be rescued after vehicles were driven into the flood waters. One motorist died after driving his vehicle into flood waters on Slayden Road where the road had been washed out.

A tornado touched down along County Road 378, east-southeast of Springdale, and moved northeast. The most concentrated area of damage was in the Pine Flat community. A number of homes and mobile homes were damaged or destroyed. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down as well. Damage occurred on County Roads 415, 369, and 469. The tornado lifted just north of Highway 278 along County Road 213. Eight injuries occurred from the tornado.
A weak tornado briefly touched down on Highway 370 near Locum and moved northeast. Numerous trees were knocked down. The tornado lifted near County Road 235.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees south of Oxford.

A weak tornado briefly touched down along Highway 356, east of Rienzi, and moved northeast. Minor damage occurred to a few homes. Several trees were knocked down as well. The tornado lifted near County Road 430.

A weak tornado briefly touched down just west of Highway 1, approximately 5 miles south of Jonesboro and moved northeast. The tornado crossed over Highway 1 and then lifted. An office building had the roof partially blown off. Two garage doors of storage units were blown in. One window was blown out of a business and a chain link fence was partially knocked down as well.

A tornado briefly touched down just southwest of Highway 158, northeast of Bay, and moved northeast. The tornado crossed Highway 158 before lifting just before it reached Highway 63. Some damage occurred to the Bay Arkansas Airport. The airport measured a 113 mph gust. A carport awning was lifted and thrown by the tornado.

A weak tornado touched down near Endville Road, just southeast of Endville, and moved northeast. A couple of homes sustained minor damage. Numerous trees were knocked down. The tornado lifted near Martin Road.

A strong tornado moved northeast out of Webster County into extreme Southeastern Calhoun County. At least one home sustained major damage and one barn was destroyed. Numerous trees were knocked down. The tornado continued to move northeast and crossed into Chickasaw County.
Straight line winds knocked large tree limbs down in Calhoun City.

A strong tornado crossed into Chickasaw County from Calhoun County and continued to move northeast. The Anchor community was the hardest hit area where one death occurred. An additional two deaths occurred east of Houston. In total, seventy-four homes were destroyed with an additional ninety-two sustaining major damage. A total of twenty-five mobile homes were destroyed with and an additional fifteen sustaining major damage. Numerous other homes and mobile homes sustained minor damage. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in the area. A total of twenty-five injuries occurred from the tornado. The tornado continued northeast and crossed into Monroe County.

A strong tornado moved into Monroe County from Chickasaw County and continued northeast. The New Wren community was especially hit hard. At least 20 homes were destroyed or sustained major damage. Hundreds of trees were snapped or debarked. Numerous power lines were knocked down. One motorist was killed as the tornado moved through the area.

A tornado briefly touched down near Pekin Road near Bowman and moved northeast. The tornado lifted near Highland Drive in Bowman. Five homes and one business garage was damaged. Three mobile homes sustained roof damage. Two brick homes and one business garage also sustained roof damage. A storage shed was destroyed. A chain link fence was blown over. A few trees and tree limbs were knocked down.

A weak tornado briefly touched down along County Road 513, northeast of Black Oak. The tornado moved northeast crossing Highway 18. The tornado lifted southwest of Monette along County Road 506. A pivot irrigation system was flipped over. Two telephone poles were knocked down. A few tree limbs were broken.

After lifting for 4 miles, a violent EF-5 tornado touched back down southwest of Smithville and moved northeast. The town of Smithville was almost completely destroyed by the tornado. Homes and businesses were completely wiped off of their foundations. The town hall, post office, police station, and four churches were destroyed. All appliances and plumbing fixtures in the direct path of the tornado were shredded or missing. Granite tombstones were knocked down in the opposite direction of the tornado passage. A ford explorer that was parked a half mile away from the town's water tower was picked up by the tornado and thrown into the top of the water tower. The vehicle was then thrown an additional few hundred feet. In total, 117 structures were destroyed with an additional 50 structures sustaining major damage. Numerous other structures sustained minor damage. Trees were debarked, twisted, and snapped. Power lines were knocked down and the town's water system was destroyed. A lot of the homes that were destroyed were well built, bolted to their foundations and were less than 10 years old. A total of 16 fatalities occurred from the tornado. Thirty-seven injuries occurred as well. The tornado continued northeast after destroying Smithville and crossed into Itawamba County, Mississippi.

A violent tornado moved northeast from Monroe County, Mississippi into Southeast Itawamba County. The tornado weakened as it moved through Itawamba County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. One home sustained roof damage. The tornado continued northeast and crossed over into Marion County, Alabama.
Straight line winds produced roof and structural damage in Okolona.
A weak tornado touched down on the shore of Sardis Lake and moved northeast across the lake. The tornado lifted by the time it reached the other shore. No damage occurred from the tornado.

A tornado touched down about a quarter mile west of County Road 253 in East Central Tippah County and tracked northeast. The tornado lifted between County Road 254 and the Tippah/Alcorn County line. One home and two mobile homes sustained minor damage. A portion of a mobile home roof and awning was ripped off. Several trees were either snapped or uprooted. A few telephone poles were also snapped off.

A tornado touched down south of Counce and moved northeast toward Pickwick Lake. The tornado lifted just before reaching Pickwick Lake. At least 15 homes sustained moderate to major damage. A number of other homes sustained minor damage.  Two mobile homes were destroyed. A pizza restaurant and a hardware store were also destroyed.  Numerous trees and power lines were also knocked down. Two minor injuries occurred from the tornado.

Heavy rain brought the Wolf River to near record levels in Germantown. Collierville-Arlington Road was flooded between Shelton and Raleigh-LaGrange. Two vehicles had to be pulled to safety as a result. The AgriCenter RV Park and Farm Road in Shelby Farms was partially flooded. An RV was damaged as a result. Humphreys Boulevard near Walnut Grove Road was flooded as well as Wolf River Boulevard in Germantown between Germantown Parkway and Riverdale Road. Walnut Bend Road in Cordova was flooded and the flood water approached homes in the area. A few businesses in the area of Walnut Bend were flooded.
The severe (D2) drought ended across the area.
The severe (D2) drought ended across the area.
The severe (D2) drought ended across the area.
The severe (D2) drought ended across the area.
The severe (D2) drought conditions ended across the area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Corinth. Numerous streets were closed as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding all across Lee County. Numerous roads were flooded in Baldwyn and Tupelo as a result.
Heavy rain produced widespread road flooding all across Panola County. Numerous streets were washed out near Crenshaw and Como.
Straight line winds knocked trees down between Crenshaw and Como. At least five homes in Crenshaw, were damaged by fallen trees. Two of the five homes sustained major damage.

Straight line winds knocked down trees on to county vehicles on Highway 284 and at the intersection of Highway 75 and Highway 70. One mobile home was severely damaged at the intersection of Highway 70 and Highway 79 in Chatfield. Two mobile homes were severely damaged in Shearerville.
Quarter size hail covered the ground.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 59 between Covington and Mason. The highway was covered by a foot of water in places.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees between Upper and Lower James Creek Roads just north of Ravenden Springs.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down in Warm Springs and a power line in Middlebrook.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of power lines at the intersection of County Road 224 and Highway 141 in the town of Beech Grove.
Straight line winds destroyed a shed in Rector.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree and a couple of power lines near the intersection of Railroad Street and Frisco Street.
A trained spotter reported a 62 mph wind gust on his personal weather station.
A wind gust of 66 mph was recorded at the Sheriff's Office in Dresden.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Lucy Elementary School in Millington. Amherst Road had at least 10 inches of running water over it.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding in Jonesboro. Numerous streets were closed including Carraway Road, Nettleton Road, Harrisburg Road and Grant Avenue. A few cars became stranded in the flood waters. The Dollar Tree parking lot was flooded as well as areas near the Fairgrounds and Equine Center at Arkansas State University.
Straight line winds knocked multiple trees and power lines down at Highway 75 and County Road 306, south of Parkin. A few homes sustained minor damage.
Half Dollar to golf ball size hail fell near Arlington.
Penny to quarter size hail fell from near Griffen to Longtown.

Heavy rain produced widespread flash flooding from Downtown to Midtown Memphis. Numerous streets were closed or at least partially closed including Third Street and Gaston, North Parkway and Watkins Avenue, North Parkway and Cleveland, Raleigh-Millington and Jones, Interstate 55 and Brooks and many more. Vehicles became stranded in flood water at the intersection of Sam Cooper Boulevard and East Parkway.
Heavy rain caused water in storm drains to back up flooding Belvedere Street in West Memphis.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Walnut Ridge.

Straight line winds caused partial roof damage to three homes. A carport and an awning were also destroyed. A few trees and privacy fences were also knocked down. The damage occurred on the south side of Malden.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Piggot.
Straight line winds ripped part of a roof off a house in Campbell. Numerous tree limbs were also knocked down.
A weak tornado touched down in open country. No damage was found.
Straight line winds damaged a carport and knocked down tree limbs near Portageville.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Cooter.
Straight line winds caused significant damage to the roofs of a home and a barn in Cottonwood Point.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in the vicinity of Caruthersville. Strong winds lasted for 30 minutes.

A tornado touched down in West Memphis and a large storage building received major roof damage with numerous contents removed and a few walls crippled. A mobile home received extensive damage and a tree fell on one residence. A few other tree limbs were snapped and a power pole was knocked down just east of the intersection of Highway 70 and Club Road. The estimated peak wind was 90 mph.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple power lines across Crittenden County.
Straight line winds knocked down a few power lines and large trees near the intersection of Highway 76 and Main Street in Somerville.
Straight line winds caused roof damage at an apartment complex in Tiptonville. An outdoor carwash suffered major damage while several trees and power poles were knocked down.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines at Summer Avenue and Raleigh Lagrange Road. A large tree was knocked down just north of Stage Road near Appling Road.
Straight line winds knocked power lines down and caused minor roof damage to a home.
Straight line winds caused minor damage to the roofs of several homes in Newbern.

Straight line winds caused a swath of damage from Troy to Union City. Multiple trees and power lines were knocked down. Some homes were damaged by fallen trees. One building was destroyed and multiple power lines were knocked down. A flag pole was broken and a business sign was damaged.
Straight line winds knocked multiple trees and power lines down in Halls. Several homes had minor roof damage.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Trumann. Highway 69 was closed in town as a result of high water.
Heavy rain flooded fields behind homes on Zaida Avenue in Caruthersville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Pillowville. The intersection of Highway 124 and Presson Road was covered with 10 inches of water.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines and small tree limbs in the Brownsville area.
The ASOS at McKellar Field recorded a 58 mph gust.
The ASOS at McKellar Field recorded a 61 mph gust.

Straight line winds caused damage to many houses and knocked down many trees and power lines in the Paris area. Some of the trees fell on homes causing additional damage. One home was destroyed and 34 homes suffered minor to major damage. One mobile had minor damage.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in the Oxford area. The canopy was blown off a gas station at the intersection of Highway 278 and Thacker Road.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across McNairy County. Communities most impacted were Adamsville, Selmer, Stantonville and Milledgeville.  A few industrial buildings were damaged.

Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a house and ripped a gas line up in New Albany. A house had shingles ripped off and a barn roof was blown off. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in New Albany and across northeast Union County.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines across southern and central parts of Pontotoc County.
Straight line winds caused major damage to two homes and minor damage to one home. A roof was ripped off a mobile home in Shannon. Several trees were knocked down as well.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across much of Hardin County. A house and two vehicles were damaged by fallen trees in the Shiloh area. Across the county a total of five homes suffered minor damage and a mobile home had major damage. One farm building was also destroyed. Areas most impacted besides Shiloh included Bruton Branch, Pickwick, Counce and Walnut Grove.

Straight line winds caused damage across parts of Southern Dunklin County. Two irrigation systems and the roof of a mobile home were damaged in Senath. An irrigation system was damaged and a roof was blown off a mobile home in Hornersville. The mobile home also had window damage. In the Rives community, the side of a mobile home was caved in, windows were broken and a screened in porch was damaged. A pop up camper was destroyed and a meter box was torn from the side of the mobile home.
Straight line winds resulted in minor tree damage in Hickory Ridge.
Straight line winds destroyed two grain bins in Tunica County.

Straight line winds destroyed one home and caused major damage to two others in Tallahatchie County. Two homes had minor damage and one business was destroyed. One farm building was destroyed while another had major damage.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Alcorn County. Thirty roads across the county were closed due to flooding.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across Panola County.
Straight line winds damaged a home in Alcorn County rendering it uninhabitable.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Stanton.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Madison County.

Heavy rain brought the Black River in Black Rock to just under record levels in late April and the river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Homes and businesses sustained minor damage from the flooding. Black Rock and Portia were evacuated, but Portia was spared from any damage.  Many roads and bridges were also flooded and/or damaged. Portions of Black Rock and Powhatan Courthouse State Parks were flooded. Several thousand acres of cropland was flooded as well.

Heavy rain from numerous rounds of severe storms brought the Black River at Pocahontas to record levels during late April which continued through the end of May. The crest surpassed the Flood of 1915. Two levees broke sending water further away from its normal banks. Much of the area around Pocahontas was flooded as a result. U.S. Highway 67 was flooded between Pocahontas and Walnut Ridge. The Current River was also extremely high in Eastern Randolph County. Numerous homes and businesses were flooded. Roads and bridges were flooded and/or damaged. Evacuations occurred in Pocahontas and East Pocahontas. A woman drowned when she drove her vehicle into flood waters on Highway 67 between Pocahontas and the Lawrence County line during the early morning hours of May 3rd.

Heavy rain brought the Black River near Corning to record levels in late April that continued into the beginning of May. The record crest surpassed the Flood of 1945. Shallow flooding extended for several miles away from the river. Several homes and businesses sustained minor damage from the flooding. Many roads and bridges were closed and/or damaged including Highway 62, Highway 67 and Highway 155. The Clay County Airport was flooded as well.

Heavy rain during the end of April into the beginning of May caused the Cache River to rise above flood stage. Numerous roads were closed and/or damaged. Some homes sustained minor damage. One man drowned while attempting to check on his flooded home. He became disorientated and could not tell where the road and the flood waters were. He drove his vehicle into a flooded ditch as a result.

Heavy rain during late April into the beginning of May caused the St. Francis River to rise above flood stage. The river rose to near record levels in the beginning of May and remained above flood stage through the end of May. A break in the levee in Butler County, Missouri, north of Clay County, caused some concern that additional flood water would move into Clay County. However, the water never made it into Clay County. A few homes sustained minor damage. Several roads were closed and/or sustained damage. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded. A man drowned when his boat capsized in the flood waters.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River to rise to near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several roads were closed and/or damaged. A few homes sustained minor damage. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River at Lake City to rise to tie the all-time record crest set back in 1979. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several homes sustained minor damage from the flooding. Several roads were closed and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River to rise to near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several homes sustained minor damage from the flooding. The city of Payneway had to be evacuated as a result of the flooding. Several roads were closed and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River to rise to near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several homes sustained minor damage from the flooding. Several roads were closed and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded. A man drowned when he disobeyed closed road signs on Highway 42 and drove his vehicle into 12-18 inches of running water that covered the road. The vehicle was then swept away.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River at Madison and L'Anguille River at Palestine to rise to near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several homes sustained minor damage from the flooding.  Several roads were closed and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded.

Heavy rain during late April into early May caused the St. Francis River and L'Anguille River to rise to near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of May. Several homes sustained minor damage from the flooding.  Several roads were closed and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of cropland was flooded. The Mississippi River was also at near record levels. Backwater from the Mississippi River aggravated flooding further on the St. Francis River and L'Anguille River.
Straight line winds pealed a metal roof off a building in Toone.
Quarter to golfball size hail fell south of Holly Springs.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in the College Hill area. Numerous roads were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along County Road 514 and County Road 515.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Amory.

Heavy rains during late April into the beginning of May caused the St. Francis River to reach near record levels. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month. Numerous roads were flooded and/or damaged. Several homes and businesses sustained minor damage due to flooding. Several agriculture fields were flooded. The town of Hornersville was flooded. In addition, the town of Wilhelmina was evacuated due to flood waters.

The Mississippi River rose to record levels in Caruthersville by mid-May. The city of Caruthersville held back the river by reinforcing the flood wall with sandbags thus the city was able to stay mainly dry with the exception of a few streets that were flooded. However, surrounding areas were flooded including many agriculture fields and a few homes right along the river. The casino boat in Caruthersville was closed due to flooding. Barge traffic was closed for a short time on the river. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River at Helena-West Helena rose to near record levels during the beginning and middle part of May. Helena-West Helena escaped the flood waters by reinforcing the flood wall with sandbags. A residential area off of Highway 44 and Lithium Road was evacuated as a precaution. A few roads were flooded and/or damaged. Several thousand acres of fields were flooded. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to record levels by the beginning and middle part of May. Levees held back the water thus only a few homes along the river were flooded and sustained damage. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels at Osceola during the beginning and middle part of May. About 50 homes were damaged by backwater flooding from the Mississippi River into tributaries and along the Mississippi River itself. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning and middle part of May. A few homes located right along the river were flooded and sustained damage but mostly forest area along the river was flooded. A few roads were flooded and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of fields were flooded. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning and middle part of May. The area known as Tunica Cut-Off was flooded as many as 357 homes sustained damage. All nine casinos in Tunica County were closed and sustained some damage from flooding. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. Several hundred acres of fields were flooded as well. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning and middle part of May. The Lakeview community was flooded. Several homes were flooded and sustained at least minor damage. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged as well. Several hundred acres of fields were flooded as well. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels in Memphis during the beginning to middle part of May. Portions of Beale Street, Riverside Drive, Tom Lee Park and the Pyramid parking lot were flooded. Portions of Mud Island flooded as well including the Mud Island Ampitheater. The flooding wiped out nearly half mile section of the eastern bank of Presidents Island. As a result, the port at McKellar Lake was closed. Several businesses on Presidents Island sustained damage. Backwater from the Mississippi River caused the Wolf River to rise above flood stage. Numerous homes along the Wolf River in North Memphis and Raleigh were flooded as a result.  Two mobile home parks in Millington were evacuated due to concerns of high water on Big Creek from backwater of the Mississippi River. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning to middle part of May. A few homes along the river were flooded and sustained damage. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning to middle part of May. A few homes along the river were flooded and sustained damage. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to near record levels during the beginning to middle part of May. A few homes along the river were flooded and sustained damage. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.

The Mississippi River rose to record levels in Tiptonville during the beginning to middle part of May. A few homes along the river were flooded and sustained damage while additional homes in Tiptonville were flooded and sustained minor damage. Campgrounds at Reelfoot Lake were flooded. Several thousand acres of agriculture fields were flooded. Several roads were flooded and/or damaged. Lake County Airport was closed due to the flooding. The river remained above flood stage through the end of the month.
A three month old baby was left by accident in a vehicle during a hot May morning. The baby died as a result.
Three deaths occurred in the Memphis area as a result of the heat.
One death occurred in Brighton as a result of the heat.
Quarter size hail fell on County Road 272 between Corning and Piggott.
A gust front ahead of a line of thunderstorms knocked some shingles off a roof of an apartment building in Jonesboro.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Warm Springs and Pocahontas.
Straight line winds knocked down two trees on Clifton Road to the northeast of Savannah.
Straight line winds knocked trees down, ripped shingles off houses and blew over a metal porch in the Pine Flat Community.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines just southwest of Counce near Pickwick Landing.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Northern Tippah County.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Highway 45 and Highway 72.
Quarter size hail was reported on Highway 365 just north of Burnsville.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Falkner.
Two inch hail damaged a metal roof of an office building and a couple of greenhouses near Lorado.
Dime to quarter size hail fell in the town of Biggers.
Quarter size hail fell on Highway 141 just south of Walcott.
Quarter size hail fell in the Jonesboro area.
Nickel to Golfball size hail fell in Neuhardt.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Bay.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down and flipped a trampoline in the town of Rector.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines in the town of Moro.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 90, west of Highway 135, near Knobel.
Straight line winds knocked down trees all across Greene County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Paragould.

A tornado touched down just north of U.S. Highway 412, about 4 miles east of Paragould. The tornado overturned a semi-truck on Highway 412. Two homes, one business and one barn on the south side of the highway sustained roof damage. Windows were also blown out. The tornado continued on a south-southeast path and caused severe damage to a single wide mobile home along County Road 932. The entire roof was blown off and more than half of the walls were knocked down. A second single wide mobile home along County Road 905 sustained partial roof damage. A business size metal storage building along County Road 905 sustained significant roof damage and a steel carport was destroyed. Sheet metal from the storage building was found in cornfields up to a mile away on the track. Several trees were uprooted and branches were knocked down all along the track. The tornado lifted in a corn field, a quarter mile east of County Road 932.

Straight line winds knocked down trees all across Craighead County. In addition, signs were blown off of buildings in Monette. Power poles and power lines were knocked down along Highway 226 near Valley View as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Cardwell.

Straight line winds produced damage from near Etowah, to south of Keiser, to the Mississippi River. Trees were knocked down all across Mississippi County. Power lines were also knocked down. A fire house in Etowah lost its roof due to the winds. A semi-truck was overturned near mile marker 41 on Interstate 55 south of Keiser. Winds were reported near 60 mph near the Mississippi River by amateur radio.

The ASOS at Memphis International Airport reported a wind gust of 60 mph as the squall line moved through. Trees and power lines were knocked down in the area from southeast of Bartlett to the Hickory Hill area.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees throughout Germantown and Collierville.
Quarter to ping pong size hail fell in Walls.

Winds were estimated at 95 mph at the Olive Branch AWOS. Major damage occurred to airport hangars. Doors were blown out of two hangars while another one had the side panel blown out. One employee was injured when the wind slammed a hangar door into his hand. Two planes were overturned and damaged. In total, eight planes sustained damage. Minor damage occurred to buildings surrounding the airport.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines all across Tate County.
Straight line winds produced roof damage to a restaurant in Wheatley.
Straight line winds knocked a tree down on Military Road in Helena-West Helena. In addition, several trees were knocked down across eastern sections of Helena-West Helena.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down near Sardis Lake. One tree fell on a camper in the Oak Grove Camp area of Sardis Lake. Two people were killed and one person was injured as a result.

Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down in the Lula and Moon Lake area. Two homes sustained damage as well. A tractor-trailer was overturned on Highway 49 heading toward the Helena Bridge. A second tractor-trailer was overturned at the intersection of U.S. Highway 278 and Highway 6, east of Clarksdale.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down across Eastern Tallahatchie County. A couple of homes sustained damage from fallen trees. A shed was also destroyed in Tutwiler.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines between Big Creek and Calhoun City. In addition, two homes in Calhoun City sustained roof damage.
Quarter to ping pong ball size hail fell near Highway 79 just west of Marianna.
Straight line winds knocked down the back wall of a farm shop near County Road 535. The roof was also ripped off the shop. Several trees were also knocked down in Kennett.
Quarter size hail fell near Como.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees along Highway 310 outside of Como.
Penny to nickel size hail fell in the Olive Branch area.
Straight line winds knocked down four large trees across Weakley County.
Straight line winds knocked a couple of trees down near Roan Creek between Clarksburg and Yuma.

Straight line winds produced minor roof damage to a home along Independence Loop near Independence. A tree fell onto a home in Lexington injuring an occupant. Additional trees and power lines were also knocked down in Lexington. A few homes sustained minor roof damage and a metal storage shed was blown off its foundation as well.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Crawfordsville.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines along Highway 100 near Decaturville. Four homes sustained damage from the fallen trees.
A 72 mph wind gust was recorded at the Memphis International Airport.
Straight line winds produced minor roof damage to a house, east of Arlington in Fayette County.
Quarter size hail fell near the intersection of Elmore Road and Goodman Road in Southaven.
Heavy rain flooded a low water crossing in Parsons.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Saltillo.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines across Calhoun County. Trees were reported down in Ellard, Calhoun City, and Vardaman.

A tornado briefly touched down in the town of Vardaman knocking down large trees. One tree fell on a house injuring an occupant and destroying the roof of the home. Other trees were snapped. Additional homes were damaged by fallen trees. Major damage occurred to several tractor sheds. One shed was blown into a tree line approximately 100 yards away.
Numerous large hail reports ranging from quarter to pool ball size were reported in the Cordova and Germantown areas.
Straight line winds snapped six power poles on Elizabeth Street in Tupelo. In addition, the winds overturned a tractor-trailer on Highway 45 north of Verona.
A 60 mph gust was recorded on a personal weather station in Cordova. A few trees were knocked down near Walnut Grove Road and Sanga Road.
Straight line winds knocked down three trees in Mantachie.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in the Waverly Farms area.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees in Ripley.
A 63 mph wind gust was recorded on a personal weather station in Atoka.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Fulton.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in the Tupelo area. Several trees were knocked down in Tombigbee State Park, east of Tupelo as well.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees approximately six miles west of Sherman.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Clarksdale.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Charleston.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Prairie.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding north of Bradford. Water covered Highway 45E near the Obion River.
Nickel size hail covered the ground in Wynne.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell between Samburg and Troy.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Burlison.
Nickel size hail fell from Bartlett to Arlington.
Straight line wind gusts were estimated at 60 to 65 mph from Ellendale to Arlington.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and a few power lines across Fayette County.
Quarter size hail fell near Highway 78 and Magnolia Drive in Olive Branch.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Henderson.
Straight line winds knocked down several large trees between mile markers 43 and 45 on Interstate 40.

Straight line winds knocked several trees and construction signs down in Savannah. A pharmacy and another building sustained roof damage from the winds. At Pickwick Dam, a couple of trees fell on a power pole.
An outflow boundary from a thunderstorm moved through Stanton and knocked down a few trees.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees near Highway 88 in Alamo. Power lines and trees were knocked down on Johnson Road. A storage building was damaged on Johnson Road.
Straight line winds knocked down trees throughout Henderson County.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Huntingdon.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Bible Hill Road.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding near Alamo. The intersection of Cox Road and Highway 152 was flooded.
Lightning struck an apartment complex in Southaven starting a fire that destroyed 8 units. A section of the roof collapsed into the structure as well.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees from just north of Imboden on Highway 63 into Pocahontas. A six foot fence was also blown over in Pocahontas.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines from Imboden to Black Rock. A tree was knocked on to a home in Black Rock.
A 71 mph wind gust was recorded at the Walnut Ridge Regional Airport.
A farmer was on a tractor cutting hay when a thunderstorm approached the Teasdale area. The farmer got off his tractor and was walking to his truck when he was struck by lightning and injured.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines down across Craighead County. Trees were knocked down on County Roads 333 and 318. Power lines were knocked down on East Highland Drive in Jonesboro. A tree was also blown down on Highway 163 south of Jonesboro.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Highway 364 in Vanndale.
Straight line winds knocked a tractor trailer off Highway 49 between Marmaduke and Halliday.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across the city of Osceola with numerous trees, power lines, power poles and large street lights knocked down. The West Elementary School was also damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree branches on to power lines in Frayser. Trees were also blown down on Shake Rag Road west of Millington.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees from Midtown Memphis into Cordova. A tree landed on a house in Midtown Memphis. Another large tree landed on two houses and a car in East Memphis.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Tipton County.
Straight line winds damaged a fire station in the town of Barton. Numerous trees were knocked down across the northern part of Marshall County.

Straight line winds caused moderate damage to several barns and sheds near Jumpertown on County Road 8401. Several trees were also knocked down on County Roads 8031 and 8061 in Northwest Prentiss County.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Corinth. Several roads were covered with 6 to 12 inches of water including Proper Street, Shiloh Road, Fulton Drive, North Madison Street, North Lane, 5th Street and 6th Street.
Straight line winds knocked down several large trees in Tishomingo County.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Tishomingo County. Several roads were covered with at least six inches of water for a short time.
Heat index readings ranged between 105 and 118 degrees. One death occurred as a result of the heat.

A tornado touched down about 2 miles northwest of Parsons Tennessee and scattered damage was found through forest and pasture land with large trees uprooted and snapped. The tornado then continued into Decatur County.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down across Northern Fayette County. A roof was taken off a cotton gin along Highway 222, north of Somerville.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees down near the Tennessee River in Hardin County. Some of the trees fell on a few homes. One home had its roof partially blown off.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down across Southern Decatur County, primarily south of Highway 100.
Straight line winds knocked trees down near the intersection of Highway 4 and Highway 305, east of Senatobia.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell northeast of Mantachie.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees and power lines down across Southeastern Pontotoc County.
Straight line winds knocked a few power lines down on the south side of Fulton.
Straight line winds knocked trees down near the Shannon Primary School.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down near Parham.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down near Dalton.
Heavy rain over Panola County, which lasted a couple of hours, produced flash flooding across the county. Multiple county roads were flooded including Springport Road.
Straight line winds produced extensive damage to a marina near Black Jack Point on Sardis Lake. Several boats were removed from their moorings and capsized.
Straight line winds blew off and destroyed an add-on roof that was attached to a mobile home.

Heavy rain moved over the area from East Memphis to Downtown Memphis. Up to four feet of water flooded the intersection of Madison Avenue and Manassas Street. In addition, up to a foot of water covered the two right hand lanes and shoulder of Interstate 240 North just before exit 31 Interstate 40 West to Little Rock.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Oxford. Molly Barr Street was flooded with water up to ankle depth.
Over the course of 40 minute span, three houses were struck by lightning in the Oxford area. Each strike caused a fire although minimal damage occurred as a result.
Heavy rain flooded the intersection of Highway H and Highway J north of Campbell.
Straight line winds knocked four trees in addition to power lines and power poles in Kennett.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous power lines and trees in Piggott.
Heavy rain produced extensive damage in Piggott. Multiple homes and one business sustained roof damage.

Straight line winds flattened several hundred acres of corn near the intersection of Highway 190 and Highway 54 in Eastern Weakley County.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple power poles along Highway 79 just south of Paris. A roof was blown off a sawmill in Henry.
Straight line winds associated with the outflow from a thunderstorm resulted in the partial roof loss of a church gymnasium.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Southern Tishomingo County near Belmont. Trees and power lines were knocked down near the Belmont Cemetery and along Natchez Trace Parkway. Trees were also knocked down along Red Bud Road.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Saltillo. Front, Pyle and Cartwright streets were all impacted. A tree fell on a house on Cartwright Street. Metal was blown off several roofs around town.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Tupelo. An awning was blown off a business as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Benton County.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees along Higdon Road near the community of Higdon.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees along Coontail Road near Lake Monroe.
Straight line winds produced a swath of damage between Altitude and Burton. Several trees and power lines were knocked down. Some minor structural damage occurred as well.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines in the Blackland area. A roof was blown off a house on County Road 7481, southwest of Blackland.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines between Dumas and the Prentiss County line.

Straight line winds produced a swath of damage from the southwest corner of Prentiss County near Geeville northeastward to Frankstown. Multiple trees and power lines were knocked down on County Road 6100. A few of the trees fell onto homes. Trees were also reported down on County Road 6061. In Frankstown, several trees were knocked down on Highway 30 West. Several homes on Highway 30 West were damaged as well.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell along County Road 6061 south of Geeville.

Two thunderstorms brought a long period of damaging winds to the Baldwyn area. Widespread trees and power lines were knocked down in Baldwyn. A roof was blown off a house in North Baldwyn. Several homes, businesses and vehicles were damaged in Downtown Baldwyn, some of which were damaged from fallen trees. A Red Cross shelter was opened for displaced families. Another house on Community Drive had the roof blown off. A barn and camper were blown over as well.
Two thunderstorms moved over the city of Baldwyn and produced very heavy rain. Numerous streets were flooded resulting in emergency responders having difficulty maneuvering around the city.
Straight line winds knocked down large trees in the Fulton area.
Straight line winds blew a window out of a pharmacy in Kennett.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Hayti.

Thunderstorm winds caused significant damage to some metal buildings, a house, and some very large trees. The hardwood trees were approximately 3 feet wide. One metal building had a portion of the roof peeled up as well as 2 garage doors blown in. The grain bins behind the metal building sustained dents near the top due to the winds. The house was damaged by one of the large trees falling on top of it. Two mobile homes were damaged as well with their roofs blown off. Additional smaller trees were snapped in the vicinity.

Several mobile homes were destroyed on the west side of West Helena.  One mobile home was flipped on the southwest side of a neighborhood on the outskirts of town. The bottom frame of the home struck a tree behind the home 15 feet in the air. The mobile home landed on its roof and was completely destroyed. Cars were damaged by flying debris and trees were also blown down. Another neighborhood southwest of town was damaged as well. In this neighborhood, two mobile homes were flipped. One was blown into another mobile home and a wood house. Power lines and irrigation systems were blown down in the fields between the two neighborhoods. In West Helena, only minor damage was noted to the Junior High School roof and the roof and siding of a few motels. A few storage sheds were blown over but had not been secured to the ground.
A trailer home was moved off its slab foundation on Bellvue Road near Clarksdale. A tractor trailer was overturned in the same area.

Three empty grain bins were damaged along New Africa Road. The walkway on top of the grain bins was blown down. One grain bin was moved back a foot or two off of its foundation. Each grain bin had dents near the top on the southwest side where the strongest winds hit. Power lines were also blown down in the same area.

On Highway 389 near County Road 85, south of Houston, a mobile home and a Jeep were damaged by a fallen tree. A fence was knocked down and a metal carport was blown across the road.  Awnings were torn off trailers in Houston. Trees were knocked on to cars and cars were blown off the road near Trebloc. Straight line winds caused extensive damage across much of Tallahatchie County. Trees and power lines were knocked down across the county. Further east a metal garage was extensively damaged at the intersection of Tatum Pond Road and Highway 32. A couple of mobile homes experienced roof damaged further south on Tatum Pond Road. In total eight homes were uninhabitable and two facilities were damaged which hindered the delivery of public services.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines in Jackson.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs in Red Banks.
Straight line winds knocked down trees county wide. A large tree fell on a manufactured home on County Road 501. A Ham radio tower was knocked down.
Heavy rain caused flashing flooding in parts of Southeast Memphis. Mount Moriah Road was covered with two feet of water.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Decatur County. Trees fell across Bohanas Landing Road and Highway 114.
Nickel size hail reported near Ripley.
Scattered trees and power lines were knocked down across the county due to straight line winds.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines and trees in Michie.
Straight line winds ripped vinyl siding and shingles off a house in the Nixon area.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees across Alcorn County. Several trees fell on vehicles.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines throughout most of Union County. Several county roads were blocked. A couple of houses were struck by fallen trees.
Scattered trees and power lines were knocked down by straight line winds across Phillips County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Pontotoc County. Towns hardest hit included Ecru, Toccopola, Furrs and Troy.

Straight line winds knocked down trees across Lee County. Numerous trees were blown down along Natchez Trace Parkway between mile markers 273 and 278. A home suffered roof damage in Mooreville. In total four homes suffered at least minor damage in Lee County. Four vehicles were also damaged.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Ripley resulting in several road closures.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous large trees in Belmont and Golden. A carport and two cars were crushed by fallen trees. Some structures had roofs completely blown off. In total three homes suffered major damage and 43 structures had at least minor damage in Tishomingo County.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines in Clarksdale. A tractor trailer was overturned on Highway 61.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Monroe County. Several roads were blocked by trees.
Lightning struck a store in Ripley. The attic and roof caught on fire resulting in minor damage.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Itawamba County. One business had a roof peeled back.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Crockett County.

Straight line winds knocked down a few power lines and several trees east of Bruceton.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees south of Milan.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and a few power lines across Itawamba County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in the town of Tishomingo.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines along Clayton Avenue in Tupelo.
Straight line winds knocked down trees throughout Weakley County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees throughout Chickasaw County.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple trees and power lines.
Straight line winds blew over a mobile home near Homestown in Pemiscot County. One person was injured.

Straight line winds damaged a barn roof and knocked down trees and power poles on Winchester Road east of Paris.  Several trees and power poles were snapped in Paris. A home in Paris suffered minor roof damage, losing some shingles.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines on Florence Road in Savannah.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Whitehaven.
Quarter size hail fell along Interstate 55 in Southaven.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in Charleston. The trees fell onto a few homes damaging them. One home was destroyed resulting in two minor injuries. Power lines were also blown down which resulted in seventy percent of Charleston being without power.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near the intersection of County Roads 957 and 992, approximately 3 miles south of Iuka.

A thunderstorm remained nearly stationary over Germantown for a long period of time. As a result, numerous streets were flooded with six to ten inches of water including Sherman Oaks Drive, Kilbirnie Drive near Kinlock Cove and Scruggs Drive. The intersection of Exeter Road and Farmington Boulevard was flooded with at least a foot of water.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees across North Jackson. A large tree was split and fell on a home on Dearborne Cove in North Jackson. A tree was uprooted and power lines were knocked down on Sleepywood drive. Power lines were also knocked down on Netherwood Drive.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along County Road 177 southeast of Burnsville.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in JP Coleman State Park.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees between Serepta and Vardaman.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees down across all of Randolph County. Some trees blocked roads near Ravenden Springs, Middlebrook and Engelberg communities.
Straight line winds knocked a tree onto a house, damaging the house, in Central Paragould.
Straight line winds knocked trees down, some of which fell onto power lines, near Jonesboro. A highway sign was blown into the roadway on Highway 18 just east of Jonesboro.
Quarter size hail fell north of Rector.

Straight line winds knocked down multiple trees, signs and power lines across Kennett. An apartment building suffered roof damage and the windows were blown out of a store. Several other small out buildings were also damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple large trees across Crockett County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in the Olive Branch area. The Olive Branch Airport AWOS observed a 65 mph wind gust.
A 65 mph wind gust was observed in Corinth. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down from East Corinth into Farmington. Trees fell on five homes causing roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines in the Cairo area.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines across the northern and central part of Tishomingo. Two houses were struck by trees. The power substation in Holcutt was damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down very large trees and power lines in Burnsville. Trees and power lines were also knocked down in Iuka.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees and snapped several power poles between Lamar Avenue and the I-240 loop.
Half dollar size hail fell near the intersection of Highway 309 and St. Paul Road.
Half dollar size hail fell on Highway 193 in Fayette County.

Straight line winds knocked down a very large tree on to the Vance Avenue Youth Development Center. It landed on the southeast section of the center. Two connected modular buildings that were recently renovated were damaged. A wooden deck was partially crushed and other roof damage led to some damage of the center's electronics.
