Showers and thunderstorms trained over the same area for at least an hour. Culverts could not handle the water, as a result, water rose and covered the southbound lane of Highway 363 south of Mantachie.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over Midtown Memphis for at least an hour. Streets became flooded as a result. Union Avenue near Belvedere had to be shut down and the intersection of Central Avenue and Barksdale Street had six to eight inches of standing water covering it.
Showers and thunderstorms trained over Olive Branch for at least an hour. As a result, water covered the road near the interchange of Hacks Cross Road and Highway 78.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down from Ripley to Dumas. At least 2000 homes lost power.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down across Prentiss County.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down in New Albany. One tree fell onto a house along Highway 348. Power was knocked out to most of Union County.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines across Marshall County.
Straight line winds produced roof and building damage to a restaurant northeast of Sherman.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over Oxford for a couple of hours producing very heavy rain. Major flash flooding occurred as a result. Numerous streets had at least six inches of water covering them with others flooded up to three feet. Three homes were flooded on Chandler Avenue and one home was flooded on South 18th Street. The homes had anywhere from a few inches up to a foot of water inside them. Cars and apartments were flooded along Highway 314 near the Oxford Airport.
Lightning struck a house in Oxford causing a fire. The house was destroyed as a result of the fire.
Multiple reports of quarter size hail in Corning.

A tornado briefly touched down southwest of the Corning Municipal Airport and traveled northeast across the northern portion of the airport. Two hangars were extensively damaged with a few others receiving minor damage. Many of the aircraft that were housed inside the hangar were heavily damaged as well. Two homes near the airport had windows blown out and a shed had the roof blown off. The tornado continued northeast crossing Highway 67. Power poles along the highway were knocked down. A clear path was seen in the bean field north of Highway 67. The tornado lifted near County Road 135. Large amounts of debris were found nearly 1.5 miles away from the airfield with one 930 pound piece of equipment found nearly a quarter of mile away from the building which it was being stored.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a house in Senath causing structural damage. A couple of trees were also knocked down in Kennett.
A tornado briefly touched down near the intersection of Highway N and US Highway 412 near Bucoda. A farm shed was damaged as well as the equipment inside.
Nickel size hail fell near Harmontown.
Straight line winds caused structural damage to a home and a shed in the community of Half Moon.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Caruthersville.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down across roads in Weakley County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines along U.S. Highway 45 just north of Kenton.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across Lauderdale County. Some of the trees blocked roads, one road in particular that was blocked was Highway 19, southeast of Ripley.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Crockett County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Carroll County. An awning was ripped off the rear of a building.
Straight line winds damaged doors of a large shop that were 24 feet high in Macedonia.
Pea to nickel size hail fell in Hollow Rock.
Quarter size hail fell at Pleasant View Road and Bartlett Road in Northeast Memphis.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees across Collierville Arlington Road just north of Collierville. One tree landed on a vehicle.
Straight line winds knocked down a few power lines in Ripley.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees near Sumner and Tutwiler.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Southaven and snapped a power pole in Hernando.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down onto three cars near the intersection of Caraway Road and Highway 63 in Jonesboro.
Showers and thunderstorms moved very slowly over Jonesboro. As a result, some of the streets became flooded with up to a foot of water.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding at several locations in Desoto County. The intersection of Getwell and Goodman Roads in Southaven was flooded. College Road was also flooded in Southaven. Streets were flooded in the Colonial Hills Subdivision. Flooding also occurred at Highway 51 and Old Highway 51 near Nesbit. A structure along Pleasant Hill Road in Nesbit suffered a partial collapse due to the heavy rains.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down across Lawrence County.
A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire in Walls.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down in Parkin. One tree fell onto Highway 184.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down in Marked Tree.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down across Mississippi County. A road sign for a local store was knocked down in Keiser.
Quarter size hail fell on Interstate 55 at mile marker 4.4 causing one vehicle to wreck.
Winds were measured at 56 mph with a gust of 69 mph in Halls.

Lightning struck the Henderson County Criminal Justice Complex causing extensive damage to the fire alarm system, electronic key system, National Crime Information Center records system and the 911 system.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across Dyer County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Obion County.
Wind gusts were measured at 68 moh near the border of Tipton and Shelby Counties.

Straight line winds knocked a tree down onto power lines at the intersection of Little John Road and Old Millington Road near Millington. Another large tree was split near Kirby Whitten Parkway and Ellendale Road in Bartlett. Power poles were also knocked down on Oak Road in Bartlett.

Showers and thunderstorms moved slowly over Obion County. As a result, heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Highway 22 and Highway 21 near Lassiter Corner and at the intersection of Highway 183 and Glass Road near Hornbeak.
Straight line winds knocked power poles down causing power outages north of Byhalia.

Straight line winds knocked the roof off the fertilizer bins at the Farmer's Co-Op in Harrisburg. The sign off of the Family Dollar store was also blown down. Numerous trees were knocked down around the Harrisburg area as well.
Straight line winds blew a roof off a shop building along Highway 69 in Paragould. In addition, a tractor-trailer was blown over on Tower Drive.
A tornado briefly touched down in a farm field near the intersection of County Road 147 and Highway 67, northeast of Corning.
Straight line winds knocked down a large tree and several large limbs on Highway 118 in the northern part of Tyronza and near Lepanto. One home received roof damage in Tyronza.
Straight line winds knocked down two large trees on South Parkway. Several other large trees and limbs were also knocked down across Midtown. 15,000 homes and businesses lost power.
Straight line winds removed a roof from a home on Highway 45 north of Aberdeen. Several trees were knocked down on Coontail Road. A car was knocked off the road.

Straight line winds knocked trees down on County Road 300 near Hornor.

Straight line winds knocked a large tree down at the intersection of Cobb Road and Old Highway 61 near Tunica. A shed was destroyed and an irrigation pivot was flipped in the area. In addition, power poles were blown down along Highway 4.

Straight line winds produced damage to a mobile home park in Millington. Two mobile homes sustained minor damage. A baseball field dugout roof was blown off in a baseball field adjacent to the mobile home park and tossed 20 feet. A few trees were snapped and uprooted on the west end of the mobile home park. One tree fell on a mobile home trapping the homeowner. He was later freed uninjured. A privacy fence was also blown down.

Straight line winds blew large billboards apart and broke large plexiglass signs in Kennett. Minor roof damage occurred to several buildings. Carports and a few portable buildings were blown over as well.
Quarter size hail fell near the intersection of Deadfall and McQuiston Roads near Idaville.

Straight line winds produced some minor damage to Coldwater High School in Coldwater. Two school buses had windows blown out. Roof and awning damage also occurred at the school. Several trees were knocked down in the area as well with a few of them falling on houses. A car was turned around by the winds on Highway 51 near the intersection of Arkabutla Road.
Straight line winds overturned a camper near Looxahoma. A tree limb also fell and damaged a home in the area. In Wyatte, a pole barn was destroyed.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Byhalia Road and Craft Road.
Straight line winds knocked a tree onto a house in Rena Lara.

Straight line winds caused damage across Desoto County. A tree fell on a house at Getwell Road and Windmere Road. The electric and gas lines were damaged. The house caught fire and burned down. A tree fell on a house in the Buena Vista subdivision at Thunderbird Drive along Highway 51 south of Hernando. A tree fell and destroyed an awning at the Lewisburg United Methodist Church. A house lost a lot of roof shingles on Fletcher Cove near Lewisburg.

Straight line winds shifted a home off its foundation south of Dublin near the Sunflower County line. One child was injured as a result. One agricultural shop and a couple of grain bins sustained major damage. Farm equipment inside the shop was damaged as a well.

Straight line winds destroyed two mobile homes as they were blown off their foundations while another five sustained major damage near the intersection of County Road 54 and County Road 51 near Myrtle. In addition,three homes sustained major roof damage from trees falling on them. Three agricultural buildings were destroyed with another five sustaining major damage. Numerous large trees and power lines were knocked down in the Myrtle area as well.
Straight line winds blew down a shed on Highway 32 about four miles west of Charleston. In the Paynes community a pecan tree hit a house.
A house was struck by lightning in Tupelo. The house caught fire as a result.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in the vicinity of Palestine.
Quarter to Golfball size hail fell in a corridor from Bartlett to Lakeland.
Quarter size hail fell at Presidents Island.

Damaging straight line winds snapped a few cedar trees at the ground. A small metal hay barn had roof damage and a partially built home received roof damage.
Damaging straight line winds damaged an awning at a gas station in Midtown Memphis.
Damaging winds knocked down several trees and a power pole near Forest Hill Irene Road.

Walnut Ridge AWOS reported blizzard conditions for three hours. Wind gusts were as high as 43 mph with visibilities of less than a quarter mile. Thunder was also reported. Randolph County received the second highest snow totals with amounts between eight and twelve inches with higher amounts in snow drifts.

Walnut Ridge AWOS reported blizzard conditions for three hours. Wind gusts were as high as 43 mph with visibilities of less than a quarter mile. Thunder was also reported. Lawrence County received the highest snow totals with amounts between seven and fourteen inches with higher amounts in snow drifts.

Near blizzard conditions occurred at the Corning Airport where wind gusts up to 44 mph occurred with less than a quarter mile visibility for two hours. Snow accumulations ranged from six to eleven inches.

Near blizzard conditions occurred across Greene County where wind gusts greater than 35 mph occurred with less than a quarter mile visibility for two hours. Snow accumulations ranged from six to ten inches.
Snow accumulations ranged from four to seven inches across Craighead County. A tree fell onto a house producing damage.
Snow accumulations ranged from two to six inches across Mississippi County.
Snow accumulations ranged from four to six inches across Poinsett County.
Snow accumulations ranged from two to four inches across Cross County.
Snow accumulations ranged from one to three inches across St. Francis County.
Snow accumulations ranged from one to three inches across Lee County.

Strong winds knocked down trees and caused power outages across central and southern areas of Tupelo.
Heavy rain fell in Jesup and the intersection of Highway 117 and Highway 115 was closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Decatur County. Thirteen roads were closed throughout the county.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Eastern Poinsett County. One home in Trumann had water up to the doorstep. Two homes in Tyronza had water coming in the front door.
Heavy rainfall produced flash flooding in Crockett County. Six inches of water covered  Highway 152 and other roads throughout the county.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Northwest Panola County. Minor flooding occurred at a single story apartment complex in Crenshaw. Macedonia Road north of Barnacre Road was closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain produced areal flooding across much of Hardeman County. Thirty-seven roads were flooded at the high point of the event. A couple of roads were washed out including Murphy Lane, Newton Lane and Peavine Road. Some residents of Murphy Lane were stranded for several hours.
Heavy rain produced areal flooding across parts of Chester County. Several roads were closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain produced areal flooding over parts of Madison County. Christmasville Road was flooded.
Half of an inch of freezing rain and sleet fell west of Marianna.

Straight line winds knocked numerous limbs down in Hoxie. One power pole was also pushed partway over. In addition, a small metal building was destroyed and gutters were torn from a house.

Straight line winds downed power lines and power poles blocking Highway 14 west of Harrisburg.  Power lines were also knocked down a couple miles northwest of Greenfield. Some roofs were also damaged.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines west of Jonesboro.
Straight line winds knocked down a few large trees in the southeast corner of Cross County.
Straight line winds damaged a couple farm buildings and overturned two irrigation pivots.
Strong winds ahead of a cold front knocked down several trees near Paris.
Straight line winds blew the siding off numerous homes in Caruthersville.
Straight line winds broke a telephone pole in half nearly halfway up the pole at the intersection of Highway 77 and James Mill Road. Several power lines were knocked down.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Oak Grove Heights.

Straight line winds knocked down several large trees in the University of Memphis area. A very large business sign was knocked over on Germantown Parkway in Cordova. The ASOS at Memphis International Airport reported a gust of 61 mph.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in and around Tunica.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees damaging two homes and one car.

Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a house damaging the roof.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Panola County. One home had minor damage near Sardis.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across parts of Memphis. The Poplar Avenue and International Place intersection was flooded in East Memphis. Airways Road and Swinnea Road near Memphis International were flooded. Vehicles were stuck in deep water near Walnut Grove Road and Interstate 240 in East Memphis. Water was as deep as the windows of a stalled car at Timber Creek Drive and Walnut Bend Road in Cordova.
Strong winds ahead of a cold front knocked down power lines resulting in numerous brush fires across McNairy County.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Horn Lake and Walls. Ten to fifteen homes near the  Wills Way Circle and Highway 301 area were damaged due to flooding.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a house near Highway 4 and Camille Street in Senatobia. Several trees were knocked down on Clanton Road near the Barr community.
Straight line winds knocked down two trees on Lake Shore Drive southeast of Holly Springs.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in parts of Tipton County. Brighton-Clopton Road was flooded near Brighton. A few homes on Hall Road were flooded with up to one foot of water. Walnut Grove Road and Gay Road were flooded near Burlison.
Strong winds ahead of an approaching cold front knocked down trees on power lines starting a fire in the woods near Dorsey and a barn fire in East Fulton.
A quarter of an inch of ice fell across the county.
A quarter of an inch of ice fell across the county.

Straight line winds of 70 to 80 mph caused widespread damage across Southern Henderson County. Areas of enhanced damage was caused by thunderstorm winds estimated up to 110 mph. About 250 homes were damaged and several of them were destroyed. Numerous other structures were damaged. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Three injuries were reported including one person that broke his hip.
Straight line winds of 70 to 80 mph damaged 12 structures in Hardeman County including three homes and nine businesses including a lumber yard in Toone.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees across Oxford.

Straight line winds of 70 to 80 mph knocked down numerous trees and power lines on Rose Creek Road and Sulphur Springs Road in Western McNairy County. Large numbers of pine trees were pushed over or uprooted in Bethel Springs. A few of the trees were snapped and many power lines were knocked down.  An estimated 100 structures were damaged in McNairy County with the heaviest damage in Bethel Springs area.  A couple of vehicles were crushed by fallen trees in Bethel Springs.

Straight line winds damaged about 100 homes across Chester County. A 33 foot long recreational vehicle was tossed into the family swimming pool and a 16 foot trailer was wrapped upside down around some trees about 200 yards away. The heaviest damage was in the northeast part of the county. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down blocking several roads. A large barn was completely destroyed in the Jacks Creek area. Four people suffered minor injuries.
Straight line winds blew a loft off a barn north of Parsons. Three other out buildings were damaged or nearly destroyed.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees in the city of Pontotoc. Five homes suffered structural damage from fallen trees.
Straight line winds caused extensive structural damage to a few businesses on McCullough Boulevard in Tupelo. One shop had the entire front torn off.
Straight line winds blew a roof off a house in Lynn. Several trees were uprooted in the area as well.
Straight line winds blew several trees down along Highway 67 between Alicia and Minturn. A barn was also damaged near Minturn.

A weak tornado touched down a couple miles south of Greenwood Springs on Grubb Springs Road where a few large tree branches were broken and a few shingles were torn off a house. The tornado tracked northeast uprooting numerous trees and damaging a couple of barns and outbuildings along Easter Valley Road. Trees were then uprooted along Wolf Road. The tornado then damaged the roofs of three houses and uprooted more trees along Pleasant Hills Road before crossing the state line into Alabama.
A woman was struck by lightning while lifting the garage door of a storage unit and suffered a minor injury to her right arm.
Snow accumulations ranged from one to two inches across the county.
An inch of snow fell across the county.

Nickel size hail covered the ground.
Quarter size hail fell southeast of Nettleton.
Water covered the roadway at a low water crossing on Highway 219 and Rosser Circle Road, northeast of Huntingdon.

Several low water crossings became flooded across portions of Henderson County. The low water crossings included the Shady Hill Road, Wake Forrest Road, Nealis Woods Road, Taylor Road, Rock Hill Road, Rock Milam Road, Poplar Springs-Bargerton Road, Juno-Bargerton Road, and Old Exchange Road.

Several low water crossings became flooded across Decatur County with four to five inches of water. The low water crossings included the following roads: Bible Hill Road, Hog Creek Road, Concord Road, and Martin Landing Road.
Straight line winds uprooted trees near Oakland.

Straight line winds knocked down trees between Myrtle and Ingomar. Several homes sustained shingle damage. A pine tree fell on a house west of New Albany. A church was also damaged in Ingomar. Power lines were also knocked down in the area.

Straight line winds knocked several trees and power lines down between Saltillo and Tupelo. One barn was damaged near Saltillo. Several structures in Tupelo sustained minor damage. A tractor trailer was blown over as well. A tree also fell onto a house near Baldwyn.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines between New Houlka and Houston.
Half dollar size hail fell north of Houston.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 365 near Holts Spur.
Dime to quarter size hail fell near Amory.
Straight line winds knocked down large trees between Aberdeen and Greenwood Springs.
Straight line winds knocked down large trees in Amory.
Ping pong size hail fell near the Monroe and Lowndes county line.
Straight line winds uprooted pine trees east of Fulton. One pine tree fell on a house causing damage. A tin roof was blown off a barn as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across much of Calhoun County.
Heavy rain flooded numerous streets in Ripley. Many of the streets had 12-24 inches of standing or flowing water covering them.
Strong winds blew a roof off of a RV storage shed in Clarkton.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across parts of Jackson. There was flooding along portions of Christmasville Road and at the corner of Skyline Drive and Summar Drive near the Jackson-Madison County General Hospital.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Brighton. Old Highway 51 was covered with eight to ten inches of water near the Brighton Elementary School. Other roads in Tipton County also were covered by several inches of water.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Jackson making A Street and North Kentucky Street impassable.
Nickel size hail at Highway 51 near Gates.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Milan. The parking lots of a couple of businesses were flooded in the city center.
Half dollar size hail fell near Jonestown.
Quarter size hail fell on Highway 76 in Dancyville.
Golf ball size hail fell just east of downtown Henderson.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Decatur County. Multiple places on Perryville Road west of McKenzie Road were impassable due to flooding.
Straight line winds uprooted a large tree on to a nearby house causing shingle damage.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Crockett County. Many roads including some sate highways were flooded with up to two feet of water.

A tornado briefly touched down southeast of Pope. Two houses sustained roof damage. A maintenance shop was destroyed and two other outbuildings sustained roof damage. An RV and a flat bed truck was overturned. Several trees were damaged along the damage path as well.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a house near Pope causing minor damage.
Three horses were struck by lightning and killed.
Straight line winds of 60 mph moved through the region between Jonesboro and Caraway. A machine shed sustained major damage near Caraway. Numerous tree limbs were knocked down in the area as well.
Straight line winds tore off half of a barn roof and produced minor shingle damage to a couple of homes near Burlison. A tree was also knocked down in the area.
Straight line winds blew down a frame-only construction project on Post Road in Jonesboro.
Penny size hail fell about 12 miles southeast of Booneville.
Quarter size hail fell about 3 miles northeast of Trumann.
Straight line winds were measured at 60 mph in Malden. Scattered tree limbs and power lines were knocked down. Some fell on a few houses and vehicles.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Horn Lake and Southaven. A rain gauge at a spotter's home measured 4.29 inches over a period of 4 hours. Over 100 homes and businesses were affected by the flooding. Some of the homes in the Desoto Village subdivision had up to two feet of water in them. Along Goodman Road near Malone, homes and businesses had up to three feet of water standing in them. Many roads and intersections were closed due to the flooding including Highway 51 just south of State Line Road. Local proclamations of disasters were made to the governor as a result of the flooding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding over much of Shelby County. Memphis International Airport received 4.8 inches of rain over a span of a couple of hours. Interstate 55 near 3rd Street near Downtown Memphis was closed as a result of the flooding. Flooding was also reported near Macon Road and Houston Levee Road in Cordova, Brunswick Road and Old Brownsville Road in Northern Shelby County. Two people were trapped in a flooded car at Lamar and East Shelby Drive.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding over portions of Northwest Fayette County. The intersection of Hwy 196 and Orr Road was flooded as a result.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Collierville-Arlington Road and Raleigh-Lagrange Road, north of Collierville.
Straight line winds of 67 mph were measured just north of Charleston. Several trees were knocked down in the area.
Quarter size hail fell just north of Coffeeville.
Straight line winds estimated at 60 mph occurred between Oxford and Tula. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in the region. At least six streets were blocked by fallen trees in Oxford.

Straight line winds knocked numerous trees and power lines down across Panola County. At least four homes were damaged from fallen trees. Fifteen roads were closed due to fallen trees. Numerous power outages occured as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Batesville. Six businesses reported anywhere from six inches to a foot of standing water in them.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Pontotoc. Several streets were covered with water as a result.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across much of northern and western Carroll County. About 20 roads were closed due to flooding. A couple of homes on Williams Street and Northwood Drive in Huntingdon were evacuated due to flooding.

Straight line winds knocked down a tall light pole and fence at the Lafayette County High School football field.  Several trees and power lines were knocked down across Oxford causing the closure of four roads including Highway 6 for a brief time.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and a few power poles in Ravenden. One person was injured by a falling tree.

A swath of sporadic straight line wind damage stretched across Madison County. The damage started south of Bemis continued into Jackson then extended north roughly between Old Medina Road and Christmasville Road to the Gibson County line. Numerous trees were knocked down with the most intense damage north of North Parkway in Jackson. A large tree fell on a house in Bemis causing extensive damage. Another large tree fell and destroyed a barber shop in Bemis. Numerous trees were knocked down on Hickory Hollow Drive east of the center of Jackson where one tree fell and damaged a porch of a home. A middle school roof in Jackson was damaged. A tree damaged a home in North Jackson. A metal barn and outbuilding on Christmasville road were destroyed.
Straight line winds knocked down a several trees from Medina to Milan. A few trees were knocked down on Stinson Road west of Milan.
Quarter size hail fell from Jackson to the Gibson County line.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines around Martin. One tree fell on a car.

Approximately five inches of rain fell across northern and western Poinsett County resulting in flash flooding. A few homes and several county roads were flooded. Many of the roads that were flooded were badly damaged and had to be repaired.

Approximately seven inches of rain produced flash flooding across Northern Cross County. Highways 42 and 193 and multiple county roads were flooded near Hickory Ridge.  One home suffered minor flood damage near Hickory Ridge. The CO-OP was completely flooded. Highways 1 and 42 were flooded near Cherry Valley. A culvert on an unnamed county road was washed out leaving four families stranded. One home had minor flood damage near Cherry Valley.
Straight line winds knocked down a power pole on Highway 1 in Cherry Valley and several trees along Highway 163.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding east of Jonesboro where the east end of County Road 912 was closed.

The tornado touched down on Mount Lebanon Road and tracked east destroying two homes. The wind moved cars and trucks a significant amount. There was also damage to grain bins and trees were knocked down. A shop was destroyed.
A weak tornado crossed from Monroe County into St. Francis County. A few trees and power lines were knocked down. Two tractor trailers were blown off Interstate 40 before the tornado lifted.
Straight line winds produced damaged to a couple of homes northwest of Covington.  The homes had roof and some structural damage.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding around Walnut Ridge. Up to a foot of water covered many secondary roads in the vicinity of Walnut Ridge.

Straight line winds resulted in damage within the city limits of Jonesboro. Windows on a church van were blown out along North Main Street. A restaurant along East Word Avenue had the roof ripped off from the building. Trees were knocked down along North Third Street. The highway department reported lots of debris in the roadways in the vicinity of the area.
Heavy rain produced a drainage canal to rise and begin flooding the area near Margaret Street in Piggott. Water nearly flooded a few homes. Margaret Street was closed as a result.
Heavy rain occurred in Oak Grove Heights. As a result, a drainage ditch flooded the Dollar General parking lot with six to eight inches of water.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down along with numerous 3-4 inch limbs in Downtown Tupelo.

Straight line winds snapped power poles northwest and southeast of Waldenburg. In the town of Waldenburg, one power line plus several billboard and business signs were knocked down. The roof off of several buildings (warehouse style) at the Farmer's Supply fertilizer plant were ripped off.
Straight line winds broke up a large pivot irrigation system near mile marker 17 on Interstate 55 near Jericho. In Jericho, a big oak tree fell on a SUV.
Quarter size hail fell along Interstate 55 near Jericho and in the town of Jericho itself.
Golf ball size hail fell northeast of Marion.

Straight line winds knocked 28 power poles down on Casino Strip Resort Boulevard near Robinsonville. In addition, one car was blown in a ditch. Three additional cars had windows blown out due to the wind. An irrigation pivot system was turned over. One building also sustained roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked several trees down along County Road 231, northwest of Iuka.

A slow moving thunderstorm produced very heavy rain causing flash flooding in South Fulton. The rain caused Harris Creek to rise rapidly and it flooded many streets and a few homes. Water rescues occurred as a result with water as high as knee to waist deep in a few locations.

Straight line winds knocked four power poles down near the intersection of Macon Road and Berryhill Road. Several trees and fences were also knocked down in the area. Tree branches were knocked down as far west as the intersection of Germantown Road and Macon Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Craighead County. Several roads in the Jonesboro area were flooded including Phillips Drive and Washington Avenue.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across much of Southern Cross County. Some roads were flooded mainly south of Wynne.
Numerous reports of quarter size hail in the Valley View and Lawson Road areas.
Quarter size hail fell near Trumann.
Straight line winds knocked down six power poles and tore the roof off a Co-Op building in Waldenburg.
Three teenagers were struck by lightning on Oxford Street in West Memphis. All three were injured.
A lightning strike caused a fire at an apartment complex on West Harrison Street in West Memphis. The fire caused extensive damage.
Straight line winds knocked a large tree on to a house on East Dempster Avenue in Memphis.
Quarter size hail fell near Craft Road in Olive Branch.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees in Oxford. A tree was uprooted on the University of Mississippi campus and a tree was knocked on to a house on Douglas Street.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees along County Road 917 near Armorel. A shed was also destroyed. Wood fences were blown down at six to eight homes in the area.
The ASOS at the Blytheville airport measured a sustained wind of 55 mph and a gust of 77 mph.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a truck in the Raleigh area.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of large trees and blocked Macon Road about one mile east of Highway 196.
Quarter size hail fell in southern St. Francis County near the Lee County line.

The tornado touched down just northeast of Exit 35 on Interstate 40 near Belmont. A large barn and several outbuildings were destroyed. The tornado tracked northeast producing damage to a rural church by pushing it 15 feet from its foundation. Numerous trees were snapped and uprooted along the damage path. The tornado lifted in a wooded area just to the north of Old 59 Drive. One minor injury occurred at a residence just before the tornado lifted.
Three inches of rain fell in a span of 3 hours which caused a creek outside of Pollard to flood its banks. The water flooded a house as a result.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Northern Henderson County. Numerous roads were flooded as a result including Palmer Road, Holmes Road, Rock Milam Road, Spencer Creek Road and Hamlett Road. One water rescue occurred as a result of the flooding.
Straight line winds knocked a roof off a small medical clinic in Sumner. As a result, rain flooded in the inside of the building.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Olive Branch. Several streets were flooded with six inches or more of water.
Penny size hail fell near Reelfoot Lake.
Penny size hail fell southeast of Atoka.
Straight line winds blew several large trees down, southeast of Amory.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down in Tunica.

Straight line winds blew an eighteen wheeler over in Humboldt. In addition, a small plane was blown over at the Humboldt Municipal Airport.  A power pole was snapped near the Humboldt city limits and a tree was blown down on Windy City Road.
Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down in Brownsville. Numerous roads were blocked with debris.
Straight line winds knocked large trees and power lines down in Covington.
Straight line winds knocked large trees down on Raleigh-LaGrange Road.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across much of the northern half of Shelby County as a severe thunderstorm merged with another thunderstorm. Bartlett was particularly hit hard as up to 3 feet of water covered portions of Stage Road. Vehicles were stuck in water. Water flooded homes up to a foot along Richfield Road, Spring Valley Road, and Skylight Drive. Further west, the intersection of Walnut Grove Road and Union Avenue was flooded with up to 4 feet of water in Midtown Memphis. In addition, the intersection of Macon Road and Jackson Avenue in North Memphis was flooded.
Straight line winds knocked a large tree on a car in Crawfordsville. In addition, a tree fell down on Highway 64 near Ebony.
Straight line winds knocked two trees down on a power line in Earle.
Straight line winds knocked numerous trees down in Stantonville. Some trees fell on houses and vehicles.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Senatobia. Numerous streets were impassable with over six inches of water covering them including Robertson Street, Cox Street, Hurd Street, and several others.
Biggers received 3.5 to 3.75 inches of rain which produced flash flooding. Numerous streets were flooded and impassable as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down two large trees in Cooter. A car and a fence were damaged.
Straight line winds knocked a tree into a power line breaking six power poles in Bells.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Martin. The intersection of Hamm Road and Hyndsver Road was flooded.
Several inches of rain produced flash flooding in South Fulton. Several residences had to be evacuated due to rising water.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and overturned a tractor trailer at the Belden exit of U.S. Highway 78.
Straight line winds knocked down a few road signs along with some large tree limbs just west of Mantachie.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees along the county road between Smithville and Hatley.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree on Carnation Street and a power line between Main Street and Jefferson Street.
Very heavy rain produced flash flooding across Tupelo and Verona. Numerous streets were flooded. Cars were flooded in a business parking lot in South Tupelo.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Booneville. The parking lot of a car dealership was flooded and 5th Street was closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across portions of Decatur County. Many low water crossings were flooded including ones on Concord Road, Bible Hill Road, and Hog Creek Road. Maxwell Street in Parsons was also flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Jacks Creek. A couple of roads had six to seven inches of water covering them.
Nickel size hail was reported near the intersection of Highway 100 and Highway 22, southwest of Reagan.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in the Bartlett area.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred in Coahoma County.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred across Tunica County.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred across Yalobusha County.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred across Panola County.

Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred across Tallahatchie County.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred in Phillips County.
Severe (D2) drought conditions occurred across Lee County.
A tornado briefly touched down in an open field just west of the Obion River Bridge on Highway 51. No damage occurred.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines in South Fulton.

A tornado touched down just southwest of the business district in Caraway and moved northeast. The tornado lifted near the far northeastern edge of town. Significant structural damage occurred as a result of the tornado. Damage occurred to many roofs of homes, businesses, churches and a convenience store. Several dozens of trees were uprooted as well.
Straight line winds produced some minor damage to a farm shop building and a few grain bins in Milligan Ridge. Power lines were knocked down as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees between Fowlkes and Roellen. HIghway 210 in Fowlkes and Don Hurley Road near Roellen were blocked as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines between Dyer and Rutherford.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees just south of Paris.
A tornado briefly touched down in a field northeast of Marion. The tornado then moved northeast onto the Mississippi River before lifting. No damage was reported.

A quarter of an inch of ice fell across the far northwest tip of Shelby County near Shelby Forest. The rest of the county received around a tenth of an inch of ice as rain did not change over until the morning hours of December 6th.
A combination of a quarter of an inch of ice and around a half an inch of sleet fell across Haywood County.
A combination of a quarter of an inch of ice and around a half an inch of sleet fell across Crockett County.

Over seven inches of rain produced flash flooding across Poinsett County. Water entered four homes in Trumann. Several streets in Trumann were flooded including Primrose Lane. Highway 69 at Highway 163 in Northern Poinsett County and MB Lane off Highway 118 near Marked Tree were closed due to wash outs. Ditches throughout the county were filled to capacity.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Piggott. The Piggott Municipal Airport was closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Marianna. Highway 79 about five miles west of Marianna was flooded.
Over four inches of rain produced flash flooding across Obion County. Widespread street flooding occurred in Union City and Highway 183 was flooded in Eastern Obion County.
Heavy rain produced widespread street flooding across Tipton County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in West Memphis. Gibson and Barton Avenues were covered by a foot of water.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Northern Poinsett County. Senteney Road was flooded for nearly a mile long stretch.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding northeast of Jonesboro. Two and a half feet of water covered Prospect Road and Britney Lane.  Several cars were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in St. Francis County. Highway 261 near Palestine was flooded. Dawson and Washington Roads were flooded in Forrest City.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Crump. Riverside Drive was closed due to flooding.
A combination of a quarter inch of ice, between one and a half to two inches of sleet, and one to three inches of snow fell across Dunklin County.
A combination of a quarter inch of ice, between one and a half to two inches of sleet, and up to an inch of snow fell across Pemiscot County.

The combination of around a tenth of an inch of ice and a trace of sleet fell across Coahoma County.

A tornado touched down six miles west-southwest of Hughes and traveled north-northeast. Three mobile homes were destroyed near Hughes. Roof damage occurred to two homes and a barn was damaged. A number of irrigation pivots were overturned. Near the community of Wildwood a metal shed was destroyed. Power lines were also damaged along the path. The tornado lifted one mile northwest of Tarsus. The peak winds were estimated at 130 mph.
Straight line winds knocked over a tractor trailer near mile marker 276 on Interstate 40 west of West Memphis.
Straight line winds knocked down utility poles along West Liberty Avenue in Covington.

A tornado touched down in Rena Lara and tracked northeast. There was major damage to a mobile home where the fatality occurred. Two large garage sheds were completely destroyed. Two football light poles were bent and destroyed at the Cohoma County High School. There was roof and window damage to the elementary school on Bobo-Sharard Road. Several homes had minor roof damage and four homes had significant roof damage on County Road 332. Several trees were uprooted or snapped off along the path of the tornado. The tornado lifted just west of Clarksdale. The peak winds were estimated at 120 mph.
Straight line winds caused widespread damage across Coahoma county. Many homes had minor damage with several receiving major damage. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down as well.

A tornado touched down on Flea Harbor Road in Southern Tunica County and traveled northeast. A church was pushed off its foundation by 10 feet or more. Multiple homes were damaged on Flea Harbor Road. A trailer was rolled and debris was thrown at least a mile from home. Power lines were snapped with large power lines snapped on Six Mile Lake Road. Peak winds were estimated at 90 to 100 mph.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Redmond Road.
Straight line winds knocked down a shed and trees along Tibbs Road in Tunica County.

A tornado touched down in Northern Panola County near the intersection of Highway 310 and Pleasant Grove Road causing minor roof damage to a home. The tornado uprooted and snapped off trees in Panola County and then tracked northeast into Tate County. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.

A tornado tracked northeast from Panola County and caused roof damage at four homes near Hammond Hill Road. A two story home received damage when a covered porch was lifted and deposited on to the roof of the garage. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across Northwest Panola County. Major building damage occurred on Highway 315W near the Panola and Quitman County line. There was farm damage near the intersection of Landfill and Springhill Roads where a crop duster was flipped. A tree was knocked on to a house north of Highway 310 and Bishop Road. Trees were knocked down on several roads and multiple power lines were downed. There were two vehicle accidents with injuries due to fallen trees.

Straight line winds caused widespread damage across parts of Tate County especially Senatobia. Trees and power lines were knocked down in the city. Hundreds of homes had mainly shingle damage. Several mobile homes and businesses had major damage. A few agricultural buildings also had major damage. A car was blown off the roadway along Interstate 55 at Yellow Dog Road resulting in two injuries.
Quarter size hail fell at Shelby Drive and Forest Hill Irene Road.
Straight line winds knocked a tree on to a home in Munford.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines. Some trees blocked roadways.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in and south of Oxford.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Marshall County. Seven homes and three mobile homes suffered minor damage. Two businesses had minor damaged. One injury was reported.
Straight line winds caused roof damage to several homes in the Sledge area. Four homes were uninhabitable. One minor injury occurred when a Deputy Sheriff hit a downed tree caused by the storm.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees across Tishomingo County. One business was destroyed and three transformers were blown.

Heavy rain produced flashing flooding across Shelby County. Several roads were flooded including Shelby Oaks Drive, Summer Avenue, Brownsville Road and the intersection of Millbranch Road and Timothy Road where the water was deep enough to prevent cars from moving through. Other roads were also flooded.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in parts of Jackson. Ashport Road flooded near the Highway 45 Bypass and Old Medina Road at Cooper Anderson Road was closed. Several other roads were flooded along with many yards.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding around Greenfield. Several roads were flooded.
Heavy rain resulting in flash flooding in Ripley. A road near Highway 15 was flooded.
Heavy rain cause moderate to heavy street flooding across Southern DeSoto County.
Heavy rain cause moderate street flooding in Medina.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Henry County. Several roads were closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding throughout Henderson County. Over a dozen roads were closed throughout the county.
A tornado briefly touched down near Hayti and damaged a roof to a building. Maximum winds were estimated at 90 mph.

A tornado touched down near Deering and overturned a single wide trailer on to a truck and tree. There was damage to several homes including tree and roof damage. A carport and shed were also damaged. Maximum winds were estimated at 90 mph.
Golfball size hail fell in the Hornersville area.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and caused minor roof damage near Dundee. A greenhouse was turned over.
Straight line winds overturned a tractor trailer near Interstate 69 west of Hernando.
Straight line winds knocked down some trees in Pontotoc.

Straight line winds knocked trees down near Briar Ridge Road in Tupelo and ripped the shingles off a roof in Guntown. A trampoline was wrapped around a tree and carport was damaged in Guntown as well. A home was damaged in Belden.
Quarter size hail was reported near Charleston Boulevard in Tupelo.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 6 between Nettleton and Bigbee.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees and ripped shingles off a roof near Dennis. One tree fell on a truck near Highway 25 and Old Highway 25 on the south end of Dennis. Trees were also knocked down in the northern part of Belmont and near Paden. One minor injury was reported. Minor structure damage to homes was also reported. Trees were also knocked down in Tishomingo State Park. One tree fell and caused minor damage to a cabin. More trees were toppled along Natchez Trace Parkway from just north of the intersection of Highway 4 to Highway 30.

Straight line winds caused structural damage to building and knocked down trees along Van Buren Road near Fulton. A spotter measured a 58 mph wind gust in rural Eastern Itawamba County north of Tremont.

Straight line winds heavily damaged a medium sized metal out building at the end of County Road 120 near Highway 15 north of Walnut.
Straight line winds heavily damaged a house in Cottonwood point. Power lines and trees were also knocked down in the area.
Straight line winds damaged a carport and knocked down two large trees in the Moon Lake area.
