Heavy rain resulted in water over bridges on Old Jacks Creek Road. Water also covered Old Finger Road south of Henderson.

Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines along Section 7 Road. A mobile home was blown off its foundation and several homes had roof damage. Two homes had major damage. Trees and power lines were also knocked down on Curtis Road and Curtis-Locke Station Road.
Straight line winds destroyed a mobile home off of Stribling Road near Farrell. The homeowner was injured when he was thrown from the mobile home. He later died from his injuries.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Clarksdale and the rest of Coahoma County. Some minor damage also occurred to a few buildings.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Olive Branch. Trees were blocking the intersection of Pleasant Hill Road and Getwell Road.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near Crenshaw. A canopy was blown off a building as well as a radio antenna.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees, power lines, and several large limbs in Como.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near Ecru. Thirteen homes sustained minor damage, mainly roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Calhoun City.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Chickasaw County. Three homes in Okolona sustained roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked a tree down onto a car near Jumpertown.
Straight line winds produced minor damage to fifteen homes in the Woodland Hills Subdivision near Guntown. Some construction equipment was also blown around.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Bigbee and Aberdeen. Trees blocked the intersection of Highway 371 and Old Highway 6 as well as Highway 8 and Dan Taylor Road.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in the southern parts of Somerville.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees on power lines and one barn was destroyed.
Straight line winds knocked a tree down through a house near Decaturville. Five barns were completely destroyed as well.
Nickel size hail fell from Calhoun City to Vardaman.
Golf ball size hail fell in Lambert and Marks.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree and power line at Riverside Drive in Marks.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of McIngvale Road and Middle Buster Road in Hernando.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding across parts of Randolph County. Highway 62 and others roads west of Pocahontas were flooded. Several streets were impassable in Maynard. Many county roads were also flooded north of Imboden.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding between Imboden and Black Rock. Highway 63 was flooded.
Straight line winds destroyed a large shop building north of Cardwell.

Very heavy rain fell across Northern Dunklin County. 8.50 inches of rain was recorded. Many roads were flooded across Northern Dunklin County especially in the communities of Campbell and Malden. Several homes and businesses were flooded in Malden. An apartment complex in Campbell was flooded with water up to four feet deep. Fifteen residents were rescued from the complex. Several homes were flooded in Campbell as well resulting in additional water rescues.

Several highway were flooded across Clay County. Heavy rain flooded Highway 62 in Northeast Arkansas. The highway was closed at the Missouri State line. Highway 119, Highway 90, Highway 49 and Highway 139 were also flooded.
A weak tornado touched down in Northeast Shelby County causing roof damage to a few homes along Brunswick Road. Trees were also knocked down.
Heavy rain flooded several roadways in the Walnut Ridge area. Several county roads were washed out.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and large tree limbs across Northern Tunica County resulting in several power outages.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and ripped siding off a structure.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the Brighton area. Several roads were underwater and impassable.
Penny to nickel size hail fell near Troy.
Quarter size hail fell north of Rector.
Straight line winds knocked down a large tree onto a house in Maury City. A barn was also damaged in the area.

Straight line winds knocked a large limb into a window of a house in Tunica. In addition, Several trees were knocked down in the area. One tree landed on three vehicles. Three large metal sheds were blown over as well. The Tunica AWOS measured a gust of 50 knots at the time of the storm.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across Panola County. A few trees fell onto houses producing damage.

A tornado touched down near the Pontotoc County line west of Tupelo. The tornado strengthened as it moved into Tupelo reaching a peak intensity along Clayton Avenue and Country Club Road and in the commercial area along North Gloster from Hillcrest Drive to North Green Street. The Joyner Elementary School and Maintenance Shop suffered major damage. Maximum winds were estimated at 150 mph. A woman was killed when her vehicle hydroplaned and hit a tree during the storm. The tornado continued northeast and caused significant damage near Elvis Presley Lake including toppling a 400 foot communication tower. 84 homes were destroyed in Lee County while 169 homes suffered major damage. 351 other homes had minor damage. Six mobile homes were destroyed. Nine mobile homes had major damage while 6 others had minor damage. 17 businesses were destroyed while 9 suffered major damage. The tornado then tracked into Itawamba County.

A tornado moved from Lee County into Northwest Itawamba County. The tornado tracked across rural parts of Itawamba County before moving into Prentiss County. Ten homes were destroyed in Itawamba County while 29 homes suffered major damage. 107 other homes had minor damage. 14 mobile homes were destroyed and 17 had major damage. 30 other mobile homes suffered minor damage.
The tornado tracked from Itawamba County into Prentiss County and quickly lifted in a rural area resulting in minimal additional damage.

A tornado touched down west of Union City and tracked northeast damaging 16 structures. Many structures had roofs removed and several barns destroyed. A minor injury was to an occupant of one of the homes who was sent to the hospital and released. The other occupant of the house was in the garage and saw the tornado coming. The suction was so strong he could not enter the house until part of the roof was blown off. There was major damage to large machine sheds. The tornado moved a 700 pound weight about 15 feet and threw a 40 pound jack about 50 yards. A steel trailer was bent.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across parts of De Soto County. A few roads were closed for a short period of time.
Straight line winds overturned a mobile home near Kirby Road and Hambrick Road. Twelve power poles were snapped in Robinsonville near the Casino Strip.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Camden and surrounding areas of Benton County.

Three to four inches of rain fell across Benton County, producing widespread flash flooding. Pineview Road was completely washed out. The bridge on Kelly Road was covered with two feet of water while a culvert was washed out on Rowland Road.
Three to four inches of rain fell across Weakley County. As a result, Concord Road near Latham was flooded with eighteen inches of water.

Three to four inches of rain fell across Carroll County. As a result, numerous roads and streets were flooded in Huntingdon. A few people were stranded in cars. Elsewhere in Carroll County, culverts and roads were washed out.

Straight line winds produced widespread wind damage across Lawrence County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down with a few blocking roads. One tree fell on vehicle, killing the driver, after the motorist decided to pull over due to the blinding rain. Three other occupants sustained injuries. A few trees fell onto homes producing damage. Roof damage occurred to a few other homes. At least two car accidents occurred during the storm.

Straight line winds produced widespread wind damage across Craighead County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Some trees fell onto vehicles, homes and across roads producing damage. One tree fell onto a home in Jonesboro killing the occupant. Shingles were also blown off of roofs. Numerous buildings in Jonesboro sustained roof damage. Damage also occurred to the tower of the courthouse. One plane sustained damage at the Jonesboro airport. A train with 38 cars derailed in Otwell due to the winds.

Straight line winds produced widespread wind damage across Poinsett County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. A few trees fell onto homes producing damage. A roof was blown off a building in LePanto. The King Transportation building was completely destroyed in Trumann. A couple of tractor-trailers turned over on Highway 63 and Hwy 49 as a result of the wind.

Straight line winds produced widespread damage in Mississippi County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Three tractor-trailers and one camper overturned on Interstate 55 near Osceola. Construction barrels were also blown around on the interstate.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Southern Tipton County including the areas near Brighton and Covington. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. A roof was blown off a warehouse near Brighton. Several roofs collapsed in Covington and a few of the city square buildings had extensive roof damage.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees and power lines from Millington to the Eads-Collierville area.
Straight line winds knocked trees down near Dyer and Trenton in Gibson County.
After receiving three to four inches in the morning, Trenton received another one to two inches during the afternoon which caused street flooding.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near Walnut.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Corinth.
Straight line winds blew tin off a barn northeast of Lexington. In addition, a tree was knocked down onto a house north of Lexington.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Horn Lake. As a result, water covered the intersection of Twin Lakes Road and Nail Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Falkner. Several roads were flooded as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Germantown. The intersection of Wolf River Boulevard and Farmington Avenue was covered with water as a result.
A coop observer reported 2.22 inches of rain in less than an hour in Bemis. As a result, several streets were flooded including Kentucky Street, D Street and North Missouri Street.

A tornado crossed over the Mississippi River from New Madrid County, Missouri and tracked through Lake County into Obion County. Damage across Lake County consisted of mainly tree damage with clear cutting and snapping of trees near the levee near the river towards Reelfoot Lake.

A tornado crossed into Obion County from Lake County, Tennessee and continued southeast. The tornado caused roof damage to ten homes especially along Possum Trot Road and Treece Road. Significant tree damage also occurred along the path. The tornado lifted near the intersection of Shawtown Road and Davis Road, northwest of Troy.
Straight line winds knocked down trees west of Troy. Brown's Meat Market and Deer Processing Plant also sustained extensive damage.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Union City.
Baseball size hail fell north of Samburg.
Golf ball size hail fell just south of Union City.
Quarter to half Dollar size hail fell in Paragould.
Quarter size hail fell south of Stanford.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Chester County. One tree fell onto a house in Glendale. A semi truck was also blown off the road on Willis Road.
Numerous trees were knocked down near Gardner.
Golf ball size hail fell south of Gleason.
Straight line winds destroyed two camper trailers and a boat near Manila.
Straight line winds blew a roof off a mobile home near Keiser. Power lines were also knocked down near Highways 181 and 239.
Straight line winds knocked down a few power lines and blew a secondary roof off of a mobile home near Blytheville.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell from the Tennessee/Mississippi State line to Downtown Corinth.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines across Weakley County. Although, Gleason was hit the hardest.

Straight line winds destroyed two sheds and a part of another shop east of Friendship. Minor roof and siding damage occurred to a couple of homes as well. Several trees were also knocked down in the area as well.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Scarborough Loop, south of Humboldt.

Straight line winds knocked down several large trees in the southern part of Paragould. A very large tree fell on a car near Highway 49 in Paragould about two miles south of Highway 412. Large trees were knocked down city wide.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Paragould. As a result Jones Road was impassable due to deep water.

Straight line winds knocked down multiple trees and power lines in Hickory Ridge. A few cars and structures were damaged by falling trees and a roof was blown off a commercial business in Hickory Ridge. Multiple power poles were knocked down on Highway 1 north of Cherry Valley.
A trained spotter measured a 71 mph gust in Marked Tree. Two high profile vehicles were overturned on Highway 63 near Marked Tree.
Ping pong ball to golf ball size hail fell from Thaxton to Pontotoc. The large hail damaged a patrol car west of Pontotoc.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple trees along County Road 135 north of Highway 32 west of Okolona. One home was damaged by a fallen tree.

This weak tornado uprooted and snapped off several trees along its path. Two houses suffered considerable damage from fallen trees. One person received a minor injury. In addition, near the touchdown point, several roof panels were blown off a poultry building. Peak wind was estimated at 90 to 95 mph.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across the southern part of Poinsett County.

Straight line winds knocked down and uprooted trees from North Jackson to Bemis. Power lines were also knocked down as well. Shingles were also blown off a few homes across Madison County. In addition, one tree fell onto a home on Chester Road.
Straight line winds knocked down trees between Milan and Medina.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees across portions of Lauderdale County.
Straight line winds knocked several trees and power lines down from the Tennessee State Line to Iuka.
Repeated rounds of thunderstorms produced flash flooding in Iuka. The Rain Road Underpass was flooded as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down trees from Brighton to the Shelby County line.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines along Highway 88 in Maury City. In addition, some minor roof damage occurred to a house along Highway 188. A few tin sheds also sustained damage.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Parsons.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across southern portions of Weakley County. Several roads were flooded as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Carroll County. Several county roads were flooded as a result.
Straight line winds knocked trees and power lines down in Burnsville.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines on Highway 72 in Iuka.
Heavy rains produced flash flooding across Decatur County. At one point, as many as fifteen roads were closed due to flooding. Many of them were low water crossings.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees down in the Huntingdon area.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees on Highway 100, west of Scotts Hill.
Straight line winds knocked trees down all across Hardin County.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees and large limbs between Walls and Horn Lake.
Straight line winds blew a few trees and power lines down across portions of Lafayette County.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees and power lines down across Alcorn County.
Straight line winds produced major roof damage to two homes in Pontotoc. Minor roof damage occurred to two additional homes. Trees were also knocked down in the area.
Straight line winds knocked a few trees and power poles down in Marianna.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding east of Adamsville. At least a foot of water flooded Overbrook Drive just off of Highway 64 from a nearby creek.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees on the western and northwestern side of Houston.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Horn Lake. The intersection of Twin Lakes Drive and Iroquois Drive was flooded with water up to just below the knee.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees across western sections of Lafayette County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Alcorn County. Several roads were flooded as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Tippah County. Several roads were washed out near Walnut and Ripley.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across Northern Benton County. Several roads were flooded as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on Highway 30 near Tishomingo.
A 62 mph gust measured by the Jonesboro Airport ASOS.
Straight line winds knocked down a large tree on to power lines on Highway 141 north of Jonesboro.
Nickel size hail was reported across the Jonesboro area.
Straight line winds knocked down multiple fence posts and removed shingles from a roof near Senatobia. Multiple trees were knocked down on houses and power poles near Woolfolk Road and Miracle Drive.
Quarter size hail fell near Senatobia.
Golf ball size hail fell near Highway 349, south of Potts Camp.
Golf ball size hail fell on the west side of Houston.
Straight line winds knocked power lines down along Highway 15 near Houlka.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Ingomar. One tree fell onto a mobile home injuring one occupent and damaging the home.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell near Amory.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 9 near Alpine.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines down in Thrasher.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on the west side of Burnsville.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines between Glen and Jacinto.

Heavyr rain produced flash flooding across Hardeman County. Several roads had up to 8-10 inches of water on them including Taylor Road in Middleton, Young Road in Bolivar, Old Toone Road, and Front Road in Toone.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding southwest of Wildersville. As a result, Highway 104 and nearby roads were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near Highway 302 and Alexander Road. A awning at a church near Highland Street and Pigeon Roost Road was completely destroyed.

Very heavy rain fell across the southern half of Shelby County. Rainfall amounts of 5 to 9 inches were reported causing widespread flash flooding. Dozens of streets were flooded across Southern Shelby County and many vehicles were trapped in water. Several people had to be rescued. Several homes and businesses were also flooded. The hardest hit area was along Nonconnah Creek where many homes and businesses from Lamar Avenue downstream to Interstate 55 experienced some degree of flooding. About 100 mobile homes were flooded in a mobile home park west of Memphis International Airport. Nonconnah Creek had a record crest at the Winchester gage of 26.64 feet and at the Farriesview gage of 34.33 feet.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Hernando. One to two feet of water covered Byhalia Road west of Malone Road. The road was closed.
Heavy rain across the southwest sections of West Memphis forced the evaculationa of some homes due to high water.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across much of St. Francis County. Over 7 inches of rain was recorded at Wheatley. Many roads were flooded across the county and homes were evacuated in Madison due to flooding along Crow Creek. Five families were evacuated from homes in the Stonebrook subdicison in Forrest City.
Lightning struck and killed a teenager as he was running to take cover from a storm. He was found underneath a tree in a church's parking lot.
Lightning struck a building at the Osceola Municipal Airport. As a result, a fire occurred which caused major damage to the building.
Two thunderstorms merged together over Trumann. As a result, the intersection of West Main Street and North Pine Avenue was covered with seven inches of water.
Quarter size hail fell in Scobey.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines in Houston. One house was damaged as well as two hangars at the airport.
Straight line winds knocked trees down in Okolona. One house sustained damage after a few tree limbs fell on the roof.
Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down in Becker.
Quarter size hail fell in Bemis.

Thunderstorms trained over McNairy County for several hours. As a result, flash flooding occurred in Selmer. At least one mobile home was surrounded by flood water trapping the resident. In addition, flooding occurred along Sulpher Springs Road where a home also became surrounded by flood waters. An unknown number of people were trapped in the home.

Thunderstorms trained over the Oakland and Somerville areas for about five hours. Rainfall was measured at 6.25 inches in Oakland. As a result, flash flooding occurred in the Northwood Estates subdivision. Black Ankle Drive was also flooded.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines all across Panola County from Batesville to southwest of Courtland. Roof damage occurred to a house and to a metal storage building along Sullivan Road.
Straight line winds knocked down several large trees in Ripley.
Straight line winds produced damage to an outbuilding in Booneville.
Straight line winds knocked several large trees and power lines down near Fulton.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees, tree limbs, and power lines near Sharon.
Straight line winds knocked down large trees and power lines on Old Medina Road in Jackson.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in and around Camden.
Straight line winds knocked down power and light poles along Parker Road and Highway 63 in Jonesboro.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines along Airways Boulevard in Jackson.
Straight line winds knocked down large tree limbs and lifted shingles off a roof in Henderson.
Straight line winds knocked a large tree onto a house on Norfolk Street in the vicinity of Interstate 240 and Person Road in Southwest Memphis.
Straight line winds snapped and uprooted trees near the railroad tracks at the intersection of Poplar Pike and Poplar Avenue in Germantown.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines all around the Bartlett area.
The ASOS at McKellar Field in Jackson measured a 62 mph wind.
Straight line winds produced some tree damage east of Somerville.
Straight line winds knocked down trees near the intersection of Highway 368 and Highway 18 in Grand Junction.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Brownsville. Several roads and underpasses were flooded as a result.
Straight line winds blew a roof off of a trailer along Rabbit Ridge Road. In addition, several trees and power lines were knocked down in around Byhalia.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees across Northern Tippah County including in the city of Walnut.
Straight line winds produced damage from northwest of Piggott to south of Rector. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. In addition, a roof turbine was blown off in Rector.

Straight line winds produced damage around the Paragould area. Two restaurant signs were knocked down onto Highway 412. Roof damage also occurred to a few homes north of the intersection of Highway 49 and Highway 412.
Straight line winds produced damage around the Jonesboro area. The ASOS at Jonesboro measured a 58 mph wind gust. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Jonesboro.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees between Maynard and Pocahontas. One tree fell onto a house damaging the roof.
Straight line winds knocked down a couple of trees in Trumann.
Straight line winds knocked a large limb down onto a shed and destroyed it near Weiner.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Henderson.
A thunderstorm sat nearly stationary over Henderson for awhile. Numerous streets became flooded and were closed. A few county roads also became impassable. A total of 1.42 inches fell in 30 minutes.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Southaven. As a result, ten inches of water covered Brookhaven Drive.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Clarksdale. As a result, several streets were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked several trees, power lines, and power poles down across Coahoma County especially from Clarksdale to Green Grove.
Showers and thunderstorms trained over Northern Dunklin County for at least 1-2 hours. Numerous county roads were impassable due to flash flooding as a result.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Halls. Highway 88 was covered with at least a foot of water.
Showers and thunderstorms trained over Madison County for a period of time. As a result, Riverside Drive was washed out southwest of Jackson.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding around Jackson. Numerous roads had at least six inches of water covering them. In addition, Clement Road had pavement washed away due to the flooding.
The ASOS at the Blytheville Airport measured a 60 mph gust as a line of thunderstorms moved through the city.

Showers and thunderstorms remained nearly stationary over Hollow Rock for over an hour. As a result, the fire station was flooded. In addition, the intersections of Highway 641 and Mill Street as well as Highway 641 and Main Street were impassable due to flooding.
Slow moving thunderstorms produced some flash flooding across Eastern Lauderdale County. Highway 209 between Gates and Halls was closed due to flash flooding as well as Highway 19 near Durhamville.

Slow moving showers and thunderstorms produced additional flash flooding across Eastern Lauderdale County a day after thunderstorms had already produced flash flooding. As a result, Highway 19 was flooded again near Durhamville. In addition, roads near the Autumn Hills community were flooded.
Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding across Western Haywood County. As a result, the intersection of Highway 19 and Old Highway 19 was closed due to flooding.

Slow moving thunderstorms produced flash flooding across North Jackson. As a result, the intersection of Ridgecrest Road and Henderson Road was closed due to flooding. In addition, a portion of East University Parkway was washed out.
A downburst blew trees and fences down throughout a neighborhood in Horn Lake. A chimney was also blown off the roof of a home.
Quarter size hail fell at the intersection of Highway 15 and Highway 76 in Pontotoc. A windshield was reported broken due to the hail.
Showers and thunderstorms trained over Trenton for a couple of hours. As a result, flash flooding occurred and South College Street had to be closed due to high water.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over Northern Carroll County for a couple of hours. As a result, flash flooding occurred in a few locations between Trezevant and Huntingdon. The intersection of Highway 190 and Oak Grove Road in Trezevant had to be closed due to high water as well as the South Bypass around Huntingdon.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Chisholm Lake. As a result, Chisholm Lake Road and the bridge near the lake were impassable due to high water.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over Southern Tipton County for several hours including the cities of Covington, Brighton, and Atoka. Widespread 4-5 inches of rain fell over this particular area. Numerous roads were closed due to flash flooding including Jack Bennett Road and Brighton Road.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over Shelby County for several hours. At first, the heavy rain fell from Millington, to Bartlett, to Arlington. Widepread 4 to 6 inches fell across this northern corridor with isolated 7-8 inches in a few locations. Some locations picked up 1.75 to 2 inches of rain in a 1 hour and 15 minute time frame.  Several homes near Millington were flooded from high water. Water rescues were needed in Mount Terrace for rescuing residents trapped in flooded homes. Numerous streets were closed some of which that had never been closed before due to heavy rain including Bartlett Boulevard and Stage Road in Bartlett. The corridor of the heavy rain shifted southward to Southern Shelby County by 8 am CDT as the cold front sagged south and stalled. Heavy rain fell from Whitehaven, to Germantown, to Collierville. Rainfall amounts ranged from 4 to 7 inches. The heavy rain produced a 20 ft hole in the roof of the Southland Mall near Whitehaven. Again, numerous streets and roads were closed in this corridor as well. In total, 74 homes sustained minor damage from flooding with one apartment complex that contained 31 units. One road also sustained damage. In addition, one business sustained minor damage from flooding as well.

Showers and thunderstorms trained over DeSoto County for several hours. Widespread 3-6 inches fell across the county with a small corridor, near Horn Lake and Olive Branch, that received as much as 8-10 inches of rain. Major flooding occurred near Hernando. Four homes near Cedarview had sewage back into the houses. An apartment complex near Southaven was flooded. Numerous roads and streets were closed due to high water. Some roads sustained damage from culverts washing out or gaping holes developing in the asphalt. Small rivers and streams overflowed their banks producing additional flooding. In total, 55  homes sustained minor damage from flooding with 4 sustaining major damage. Fifty-eight apartment units sustained minor damage with 8 sustaining major damage. Sixty-seven businesses sustained minor damage with ten sustaining major damage.
Straight line winds blew a roof off a classroom building onto a nearby roof.

A tornado briefly touched down just north of Highway 62 near McDougal. Four homes sustained damage. The most significant damage was to a double wide mobile home which had half of the roof torn off. Several trees were knocked down with a few falling onto homes.

Straight line winds produced minor damage to homes in a residential neighborhood and to several businesses mainly from shingle damage or from falling trees. The most significant damage was to a convenience store which had the roof shifted off which then caused a load bearing wall to collapse. One minor injury occurred as a result.
Straight line winds produced some structural damage to a few homes on Johnson Road near Reelfoot Lake.

Straight line winds damaged a roof of a discount store on Lake Road in Northwest Dyersburg.  Several homes also had partial roof damage mainly due to falling trees. A couple of trees were knocked down in the area as well especially on Owen Drive and Pennell Lane.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near Henning.  A couple of homes on Joe Barfield Road sustained minor damage.
Half dollar size hail fell on Highway 22 just north of Milledgeville.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 100, southwest of Decaturville, just inside the county line.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Sardis.
Half dollar size hail fell in Hatley.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines across Southern Monroe County.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees along Highway 25 across Northern Itawamba County. Minor roof damage also occurred in the area as well.
Nickel size hail fell southeast of Baldwyn.
Half dollar size hail fell southeast of Tremont.

Straight line winds produced damage to four homes near Crawfordsville. One roof was damaged and several windows were blown out. A fence was blown down and a trampoline was blown up in a tree. A trailer full of equipment was also blown over. In addition, a 100 year old house had the front pillars knocked down. Numerous tree limbs were blown down.
Golf ball to hen egg size hail fell near Pleasant Ridge.
Quarter to golf ball size hail fell near Shannon and Brewer communities.
Half dollar size hail fell in Randolph.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell from Frayser and Raleigh into Bartlett.
Quarter size hail fell near Milligan Ridge. At least one farm lost 1200 acres of cotton to the hail storm.
Quarter size hail fell near Eastview.
Golf ball size hail fell southwest of Biggers, near Current River Beach.
A trained spotter measured at 63 mph gust. Large tree limbs were knocked down in the Nesbit area. Church Road was blocked by numerous large limbs.

Straight line winds knocked down utililty lines across Central Avenue at Belvedere Boulevard in Midtown. East and westbound lanes were blocked. Multiple trees were knocked down at Mendenhall Road and Poplar Avenue in East Memphis. Large limbs were knocked down on to a house and power lines in the East Acres Community of Millington north of the Naval Base.
Large hail from the size of quarters up to golfballs fell from Bartlett to the east side of Millington.
Quarter to Golfball size hail fell in Earle.
A weak tornado damaged a rice field. The tornado crossed a road into another field with no crops and then lifted. Peak winds were estimated at 60 mph.

Straight line winds damaged the wall and roof of a metal building housing a discount store in northern portions of Harrisburg. Debris from the building broke windows in another building located to the immediate north. A tree approximately one quarter mile northeast of the building was snapped. Widespread trees were uprooted in Greenfield. There were also reports of minor roof damage in Greenfield. There were several trees and power lines knocked down further east in Truman.
Straight line winds knocked power poles and trees down near U.S. Highway 63 and Nestle Road. A semi truck full of chicken parts was blown over on Highway 18 and Highway 69.
Straight line winds caused damaged throughout Tunica County. There was damage to a mobile home and minor damage to a farm shop. Two houses were also damaged.
Straight line winds caused minor roof damage at the Strayhorn Elementary School along Highway 4. Trees and large limbs were knocked down along Highway 4 in the western part of Tate County.
A home weather station measured a 74 knot gust west of Ridgely.
Straight line winds knocked large trees down blocking County Road 59 near Highway 30 west of New Albany. Trees were also reported down in Blue Springs.
Straight line winds knocked a large tree on to a house in Sherman.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along County Road 1766.
Straight line winds knocked down trees across Mantachie.
Straight line winds snapped a couple of large trees in half at Burlison.
Straight line winds snapped three trees with 12 inch trunks near the Dyersburg Golf Course.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees on roads across southern Henderson County.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power poles across northern Henry County, particularly in the Cottage Grove area. Five power poles were broken across the county. A barn was damaged on Jones Bend Road and a tree fell on two vehicles on New Boston Road. Both vehicles suffered damage.

Heavy rain fell near Batesville which produced 1.5 inches in one hour and a total of 3.50 inches over an 8 hour span. This caused a creek to rise out of its banks and flood eight businesses and two homes in the southern part of town. In addition, a possibly impaired driver drove into flood waters on a road that was currently under construction with the installation of new culverts. One fatality and one injury occurred from the accident.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Lafayette County near Taylor. A culvert on County Road 347 was washed out.
Lightning struck a tree in Hayti City Park which then fell on a vehicle. The person inside the vehicle was killed.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the Union City area. The road was closed at the intersection of Highways 184 and 51 due to high water. Flooding also occurred along Harris Road northeast of Union City where water was greater than six inches deep. A section of Second Street in Downtown Union City was also closed due to high water. A spotter in Union City reported 3.66 inches of rain between 8:00 am LST and 12:25 pm LST.

A weak tornado produced intermittent damage in the Lost Creek and Willow Oaks areas located to the east of Decaturville near the Tennessee River in East-Central Decatur County. Several trees were uprooted and one home had small clusters of shingles peeled away. Several other homes had damage to trim and flashing. Estimated maximum winds were 75 mph.
An uprooted tree fell on a car on County Road 405 west of Houston. A large oak tree fell on a trailer near Houlka. Several trees were knocked down on Highway 32 west of Houlka.

Strong winds knocked down a tree on Highway 30 just east of New Albany. The tree struck two cars killing one person. Two others received minor injuries. Several other limbs were knocked down in the city.
Strong winds knocked down a tree on a truck at the intersection of Highway 100 and Highway 64 resulting in one injury.
Straight line winds blew the roof off a barn in Hoxie and knocked down several large trees in Walnut Ridge.

The first tornado occurred southwest of Amory and affected areas south of Highway 278, near McAllister Road and Little Coontail Road. Trees were uprooted and broken. Falling trees damaged the roofs of several houses. Damage along this track was intermittent. Maximum winds were estimated at 75 mph. South of the track an area of non-tornadic wind damage was noted.

The second tornado affected the community of Amory. Numerous large trees were uprooted and broken. Light poles were bent. Falling trees damaged the roofs of several houses, carports and storage sheds. Other homes had areas of shingles removed. Maximum winds were estimated at 95 mph.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in the Amory area. Several roads were flooded including Hatley-Smithville Road and Highway 278 east of Amory.
A weak tornado briefly touched down south-southwest of Brownsville along Shaw Chapel Road. No damage was reported.
The rear flank downdraft associated with the tornado that occurred southwest of Amory uprooted and snapped trees south of the tornado track. One home had minor roof damage.
Straight line winds uprooted trees along Cecil Wall Road near the Henderson and Carroll County line.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in and around Brookland. Numerous roads were flooded including Bernis Street. Rainfall amounts ranged between 2.5 and 3 inches.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding south of Humboldt. Water was flowing over the intersection of Bethel Church Road and Windy City Road.

The first damage from this tornado was to trees and a storage building along Campground Road east of Algoma. Trees and outbuildings were damaged along Mississippi Route 342. The most substantial damage was observed along Highway 278. Several large trees were uprooted, one of which fell on a house. Roof debris from this house landed 150 yards to the northwest of the house. The last damage observed was along Dozier Hill Road north of Trace State Park. Observations suggest that the tornado touched down intermittently along this path. The average path width was around 125 yards. Estimated peak wind was 75 mph.

This tornado developed over Northern Bolivar County and moved into Coahoma County. It strengthened and produced EF-3 damage south and east of Clarksdale where the two fatalities occurred. Twelve homes and two businesses were destroyed. Two homes also suffered minor damage. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. The tornado continued into Quitman County.

The tornado moved from Coahoma County into Quitman County and temporarily weakened. The tornado damaged nearly 20 homes to the west and southwest of Marks. The tornado then tracked into Panola County.

This tornado moved from Quitman County into Panola County. Numerous trees were snapped or uprooted. As the tornado approached Interstate 55 the tornado damaged several homes. This is where the tornado reached peak intensity with winds estimated at 160 mph. The tornado crossed Interstate 55 between Sardis and Como and then dissipated east of Como. A total of 29 homes were affected in Panola. Eight homes were either destroyed or suffered major damage.
The tornado developed over Southeast Tate County. The tornado caused minor roof damage to a house in Tyro before moving into Marshall County.

The tornado tracked into Marshall County from Tate County. As it moved into Marshall County the tornado heavily damaged several homes along Highway 4. The tornado produced damage to a church and surrounding trees southwest of Holly Springs that approached EF-4. The tornado moved across the southeastern edge of Holly Springs causing EF-2 to EF-3 damage. Numerous trees were uprooted or snapped. About 200 homes were damaged in Marshall County. Two fatalities occurred in Marshall County along with at least 30 injuries. The tornado then tracked into Benton County.

The tornado crossed from Marshall County into Benton County near Highway 4 west of Ashland. The tornado appeared to strengthen as it entered Benton County. Several houses west-northwest of Ashland has damage approaching EF-4 with EF-4 damage observed in Northeast Benton County. Six fatalities occurred in Benton County. Eighty-five structures were affected in Benton County. Seventeen homes and fifteen mobile homes were destroyed. Fifteen homes and three mobile homes suffered major damage. Twenty homes and seven mobile homes had minor damage. Many acres of timber were also damaged or destroyed. The tornado then continued into Tippah County.

The tornado crossed from Benton County Mississippi into Tippah County. The tornado moved across far northwestern Tippah County damaging several homes in the Three Forks Community. One fatality occurred in Tippah County. Over 100 houses were affected and about 45 homes were destroyed. The tornado then crossed the Tennessee state line into Hardeman County.

The tornado crossed from Tippah County into Hardeman County. As it crossed over the state line it destroyed a large metal agricultural building. A couple of houses and businesses were also damaged. The tornado then moved into McNairy County.

The tornado moved into McNairy County from Hardeman County and began weakening. Around 15 homes were damaged or destroyed south of Selmer. The last observed damage was near Highway 45 on the southeast edge of Selmer.
This tornado occurred in Western Madison County. The tornado damaged several storage sheds and caused roof damage to a home.
This tornado occurred in Western Prentiss County. The tornado damaged several mobile homes and uprooted trees. One home slid off its foundation.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines on Huddleston Street.

Very heavy rain occurred across Northern Monroe County. Rainfall amounts of up to 10 inches were measured. Flash flooding resulted in 50 homes becoming uninhabitable. Forty county roads were closed. Ten city streets were closed in Amory and three were closed in Smithville. Twenty people were rescued by vehicle or boat in Amory, Smithville, Wren and unincorporated areas especially along the Tombigbee River.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Vardaman. Several streets were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Chickasaw County. Jefferson Street in Houston was flooded. County Road 31 north of Houston was flooded. A car was submerged in water in Okolona.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Itawamba County. Several roads were flooding with a few wash outs in the southern part of the county.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Tallahatchie County. Several county roads were flooded.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in the southwest part of Lee County near Pleasant Grove. County Road 54 was washed out leaving a 10 foot wide gash in the road. This resulted in the closing of the road from the intersection of County Road 101 west. Three homes were impacted by the closure.
Heavy rain resulting in flash flooding in the Corning area. Neighborhoods were flooded and cars stalled.
A tornado touched down southwest of Marianna. A mobile home was destroyed. There was roof damage to homes.
Straight line winds knocked a large tree on to a car on Rich Road.
Straight line winds knocked down fences and tossed patio furniture. A gazebo was also damaged.
A person drowned when attempting to swim in the St. Francis River while it was flooded.
Straight line winds damaged two mobile homes in the Deer Creek area. The swath of damage was 75 yards wide and 150 yards long.

Heavy rain in late 2015 caused flooding along the St. Francis River through much of January. The St. Francis went above the action stage of 29 feet on the afternoon of January 3, 2016 and then climbed above the flood stage of 32 feet on January 6, 2016. The river remained above flood stage until January 16, 2016. A man was swept away after driving into a flooded road near Newcastle during the late afternoon of January 3, 2016.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the eastern part of Memphis. The left lane of I-240 at the I-40 interchange was covered with a foot of water. The ramp to I-40 eastbound from Sycamore View Road was also flooded.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Downtown Memphis. Interstate 40 was flooded at Danny Thomas Boulevard.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Mason. Several roads were flooded included Gainsville Road, Highway 59, Saint Paul Road and Canaan Grove Road.

The tornado snapped or uprooted several trees southwest of, and at the Crockett County Golf Club. It caused roof damage to a mobile home and a permanent structure just south of Highway 412. Two tractor trailers were overturned on Highway 412, with one driver injured. North of Highway 412, the tornado damaged several storage sheds and caused roof damage to several homes. The tornado then crossed Highway 88 and caused roof damage to several buildings at the Crockett County High School. The tornado damaged additional storage sheds and a home roof on the east side of North Cavalier Drive before dissipating. Peak estimated wind was 95 mph.
Heavy rain resulting in flash flooding in Northwest Hardin County. A car was swept away on Martin Road at Middleton Creek. The water rescue was successful.

Straight line winds ripped siding off a building and knocked multiple tree limbs down in Ravenden Springs. An out building was heavily damaged and power poles were knocked down on Long Road near Shannon.
Pea to nickel size hail covered the ground west of Pocahontas.

The tornado caused intermittent damage from west-southwest of Marvell into the town of Marvell. The tornado downed power poles and damaged a small outbuilding along Highway 1 southwest of Marvell. In town, the tornado bent street lights and a power pole. Tree limbs were broken and a baseball field scoreboard was knocked down. Peak estimated wind was 80 mph.
Ping pong size hail fell near Colt.

The tornado caused intermittent damage in far Northern Phillips County, northwest of the town of Lexa. The tornado damaged outbuildings and lightweight structures along Highways 316 and 201. The tornado caused roof damage to a barn and downed wooden power poles along Highway 1 north of Lexa. Peak estimated wind 85 mph.

A tornado touched down just east of Arkansas Route 75 causing minor roof damage to a house and outbuilding. The tornado then moved northeast and flipped a couple of irrigation pivots before damaging a hangar and removing a door off of a barn.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near Downtown Memphis. One foot of water covered Kansas Street under the Interstate 55 bridge.
Penny to nickel size hail fell in the vicinity of Fort Pillow State Park and Fulton.
Straight line winds knocked down large trees near Old Highway 51. Smaller trees and limbs were knocked down in the city limits of Brighton.
A large amount of hail fell one mile south of the intersection of Highway 14 and Highway 59 between Covington and Mason. The hail began as quarter size and diminished to pea size.
Quarter size hail fell north of Milan.
Quarter size hail near Skullbone.
Golf ball size hail fell on Stafford Store Road in the southern part of Weakley County.

A tornado touched down several miles south of Camden in Benton County. The tornado track was intermittent, with two primary areas of damage. The first area was south of the Old Natchez Trace Trail, from Douglas Drive to Douglas Lane. Numerous trees were uprooted, with the tree fall pattern suggesting a circulation. The second area of damage was between Highway 641 and Old Highway 69. The tornado damaged the roof of a barn. Nearby, the tornado blew in the large door of a metal workshop and removed most of the workshop's door. Portions of the roof landed across old Highway 69. The estimated peak wind was 90 mph.
Heavy rain resulted in a road becoming impassable due to rushing water in Ravenden.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding near Pocahontas. Parts of Highway 166 were closed due to high water.

Very heavy rainfall occurred across the Jonesboro area. Over five inches of rain fell in some spots and as a result widespread flash flooding occurred. Many roads were flooded and impassable with over two feet of water. Several roads were washed out as well. The police department responded to 32 calls of stalled vehicles in water. Many parking lots were flooded. There were also reports of water entering homes. Two feet of water was reported in a home on the 2500 block of Mary Jane Street in East Jonesboro.  At least three water rescues from vehicles occurred. Flooding also occurred on the Arkansas State Campus.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Manila. Water over six inches deep was common in the residential areas of Manila.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Trumann. Ozark Street was closed due to high water.
Quarter size hail fell in West Jonesboro.
Straight line winds took large chunks of siding off a building in downtown Jonesboro.
Quarter size hail fell in Lepanto.
Straight line winds knocked down dozens of trees and several power poles. The damage occurred mostly on the north side of Wynne.
A home weather station anemometer recorded a gust of 80 mph. A shutter was blown off a home.
Straight line winds knocked over a tractor trailer on Interstate 55 south of Burdette.
Quarter size hail fell north of Halls.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Drummonds and power poles in Atoka.
Penny to Quarter size hail fell around Atoka and Brighton in Southern Tipton County.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Mudville Road.
Nickel to quarter size hail fell in Jackson from near Interstate 40 to downtown.
Quarter size hail fell east of Henderson.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and caused structural damage in Roby.
A weak tornado caused mainly roof damage to a home and damage to a recreational vehicle. Trees were knocked down along with a power pole. Peak estimated wind was 90 mph.
Golf ball sized hail fell north of Tunica.
Straight line winds removed shingles from a funeral home just north of Tunica.
Penny to quarter size hail fell in Hernando.
Quarter size hail fell in the Old Union Community.
Several roads and streets were closed due over six inches of flood water covering them.
Highway 1 was closed due to flash flooding.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across all of Shelby County. Several roads and streets were closed as a result including Sam Cooper Boulevard in Midtown and Collierville-Arlington in Collierville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding that closed many roads around Union City including Town and Country Road. A driver was rescued from a car on Knox-Daniel Road.
Several roads off of Route 77, east of Trenton, were impassable due to flash flooding.
Several roads around DeSoto County were impassable due to flash flooding. In addition, a local residential dam was breached causing Austin Road near Highway 301 to be closed.

Flash flooding evolved into flooding as heavy rain continued over DeSoto County. Numerous roads were closed as a result of flood water including Highway 61, south of Church Road, and Holly Springs Road. In addition, one person had to be rescued from a car that was submerged in flood water. Another swift water rescue also occurred. The heavy rain caused land to collapse near Eudora that knocked down a power pole and a power line on Fogg Road.

Continued heavy rainfall brought many road closures to Tunica County due to flooded roadways. Several homes were evacuated off Highway 3 in Robinsonville. A total of 118 homes were damaged. Forty-four roads suffered damage and 245 people were displaced.

Flooding occurred in the Barton and North Red Banks areas. A few homes affected due to roads being inaccessible. Eight people were displaced. Over one foot of water covered Moore Road near Red Banks. Highway 309 one mile south of the Tennessee state line was also flooded. A total of five roads were flooded.

Heavy rain caused drainage ditches and small creeks off of the Coldwater River to flood western portions of Panola County. Sandbagging protected 12 homes in the Crenshaw area and another 3 homes near Curtis Station. Homes were flooded on Renaissance Street in Crenshaw. A total of 35 homes and 14 roads were affected. Forty people were displaced. Two businesses suffered minor damage.
Heavy rain caused widespread flooding across Crockett County. More than ten roads were closed as a result.
A COOP Observer reported 5.52 inches of rain since the evening of March 9th. Several roads near Bemis were covered with water and closed as a result.

Another round of heavier showers and thunderstorms brought flood waters back up across Haywood County. Sugar Creek flooded numerous streets in Brownsville. Highway 87 and Highway 70 were flooded along with many secondary roads. One person was rescued from a flooded vehicle on Bunn Avenue.

Another round of heavier showers and thunderstorms brought flash flooding back into Shelby County. About 30 roads were closed due to water. The intersection of Macon Road and Houston Levee Road was flooded with at least a foot of water. A Grey's Creek area ditch, just south of the Macon Road Bridge, washed out and compromised a utility pole. Water from drainage ditches began to surround homes in the Barton community.

Another round of heavier showers and thunderstorms caused additional flash flooding near Bemis. A few residents needed to be rescued by boat. Widespread flash flooding occurred in Jackson with numerous roads closed including Airways Boulevard at the US Highway 45 Bypass, Weatheridge Drive, Shadow Ridge Drive, and Pipkin Road. In addition, Fairgrounds Park was also flooded. There were also 15 secondary road closures.
Heavy rain caused flooding in the Blytheville area. Franklin Road was flooded.

Another round of heavier showers and thunderstorms moved across Henderson County during the early afternoon hours of March 10, 2016. As a result flash flooding occurred and several more roads were flooded with more than 6 inches of water.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Carroll County. Mt. Zion Church Road was flooded just east of Huntingdon. About a dozen other county roads were also flooded. Highways 219, 22, 436 and 77 were flooded as well.

Multiple rounds of heavy rain caused flooding in Quitman County. Ninety-three homes and two businesses were affected. Seventy-nine roads were damaged and 30 people were displaced. Two injuries were reported.

Over 8 inches of rain fell along the Wolf River Basin from late on March 8th through the afternoon on March 10th. This caused flooding along the Wolf River in Eastern Shelby County. Farmland in Shelby Farms was flooded along with the Greenway along the Wolf River. Farm Road was closed in Shelby Farms. Another 3 inches of rain fell on March 12th and 13th which prolonged the flooding.

Another heavier round of showers and thunderstorms brought flash flooding back into DeSoto County. Several roads were closed east and south of Hernando. Holly Springs Road east of Hernando flooded trapping a family. A total of 12 homes were flooded or inaccessible. Camp Creek flooded nearby fields at Byhalia Road. Love Road was washed out just east of Highway 51 near Cedar Farms. Rainfall totals from late on March 8th to the afternoon of March 10th totaled over 9 inches in parts of DeSoto County.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Gibson County. At least a dozen roads were flooded.

Heavy rain over the previous two days caused flooding in Mason. Multiple water rescues by boat occurred in Mason. Main Street on the south side of Mason was closed due to flooding. Three other roads were also flooded.

Several rounds of heavy rain resulting in flooding of the Big Sunflower River in Coahoma County. Several homes had to be evacuated near the river in Clarksdale. Eighty-five homes suffered minor flood damage while two mobile homes suffered major flood damage. One road received major damage.
An agricultural levee broke near the Rutherford Fork of the Obion River. This affected eastern sections of Kenton where 20 houses were evacuated.
Heavy rain resulting in flash flooding in Weakley County. As a result Hyndsver Road near Martin was flooded.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Weakley County. As a result the intersection of Cotton Creek Road and Clay Pit Road was flooded.

Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Benton County. Valentine Branch Road in Big Sandy was closed due to a washed out culvert. Old Highway 70 was closed along with Fern Street in Camden. Liberty Church Road was covered with water. Washington Street was also closed.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding in Chester County. One home was inaccessible due to flooding.

Heavy rain caused widespread flooding across Dyer County. Several roads were closed including Highway 105 outside of Trimble and Highway 210 South. Tatumville Road, Beanhill Road and Peach Orchard Road were also flooded.

Over 7 inches of rain fell along the Wolf River Basin from late on March 8th through the afternoon on March 10th. This caused flooding along the Wolf River in Fayette County. Highways 57 and 196 were flooded. Many secondary roadways were flooded.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Hardeman County. A few roads were flooded and one road was closed due to a damaged culvert.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Hardin County. There was flash flooding along Highway 69 in Savannah. Several secondary roads were also flooded.
Heavy rain caused flooding across Henderson County. Several roads were flooded northwest and west of Lexington.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Henry County. At the height of the flooding 24 roads were flooded including Highways 77, 114 and 54.
Over six inches of rain fell over parts of Obion County causing the Obion River to flood. Turnpike road and Pleasant Valley Road were flooded along with farmland.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across parts of Tipton County. Some roads were flooded and State Highway 206 was washed out.
Heavy rain resulting in flooding across Weakley County. Several low lying and secondary roads were flooded.

Heavy rain result in flash flooding across Tate County. Highway 3 was closed just north of the intersection with Highway 4. Six homes were affected and eight people were displaced. Nineteen roads were closed and there was damage to the county courthouse and administration building.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding near the Loosahatchie River in Northern Shelby County. Four households and a total of seven people were evacuated from the 5800 block of Covington Pike Road.
Several rounds of heavy rain resulting in flooding across parts of Tallahatchie County. Forty-seven homes suffered minor damage and 43 roads were damaged.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Weiner. Water over six inches deep was common in the residential areas of Weiner.
Straight line winds damaged the roof and siding of a home. A privacy fence was downed along with a few trees.
Strong winds uprooted a tree that fell on a home in Milan on Lea Lane.

Strong winds knocked down several trees and power lines across Shelby County. A large tree fell on an outbuilding at an apartment complex in East Memphis. A large tree and power lines were knocked down at Sea Isle Road and Dearing Road. A 54 mph gust was recorded at Memphis International Airport.
A man and the horse he was riding were struck by lightning in Mantachie.

This tornado followed an intermittent path from west through southeast of the Wren Community. Trees were sporadically uprooted or large branches broken. The tornado caused minor damage to a residence south of Wren and to a few storage buildings in this area. Peak winds were estimated at 70 to 75 mph.

This brief tornado occurred just northeast of the Monroe County Airport. This tornado broke branches or uprooted several trees, one of which fell on a church. Peak winds were estimated at 65 to 70 mph.

The tornado damage was spotty and intermittent along the path. Tree damage occurred along County roads 5141,5051,and 5091. A mobile home was damaged along County road 5091. A stand of pine trees was damaged north of Highway 4, approximately 1.5 miles northeast of Hobo Station. The last damage was observed west of New Site. Although the tornado was rated an EF1, the EF1 damage was confined to isolated areas. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph. Other wind damage occurred across the county, especially in the Wheeler vicinity and just south of Booneville.

The tornado developed northeast of Belmont and crossed into Alabama east-northeast of Belmont. Tree damage was noted along highway 993 and a barn was damaged along highway 68. Peak winds with the tornado were estimated at 80 mph. To the southwest of the tornado track, a larger area of strong winds associated with the storms' Rear Flank Downdraft (RFD) affected northern and northeastern portions of Belmont. Winds in this region likely approached 80 to 90 mph. These winds caused tree and roof damage, especially in the Valley Road area.

The Current River experienced a record flood upstream at Doniphan, MO in early May. The water moved downstream and caused the evacuation of Success, AR on May 1st. Highways 328 and 211 were flooded along with thousands of acres of farmland. The swiftness of the water deposited large amounts of sand and gravel across much of the farmland. Highway 67 south of Corning was flooded.

The levee east of Pocahontas broke in several places during the morning hours of May 3rd. Water poured south along the Big Running Water Creek across thousands of acres of farmland. Many small communities were flooded. Several water rescues occurred at the intersection of Highway 67 and Highway 90 in Shannon.

The Black River levee east of Pocahontas suffered several breaches during the early morning hours of May 3rd. The water flowed south along the Big Running Water Creek and eventually flooded parts of Lawrence County. Highway 63 was closed between Portia and Walnut Ridge. Water flowing over the highway damaged the shoulders. Roads leading into Clover Bend were flooded and several houses in the area had water inside them.

Heavy rain brought the Black River at Pocahontas to a record crest that topped the April 2011 flood. The levee east of town broke in at least nine places, including one 300 yard stretch, sending water across much of Randolph County. East Pocahontas was flooded and suffered major damage. Highway 67 was flooded between Pocahontas and Walnut Ridge. Highway 67/62 between Pocahontas and Corning was flooded. Highways 166 and 304 were also closed. Highway 304 was closed for 37 days. The Current River also flooded farmland in eastern Randolph County. Numerous homes, farms, businesses and vehicles were flooded. Many roads and bridges were flooded and damaged. More than 500 people were evacuated Pocahontas. At least 50 homes were destroyed or damaged by flooding in Pocahontas. The Elnora Freewill Baptist Church was heavily damaged. The Randolph County Jail had to evacuate prisoners.

Heavy rain brought the Black River at Black Rock to just under record levels in early May. Homes and businesses suffered minor damage from the flooding. Many road and bridges were also flooded and damaged. Thousands of acres of cropland was also flooded. The Lawrence County Dive team performed 14 rescues in the first couple days of May. They rescued people from their vehicle on County Road 514 on May 2nd. The dive team rescued two people from a home on May 3rd.

The tornado started just south of Highway 42 about 5 miles west of the town of Cherry Valley causing damage to two farmsteads. Other damage included downed tree limbs and minor damage to a few farm outbuildings and one grain bin. Estimated peak wind was 100 mph.

The tornado touched down along Highway 88 about 4 miles west-northwest of Halls. A mobile home was shifted from its foundation and destroyed. The tornado continued east-northeast and crossed Double Bridges Road where it caused significant roof damage to one home and destroyed an outbuilding of another home. The tornado continued across Mill Creek Road to Church Road where three homes were damaged. The roof was blown off of one home and completely destroyed the kitchen area. The other two homes suffered roof damage, fence damage and a collapsed garage. The tornado continues east-northeast and reached its maximum intensity as it moved across Highway 51 in the Poplar Grove Community. The damage was rated as a strong EF1 tornado with winds of 110 mph. There was significant structural damage to one home with the complete loss of the roof. The house was also shifted off its foundation. A machine shed was also destroyed. Many trees were snapped and uprooted along the entire path of the tornado. In addition, several power lines were knocked down. The tornado then moved into Dyer County.

A home suffered minor damage with windows blown out and debris thrown into trees. More trees were snapped. The tornado weakened and continued east-northeast across Pond Creek to Ashley Road where it damaged a mobile home. The tornado then lifted just to the east-northeast and the damage path ended.

The tornado developed in far eastern Pontotoc County along Lee Line Road. The tornado then caused EF-0 and EF-1 damage to homes and trees just west and north of the Tupelo Airport. As it approached Colonial Estates Road the tornado intensified and damaged numerous homes. Two homes had roofs completely removed and non-brick exterior walls collapsed on one of them. Several homes saw partial roof damage. As the tornado crossed McCullough Blvd., several businesses were damaged including one which had the roof partially removed. The tornado weakened and continued on snapping trees and causing some slight structural damage as it crossed I-22 where it hit buildings just south of Barnes Crossing Mall.  The tornado intensified again as it crossed Bog Oaks Golf Club and approached an assisted living center. The tornado caused considerable roof damage to the assisted living center. The final damage seen before it lifted was observed along County Road 851.

After crossing Highway 371 the tornado continued to uproot and snap off numerous trees and caused minor damage to several mobile homes. The last damage observed was east of Ramey Road northeast before dissipating.

The tornado damage was EF0/EF1 in Alcorn County with numerous trees knocked down. A home received moderate damage to mainly the roof while several manufactured homes were damaged. Several outbuildings and sheds were also damaged. Peak winds in Alcorn County were near 100 mph.  Most of the path was in rural areas in Alcorn county. The tornado crossed into Tishomingo County.

The tornado reached maximum intensity of EF-2 just northwest of Burnsville near Highway 72 where several well built homes suffered significant damage. Peak winds were estimated at 115 mph. Otherwise the tornado tracked through rural areas knocking down trees. A home on County Road 294 suffered minor damage before the tornado lifted.

Several residential structures and metal buildings had roof damage. Many homes and recreational vehicles were damaged by falling trees. The tornado crossed Pickwick Lake and caused minor damage to an industrial facility and a residence east of the lake. Peak winds were estimated at 85 to 90 mph.

The tornado developed just south of Hamilton, MS and rapidly increased in intensity. Substantial damage to residences and outbuildings occurred along Seely Drive south of Hamilton Road. Numerous trees were uprooted or trunks snapped along the track. A tree fell on a mobile home on Center Hill Road north of Hamilton killing the resident. The tornado continued north-northeast, uprooting trees and causing minor structural damage. The tornado dissipated near West Road. Three injuries were also reported. Peak winds were estimated at 130 mph.

Tornado occurred mostly in forested areas. Several homes received primarily roof damage. Several transmission line towers were destroyed approximately 2 miles north of Highway 278. Peak winds were estimated near 115 mph.
Street and road flooding occurred in Marianna. Flooding was reported along Highway 79.
Street flooding was reported in Helena-West Helena. Flooding was reported along Highway 49 in Marvell.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding on Highway 79 in Marianna.
Reports of widespread street and low lying flooding across the county and especially in Senatobia.

A tornado touched down one quarter mile east of Brunswick Road interchange along Highway 385 in the Salem Estates Subdivision. The tornado tracked non-continuously northeast to the Tipton County line, near the Collierville-Arlington Road. Damage sustained in the Salem Estates subdivision was rated an EF-0. One roof of a home was partially removed along with several blown out windows. In addition, some minor tree damage occurred in this area. Further northeast, along Moose Road west of Beaver Creek, the tornado intensified and produced EF-2 damage. Significant tree damage occurred from the tornado in this area. In addition, two power line support towers were knocked down and one was twisted. Significant damage occurred further northeast along Osborntown Road as extensive tree damage was observed. Large trees were snapped and uprooted. In addition, two large well constructed new homes were heavily damaged. One home had more than half of its roof removed along with all windows blown out. Brick was also dislodged from portions of the structure. The second home received extensive damage with the entire second story being removed from the tornado. Inside walls were compromised and debris was deposited inside the home and in the front yard. One minor injury occurred from this segment of EF-2 rated damage. Additional damage occurred further northeast across Macedonia Road producing additional tree damage and minor damage to one home and one mobile home. Damage also occurred just south of where the tornado crossed into Tipton County where five homes sustained light to moderate damage along Collierville-Arlington Road. This damage has been rated EF-1. One of the homes sustained significant damage to portions of the roof and adjoining levels. The other four homes had damage to the roofs and windows. Large trees, some up to 3 feet in diameter were snapped and uprooted. The tornado then tracked into Tipton County.

This tornado began in Northeast Shelby County and crossed into Tipton County along Hughes Road. The tornado tracked northeast and lifted near Beaver Creek Road. One home had minor damage on Beaver Creek Road.  Tornado damage was estimated to be EF-0.
Power outages from downed power lines reported across portions of Hardin County.
Damage to swimming pool, as well as damage to a dog house and play house.
Trees down on County Road 130 near Banner.
One tree down near home on County Road 101, as well as damage to a windshield from a tree branch.

One large tree down on the Ole Miss campus in front of Lamar Hall.
One tree down off Highway 6 in Plantersville.
Large tree down on old Highway 8 east of Houston.
One large tree down on Lake Lilly Road.
Straight line winds blew shingles off roofs near Brazil.

A tornado touched down near Old Highway 61 and damaged a farm building roof. The tornado tracked northeast for a little more than 2 miles, lifting along Norfolk Road. A pivot irrigation system was damaged and power poles were knocked down along Norfolk Road.
Straight line winds damaged a shed and knocked down trees just south of Kenton.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees.
Straight line winds moved a mobile home a few feet and damaged the underpinnings.

A tornado touched down at Southaven High School and tracked northeast crossing into Shelby County, Tennessee, northeast of the intersection of Stateline Road and Airways Boulevard. Roughly 30 windows were blown out of the High School. The school also sustained minor roof damage. Damage at the high school was classified EF-0. Many homes in the Carriage Hills subdivision sustained minor damages as well. Further northeast, more significant damage occurred near the intersection of Stateline Road and Airways Boulevard in the warehouse area. Three warehouses were destroyed including the Cooper Lighting Plant. A gas station was damaged as well. Damage was classified as EF-2 in this area. Numerous trees, power poles, and lines were knocked down. Minor roof damage occurred along the path as well.

A tornado continued northeast from DeSoto County, Mississippi. After the tornado crossed into Tennessee, several warehouses sustained damage. The DSC warehouse near Clarke Road was struck causing EF-2 damage. Three people were killed inside the warehouse. Hardy Bottling Company sustained substantial damage as well. Tractor-trailers were tossed about in the area. Windows were shattered in the Willow Lake Business Park and utility poles and trees were snapped in the area. A utility substation sustained severe damage along Clarke Road causing major power outages in the area. The tornado then continued northeast and struck homes along Maple Tree Drive and Pinbranch Court. Five homes received major damage and had to be condemned. Other homes sustained roof damage. The tornado continued northeast and struck the Hickory Ridge Mall causing a wall to collapse at the Sears Department Store. Six injuries occurred at the mall. This damage was estimated at EF-1. The tornado then struck a Taco Bell along Winchester Road before lifting. Thirteen people in all were transported to an area hospital due to injuries sustained from the tornado.

Straight line winds damaged a roof at the Fed Ex Fire Station at the Memphis International Airport. In addition, the Pinnacle Airlines hangar also received damage. A Boeing 737 was moved a few feet by the winds as well.
Straight line winds knocked down a few trees.
An EF-0 tornado briefly touched down in the Coles Point community, just south of Sardis Lake. The tornado flipped a tractor over, destroyed a shed, and caused minor tree damage.

A tornado touched down on the west side of Powell Levee Road. The tornado knocked down trees. The tornado then crossed the road and damaged a mobile home and several trees on the east side of the road. The tornado then crossed into Henry County, Tennessee.

A tornado crossed into Henry County from Weakley County, Tennessee. The tornado traveled northeast damaging an abandoned home and several trees on Bethany Road as well as a barn. On Hayes Store Road, a home suffered severe shingle damage and damage to the soffits and trimmings. Five huge oak trees in front of the home were either uprooted or broken off. Two barns at this location also received damage. Several more trees were snapped off across the street. Further northeast on Wiggins-Capps Road, a barn was destroyed, along with several snapped trees. Three more homes were damaged on Highway 69. The first home sustained shingle damage with a large antenna being knocked over by the tornado. The second home lost several shutters with also a large antenna and flag pole being knocked over. The third home lost half of the roof and a barn was destroyed behind the house. At the end of the tornado track, 3 mobile homes suffered damage with two being severe. The first mobile home had roof damage. The other two mobile homes were double-wides and were sitting on blocks. Both shifted about six feet off their blocks. A barn and a 26 X 26 ft. shop building were completely destroyed. The tornado lifted along Jones Mills Crossland Road.

A tornado touched down just south of Sardis Lake and tracked northeast, south of the southern edge of the lake. The tornado snapped and uprooted many trees. A house and its outbuildings were also damaged along the path. In addition, a few other structures were damaged as well. The path was non-continuous.
Tornado reported near Knob, Arkansas with damage to a home on Greene Road 402.

A tornado touched down in the Lafayette County Industrial Park on County Road 166 north of Oxford. The tornado destroyed the Ability Works Incorporated plant and tracked northeast hitting a county owned speculation warehouse and the Caterpillar Plant. The Elliot Lumber Company was also heavily damaged. The tornado then tracked northeast crossing County Road 101 near the County Road 104 intersection. In this area the Harvest Ministries Church, a mobile home and a veterinary clinic were all destroyed. Tree damage was noted as the tornado crossed Highway 7. The tornado continued northeast inflicting heavy damage along County Road 291 where 12 homes and mobile homes were destroyed. The tornado then damaged 2,500 acres of the Holly Springs National Forest before lifting about 2 miles east of Abbeville. A total of about 70 structures were damaged or destroyed. Eleven homes were destroyed and about 15 suffered heavy damage. About 10 mobile homes were destroyed or heavily damaged. Nine commericial structures were destroyed with another 6 suffering heavy damage. The rest of the structures had minor to moderate damage.
Brief tornado touchdown near Gosnell with one large tree uprooted on Moody Street.

This tornado formed along County Road 534 southeast of Caruthersville. The tornado uprooted trees before crossing the Mississippi River levee. The remainder of the track was then between the levees. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

This tornado formed in open country west of Bluff Road. It uprooted trees as it moved through a creek bed and crossed Bluff Road. The tornado dissipated shortly after the crossing of Bluff Road. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

A tornado touched down in the Country Farms subdivision on Schaeffer Road in Eads. One home had minor damage to the roof, gutters and a gazebo. A few small trees in the area were uprooted or snapped. The tornado then traveled northeast and caused the former Eads Elementary School to lose a significant amount of roof shingles. The tornado then crossed Collierville-Arlington Road and snapped and uprooted several trees near the Cypress Creek Canal. The tornado then tracked into Fayette County.

The tornado tracked from Shelby County and produced damage on Donelson Road where one house was stripped of some siding and roof shingles. A couple of windows were also blown out. Several trees were snapped 10 to 20 feet above the ground and many other trees were uprooted.
