A tornado touched down near Akin Road. Shortly after touchdown, the tornado crossed Yum Yum Road. A man sitting in his truck in a shed was killed when the tornado struck the shed. The truck tumbled at least 40 feet and was severely damaged. Other vehicles were tossed about from the tornado. Substantial damage to large trees in the area occurred as well. The tornado continued northeast and crossed into Haywood County, Tennessee.

A tornado crossed into Haywood County from Fayette County. The tornado produced EF-2 damage in Dancyville. One home was destroyed and another suffered severe damage. A church also had major damage and numerous large trees were uprooted. The tornado continued northeast and caused destruction in Hillville. Two mobile homes were totally destroyed and one house had major damage. A convenience store also suffered roof damage. In addition, an outbuilding was completely flattened and large trees were uprooted or snapped. Several other homes had minor damage along the path. The tornado continued northeast eventually crossing into Madison County. Cleanup costs incurred by Haywood County totaled $168,980.

A tornado crossed into Madison County from Haywood County, Tennessee. The tornado struck the town of Huntersville and produced EF-3 damage. One home was totally destroyed on Huntersville-Denmark Road. One person was killed inside the home. Another home was destroyed in Huntersville. One person was killed in this home as well. Numerous homes were destroyed or damaged along the path in Huntersville area. The St. John No. 2 Baptist Church was severely damaged and the church bus was flipped upside down and tossed several hundred feet. The tornado lifted northeast of Huntersville near Interstate 40. A rest area along Interstate 40 was severely damaged. Thirteen tractor-trailers and several cars were also blown off of the Interstate due to the tornado. One car was tossed 75 yards from Interstate 40 into a farm field. Along the track of this tornado over 50 structures were destroyed and over 80 more were damaged.
Large tree down on County Road 1178 northwest of Evergreen.
Tree down across Dorsey Evergreen Road.
Three trees down on Highway 368.
Tree down in Gillis Mills Cementary.

Road sign bent in the southbound lane of Red Wolf Boulevard, near Race Street.

Several county roads were blocked to downed power lines and trees. The city of Brookland suffered from several downed trees and power lines as well. An equipment shed on County Road 741 suffered roof damage.
Tree down in resident's yard.
Gust of 58 mph recorded at Malden AWOS.
Gust recorded at Kennett Airport.

Power lines and trees down in Cardwell. Four streets were blocked. A roof was blown off a building. Several houses had roof and siding damage. Several utility poles were knocked down across southern Dunklin County. A church steeple was blown off in Hornersville.
Large tree fell on a home in north Collierville.
Tree down on power lines at holly Springs Road. Road closed by police.
Mobile home completely destroyed. Occupant was thrown out into a ditch with minor injuries.
Power pole down on shed.
Tree down in Thaxton.
Quarter size hail in South Fulton.

The tornado touched down at the Union University Campus near the U.S. Highway 45 Bypass in Jackson producing tremendous damage. Fifty one people were injured at Union University as two dormitories collapsed during the passage of the violent tornado. Eighty percent of the dorms were severely damaged or destroyed. Three academic buildings received major damage and 14 other campus buildings were damaged. Several hundred vehicles in the campus parking lots were also damaged or destroyed. The damage in the University area was rated EF-4 with maximum winds of 170 mph. The track was 125 yards wide. The damage at the university alone was estimated at $40,000,000. The tornado then tracked across the U.S. Highway 45 Bypass damaging several banks and businesses before hitting the Regional Hospital and adjacent doctors' offices. The tornado then moved across North Jackson inflicting significant damage to many subdivisions and businesses. The Chapel Creek, Indian Hills and Wyndhurst subdivisions were all struck by the tornado. The tornado also damaged the Jackson Oaks Senior Living Complex. The tornado continued to track northeast striking the Northside High School in the Oak Hill area. The tornado then moved through the Walnut Trace subdivision before crossing Old Medina Road and damaging more houses. The tornado then continued northeast causing EF-3 damage near the intersection of Christmasville Road and Ashport Road in Northeast Madison County before lifting. The Madison County Fire Station No. 11 was destroyed. The station's fire engine and pumper, water and brush trucks were all damaged. Several homes in the area were also damaged. The maximum winds were 145 mph in this area and the track was 100 yards wide. Along the track of this tornado over 70 structures were destroyed with over 500 more damaged.

A brief EF-2 tornado touchdown occurred in Spring Creek along Highway 152 about one quarter mile west of Highway 70. One home suffered total roof loss and a partial failure of the front exterior wall. Three additional homes received extensive roof damage. Large trees were snapped and uprooted. Maximum winds were estimated at 125 mph with a maximum width of 150 yards.
Straight line winds knocked down and snapped trees in a small wooden area along Roger Frye Road about one mile west southwest of Cedar Grove in Carroll County.

A weak tornado touched down just south of Chalybeate and tracked northeast. Damage was reported on County Road 227, near the intersection of County Road 225 and County Road 222, and on County Road 223. Several homes sustained minor damage. A few barns and storage buildings were destroyed. Many trees were knocked down along the path along with some power poles. One tree knocked down half of a brick chimney on a house located on County Road 222A.  The tornado was rated an EF-0 with wind speeds estimated around 60 mph. The width was estimated to be around 50 yards.

The tornado touched down in the community of Union Center about four miles west of the town of Theo. Much of the damaged occurred along County Road 654A. Six mobile homes were hit with two destroyed and two heavily damaged. Four injuries occurred in the mobile home that was destroyed. Several vehicles and a RV was tossed about as well. Numerous trees were knocked down in the vicinity. The tornado then tracked northeast across U.S. Highway 72 and struck three houses near Chapman's Restaurant. The Bethlehem Baptist Church sustained roof damage and the nearby cemetery was damaged. The tornado was rated EF-1 with wind speeds estimated around 100 mph and a width of 100 yards.

The tornado touched down near Highway 57 just east of Ramer. Several large trees were knocked down in the area. The tornado traveled non-continuously toward the northeast producing more damage in the town of Eastview where one business was destroyed and a second business was damaged along U.S. Highway 45. The tornado continued northeast and traveled through a forested area where numerous trees were blown down. the tornado continued across Highway 142. Two homes received roof damage and one mobile home was destroyed in the area. The tornado was rated an EF-1 with wind speeds estimated around 105 mph and a width of around 150 yards.
Golf ball to baseball size hail fell northwest of Jackson near the intersection of McClellan and Windy City Roads.
Quarter size hail reported in the Overland Hill Community.
A weak tornado briefly touched down about 3 miles west of Colt.

The initial tornado touchdown occurred about one mile west northwest of Dalton, Arkansas around 720 pm CST. The tornado moved northeast for 11 miles on a non-continuous path with the last touchdown near Warm Springs, Arkansas before crossing into Missouri. The maximum width was around 200 yards. The tornado was determined to be an EF-1 with maximum wind speeds near 110 mph. There were 4 minor injuries. The first touchdown occurred one mile west northwest of Dalton and destroyed one home. Minor damage occurred to another house and a detached garage with living quarters above it. The tornado touched down again near the Blackwell Community about 3 miles northeast of Dalton. A manufactured home was moved off its foundation with an outbuilding totally destroyed. Another touchdown occurred 4 miles northeast of Dalton moving a cabin off its block foundation. A fourth touchdown was noted 5 miles northeast of Dalton. Three homes had moderate roof damage. In addition, a large metal building had severe damage. Tree damage was noted near Warm Springs indicating another touchdown. The tornado then tracked into Ripley County, Missouri.
Straight line winds knocked a tree down onto a house.

The initial tornado touchdown occurred west of the Tennessee River near the intersection of Coffee Landing Road and Towboat Lane about 740 pm CST. The tornado then quickly raced northeast causing extensive damage to homes and trees just east of the Tennessee River in the Oak Grove, Cerro Gordo and Swift Communities. The tornado destroyed 59 houses, 11 mobile homes, 11 public buildings, a vacant store and 11 farm buildings. Another 117 structures received varying degrees of damage. Four of the 11 public buildings belonged to the Sharon Baptist Church. The church lost its sanctuary, preschool, academy and student center, off Cravens Road in the Oak Grove area. Two of the five injuries occurred at the church while two more injuries occurred in homes in the Oak Grove area. All three deaths occurred in mobile homes. Two of the deaths occurred in the Cerro Gordo area while the third fatality occurred in northeast Hardin County in the vicinity of Nance Bend Road and Highway 128. The tornado continued northeast before lifting near the intersection of Highway 114 and Highway 128 around 757 pm CST. The path length was about 16 miles and the maximum width was one half mile. The highest estimated winds were around 170 mph. Utility restoration costs were estimated at around $200,000.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines just south of Huntingdon.
A weak tornado touched down in an open field near Highway 79 just northeast of Monroe, Arkansas. One tree was snapped off.
Straight line winds tore a roof of a house in Springville.
Straight line winds knocked down several trees in Lexington.
Straight line winds knocked down limbs and caused some roof damage to a home in Paragould. Damage was also reported on U.S. Highway 412 at the Cache River.
Straight line winds caused roof damage to a home and destroyed a shed in Cardwell.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and damaged the underpinnings of a mobile home in Caruthersville.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and caused some minor roof damage in the West Helena and Helena area. A storage shed roof was blown off and another shed was picked up over a four foot fence and thrown into the side of a house.

Straight line winds knocked down numerous power poles and trees in the Tunica area. A tree was knocked onto a house causing moderate damage. Twenty to thirty residential homes had shingle damage and three apartment complexes had roof damage. The antenna was blown off the roof of the Tunica EMA building and an 86 mph gust was reported at the Tunica Airport. Structural damage to a few businesses occurred near the Resort District.

A small child died inside a hot car in Booneville, MS.
Wiley Avenue was flooded in Germantown.
Straight line winds knocked trees across roads in the southern tip of Decatur County.

Several hundred acres burned in a cut corn field near Bride Road between Leighs Chapel and Mt. Lebanon Road. An estimated 300-500 acres burned. More than 60 firefighters worked for 8 hours to contain the fire.
Video scoreboard at RMC Stadium in Trumann was knocked down by straight line winds.
Baseball size hail was reported in the Falkner area. A county road department truck was heavily damaged.
Straight line winds blew down a barn near Dennis.
Straight line winds knocked down a tree on North Main Street in Sardis. In addition, a power pole was knocked down on Frontage Road.
Lightning struck a home on County Road 112 outside of Tishomingo. The strike produced a fire in the storage shed. The shed was destroyed.
A weak tornado briefly touched down in the Lake Chautauqua area of western Tippah County. Two homes and two vehicles were damaged. Numerous trees were knocked down in the area.
Power poles were knocked down at Highway 301 and Oak Grove Road.
House in Hernando was struck by lightning and caught fire.
Nickel sized hail fell at the Highway 45 Bypass near the Chester County line.

This was a short track tornado that touched down in the southwest part of Tyronza and tracked northeast. There was straight line wind damage surrounding the tornado. Primarily damage to a convenience store and elementary school. Several outbuildings were destroyed and numerous trees down.

Power lines were downed near the intersection of Highway 51 and North Watkins Street in Frayser.  A large tree was knocked down across Pleasant Ridge Road between Jack Bond Road and Brunswick Road. Pleasant Ridge Road was closed. Some power lines were knocked down across Jack Bond Road.

Tornado began at the Memphis International Airport and lifted in the Balmoral area of East Memphis. The most significant damage occurred at the Cottonwood Apartments. Significant roof damage occurred at the apartments. Numerous trees and business signs down along the track.

The tornado that struck portions of Memphis from the airport to Balmoral produced a swath of wind damage as it collapsed. The swath stretched from near Balmoral through parts of Germantown and consisted mostly of tree damage.
Trees were knocked down in Henning.
Tree fell on home and power lines downed near Gallaway.
Barn destroyed along Macon Road. Roof damage to a home and a lot of tree damage along Sonny Road.
Numerous trees down in Halls. Damage to metal outbuildings.

A portable car port was blown over and a 200 gallon empty tank of propane fell over on School Street in Hornersville. Small branches and limbs down. Three rollup doors at the cotton gin complex were blown down.
The tornado touched down in farmlands near the Mississippi River and tracked intermittently northeast across the Mississippi into Arkansas breaking tree limbs and uprooting a few trees.
Tornado touched down in farmlands near the Mississippi River in Tennessee then crossed the river into Arkansas. The tornado broke tree limbs and uprooted a few trees.
A weak tornado crossed the Mississippi River back into Tennessee.  A few tree limbs were broken and trees were uprooted before the tornado lifted south of the Hatchie River northwest of Gilt Edge.

Tornado touched down in southern Lauderdale County and tracked northeast toward Ripley, lifting before reaching the town. Large tree limbs were broken and a few trees were uprooted. There was minor roof damage to one home.
Heavy rain resulted in water on area roadways. A young motorist died as a result of hydroplaning.
Trees were knocked down throughout the county along with some power lines. Eight homes were damaged.
Two tractor trailer trucks were blown over on Highway 278. Trees and power lines down across the county. Four roads were closed. Thirteen homes were damaged.

Winds caused roof damage to many structures along with numerous trees down. County Road 600 was especially hard hit. There were 17 homes damaged around the county. Twenty roads were closed and one business was damaged. A wind gust of 74 mph was measured by a spotter about 5 miles southeast of Ripley.

Damaging straight line winds blew for 20-25 minutes across Lee County. The ASOS at the Tupelo airport measured a gust of 60 mph at 1046 am LST and then a 71 mph gust at 1108 am LST. Numerous trees were knocked down across the county. There was structural damage to the former Tupelo Automotive Museum and a local salon.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines across Prentiss County. Ten homes were damaged as well.

Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines throughout Alcorn County. Some homes suffered shingle damage in Corinth. Signs were also blown down and large tree branches fell on a mobile home in Rienzi.
Measured gust of 70 mph at the RAWS site near Iuka. Numerous trees and power lines down across the county.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down due to straight line winds. A few trees fell on homes.
Straight line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines. Four homes were damaged and 20 roads were closed.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Hardin County. Numerous houses and structures around the county were damaged.

Straight line winds caused significant damage across McNairy County.  880 homes were damaged and 21 homes were destroyed. Trees and power lines were knocked down across the county. Adamsville was the hardest hit area of the county while Milledgeville and Miche also sustained damage. A man was killed by a falling tree in Milledgeville.

Straight line winds caused significant damage across Decatur County. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down around the county. A 300 foot tower buckled and fell north of Decaturville. A large tree fell on a trailer home and car in rural Decatur County. A woman was critically injured. Numerous homes and structures around the county were damaged.

Seven tractor trailer trucks were blown over on the I-40 bridge over the Tennessee River. In addition, numerous trees and power lines were knocked down across the county.  Several homes and a few structures around the county were damaged.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down throughout the county. Several homes and structures around the county were damaged.

Snow accumulations of four inches fell in Pocahontas and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of four inches fell in Paragould and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of four to six inches fell in Wynne and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of four to five inches fell in Piggott and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of five to six inches fell in Forrest City, Wheatley and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of five inches fell in Lynn and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of five to six inches fell in Jonesboro, Bay and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of eight inches fell in Fisher and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of six inches fell in Marvel and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of nine to ten inches fell in Marianna and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to the snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of six to seven inches fell in Kennett and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to snow covered roadways.
Snow accumulations of seven inches fell in Bragg City and surrounding areas. Numerous accidents were reported across the county due to snow covered roadways.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Madison Avenue and Belvedere Boulevard in Midtown Memphis.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in the 1100 Block of White Station Road in East Memphis.
Straight line winds knocked down trees on New Castle Road and Hickory Valley Road.
A barn was destroyed and a few homes sustained roof damage in the Maud community. Six or seven utility poles were down along Highway 61 west of Dubbs.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and damaged some vinyl siding, shingles and awnings.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on county roads in Craighead County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on county roads in Greene County making the roads impassable.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on Highway 1 South, south of Harrisburg.
Straight line winds blew a trailer over and a carport in Batesville. In addition, a few signs were knocked down.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Downtown Batesville. Water flooded a few homes.
A weak tornado crossed the Mississippi River and then crossed into Tipton County.
Numerous roads in Camden were flooded due to heavy rainfall.
Shed destroyed near the Highway 7 and Highway 9 split.
Part of a metal roof peeled back on a home in Water Valley.
Trees were knocked down and there was structural damage to a building near Highway 9 and County Road 174.
A short-lived tornado knocked down trees along County Road 481 south of Calhoun City. Peak wind estimated at 80 mph.

The first damage was observed to trees along Highway 348. The tornado was intermittently on the ground for the first six miles of its track, causing sporadic tree damage. The tornado intensified as it crossed County Road 172, with trees uprooted. As the tornado crossed Highway 9, several structures were damaged. Some were damaged by falling trees. Trees were also uprooted or trunks snapped. The last damage was observed along County Road 174 east of Highway 9. A total of 12 homes suffered damage. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.

The first damage was observed to trees along Euclatubba Road, south of Highway 348.  The tornado crossed Highway 348, damaging additional trees. The first structural damage occurred to homes along County Road 833. The tornado then moved into a residential area. Numerous homes suffered roof and window damage, and a few had garage doors blown out. Two homes suffered nearly complete roof removal. The tornado destroyed a church of metal construction along Mitchell St. then crossed Highway 45 and caused additional tree damage. The tornado then crossed Pratts Road about 3 miles east of Highway 45. The tornado damaged a silo, a home and a storage shed along Highway 370, and caused additional tree damage before dissipating in northeastern Lee County. A total of 37 homes suffered damage. Peak winds were estimated at 115 mph.
This brief, weak tornado damaged trees just north of the Natchez Trace Parkway to the southeast of Guntown. Peak winds were estimated at 70 mph.

A brief tornado touched down near County Road 4101 and Mississippi Highway 4. Trees were knocked down. A barn roof was removed and there was damage to a carport and a few sheds. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

The damage began on Mississippi Highway 25 extending northeast to Mississippi Highway 30. Mainly tree damage was observed along the path. Thirteen homes suffered damage along with three businesses. Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph.
A barn was damaged and car windows were blown out.
Two trees fell on a vehicle in Union City due to gradient wind.
Seven tractor trailers were blown over on Interstate 40 between mile markers 222 and 225 near Wheatley.
Windows were blown out southeast of Wynne.
Powerlines were knocked down.
Powerlines were knocked down.
Straight-line winds resulted in some structural and roof damage to buildings in Dell.
Powerlines were knocked down in Victoria.
Several homes and mobile homes sustained significant damage. Numerous trees were knocked down across the Joiner.
A tree was knocked down and a window was blown out in Burdette.
The siding was stripped from part of a house in Wilson.
Straight-line winds snapped and uprooted trees in Tiptonville.
Powerlines were knocked down at Oak and Elm Streets in Marion.
Some roads were impassable due to flash flooding. Two feet of water covered Richardson Drive in East Jonesboro.
Straight-line winds caused significant damage to a mobile home at Midway Lake.
Straight-line winds damaged several homes and barns in Elaine.
Numerous trees were uprooted and knocked down in the Fowlkes area. One carport was severely damaged and one home sustained minor roof damage.
A mobile home was damaged and three homes sustained minor damage on Bellview Road.
Approximately two dozen utility poles were knocked down across the road on President's Island.

Thunderstorm winds moved across Tunica, MS and areas south and east of the community. Several industrial buildings were damaged south of town. The Tunica AWOS recorded a peak wind gust of 79 mph. East of the airport, an apartment roof, mobile home, and a large storage shed were damaged. In total, across Tunica County, there were four homes damaged, four businesses damaged and 17 farms damaged. There was widespread tree damage along with two injuries.  A tractor-trailer was also blown over.
A farm building suffered roof damage and outbuildings were damaged in Tutwiler.  Trees were knocked down and a mobile home was damaged as well.
An elementary school and a home suffered roof damage in Sumner.

The tornado developed just east of Highway 49E, approximately 2.4 miles west-northwest of Sumner, causing damage to a grain bin. Moving to the northeast, the tornado damaged a barn and derailed 30 train cars near Tutwiler Road. Sporadic tree damage was observed along the path. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph. A total of 30 homes were damaged by straight-line winds and this tornado on this date across mainly western sections of Tallahatchie County.
Trees were snapped and uprooted in Como.
Large tree limbs were knocked down west of Denton.
Straight-line winds damaged several homes and commercial buildings in Lambert. Numerous trees were knocked down or damaged.
Straight-line winds caused structural damage to buildings along Summer Avenue. Roofing was blown off, damaging nearby vehicles.

A farm building was destroyed and spread southeast to the intersection of Key Road and Ebenezer Road.  Numerous trees and powerlines were knocked down in the area.  This damage was linked to the straight-line winds associated with the tornado that tracked just north of this area.

Several barns and outbuildings were severely damaged or destroyed by the tornado. There was also tree damage as well as roof damage to homes. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.  There was also a substantial area of straight-line wind damage.
Straight-line winds damaged a utility pole and knocked down large tree limbs on Prichard Road in western Tate County.
Trees were knocked down at the Baptist College of Health Sciences along Union Avenue.
The tornado touched down near the Arkabutla community and damaged trees then tracked northeast across Arkabutla lake and crossed into DeSoto County.  One home suffered minor damage.

The tornado tracked across Arkabutla Lake and damaged trees and sheds at the Hernando Point Park. The tornado caused additional tree damage, and damage to roofs, as it approached Highway 51. Damage to residences and storage buildings was observed as it crossed Highway 51. The tornado dissipated just east of Interstate 55. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph. A total of 210 homes were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across DeSoto County.
Straight-line winds knocked down numerous trees south of the tornado track in southern DeSoto County, just north of Arkabutla Lake.
Multiple trees were knocked down south of Hernando along I-55 near McCracken Road.
Several trees were uprooted or snapped along County Road 304.
Several large trees were knocked down along East Parkway near Overton Park. One large tree fell on an apartment complex and caused extensive damage.
Several trees were uprooted on Getwell Road southeast of Hernando.

The tornado touched down near the intersection of Eason and Jamison Roads, causing significant damage to two mobile homes. The tornado damaged another mobile home and an outbuilding on Bill Locke Road before crossing into Panola County. Peak winds were estimated at 105 mph.

This tornado crossed from Quitman County into Panola County. The tornado continued northeast, damaging numerous homes along Waldrup Road in western Panola County. The tornado dissipated east of Nash Road after crossing Highway 278. A total of 50 homes were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across Panola County.
Straight-line winds south of the tornado track caused significant damage to a small professional building and minor damage to a home on Bill Locke Road near the intersection of Jamison Road.
Straight-line winds damaged an outbuilding and knocked down some trees near the intersection of Locke Station and Jamison Roads.
Straight-line winds damaged outbuildings along Macedonia Road.
Straight-line winds knocked down large tree limbs on Highway 304.

This tornado developed just south of Interstate 269 northeast of Hernando. The tornado initially damaged trees and signs as it crossed I-269. The tornado strengthened as it crossed Craft Road. The tornado heavily damaged a stable and a large metal storage building and then crossed into residential areas east of Craft Road. Numerous homes were damaged, with some sustaining significant damage. The tornado continued northeast, causing minor roof damage, and dissipated near the intersection of Bethel Road and Interstate 22. Strong straight-line winds caused additional damage just south of the tornado track.  Peak winds were estimated at 120 mph.  A total of 210 homes were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across DeSoto County.
Straight-line winds snapped power poles south of Dunn Lane East Road to the south of the tornado track.
Gas station awning was destroyed in Courtland.
Several trees and power lines were knocked down in the Strayhorn area.
Large trees were knocked down on Braden Road and Highway 59. Four utility poles were knocked down at the Mason substation on Gainesville Road.
Trees were snapped and uprooted west of Millington.
Large tree limbs were knocked down on Highway 310 west of Como.

The tornado began near County Road 310 and Rooks Road in Panola County, damaging numerous trees as it moved northeast. A few barns sustained significant damage on Partee Road. The tornado then continued into Tate County. The peak winds were estimated at 75 mph. A total of 50 homes were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across Panola County.
The tornado crossed from Panola County into Tate County. A few trees were damaged in Tate County before the tornado lifted near Barlow Road.

The tornado began near Highway 4 and Muse Road, damaging trees and a couple of manufactured homes. Additional tree damage was observed north of Highway 4 along Mt. Gilead Road and along Old Highway 4 from Yarbough Chapel to McIntyre Church Road. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
A few power poles were knocked down along County Road 101 near County Road 104.

This brief tornado developed just west of Duscoe Road southeast of Williston. The tornado uprooted trees and caused minor damage to a residence as it crossed Duscoe Road. Along Ebenezer Loop, the tornado caused minor damage to a mobile home and uprooted trees. The final damage was noted along Mount Pisgah Road. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
Straight-line winds caused damage to roofs and knocked down trees and utility poles in Greenfield.
A brief tornado touched down destroying outbuildings and sheds. A few trees were knocked down. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph.
Straight-line winds caused structural damage to a few homes in the Gleason area. A few trees were knocked down as well.
Straight-line winds caused significant damage to a mobile home in Mrytle.
A metal roof was peeled off a home two miles north of Calhoun City.
Straight-line winds resulted in minor damage to barns and trees in Walnut and Chalybeate. Trees were knocked down at Highway 15 and County Road 306.
Straight-line winds damaged a carport and storage buildings.
Straight-line winds knocked down trees and power lines across McNairy County.
Trees and power lines were knocked down across Alcorn County.
Roads blocked by downed trees across Henry County. There were scattered power outages.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down near Westport Road and Highway 22 and along Davis Chapel Road.
Numerous trees and power lines knocked down. A barn was damaged.

Numerous large trees were uprooted in Bruceton. Two trees fell on a house and another tree fell on an outbuilding. Fences were damaged throughout the town and business signs were folded over on US 70.
Large tree limbs were knocked down on Highway 348.
Large tree limbs were knocked down just south of the tornado track.
Straight-line winds caused minor damage to a house on County Road 5011 south of Wheeler.  Small tree limbs were also broken in the area.
The tornado developed in far northwestern Lee where it damaged trees and several commercial buildings as it crossed Highway 45. The tornado then crossed Highway 370 into Prentiss County.

This tornado tracked from Lee County. Many trees were uprooted in Baldwyn, with a few trees falling on houses. The tornado damaged the roof of the high school and an industrial building on the northeast side of town. The last observed damage was to trees south of the Wheeler community. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph. A total of 54 homes and five apartments were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across Prentiss County.

The first damage was observed in the Hurricane Creek vicinity. As the tornado crossed County Road 5040, it damaged a large barn, two mobile homes, and a residence. The tornado damaged additional mobile homes along County Road 3040 and damaged several buildings at a lumber processing facility. The last damage was observed along County Road 1371.  Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph. A total of 54 homes and five apartments were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across Prentiss County.

This tornado produced minor roof damage and uprooted trees along County Road 1401. It damaged trees along Highway 356 to the west of Highway 365. The tornado then crossed into Tishomingo County. A total of 54 homes and five apartments were damaged by tornadoes and straight-line winds on this date across Prentiss County.

The tornado strengthened as it crossed into Tishomingo County from Prentiss County causing its most significant damage along Highway 365. The tornado damaged several homes and storage buildings before dissipating near the Tennessee-Tombigbee Waterway. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
This brief tornado caused minor damage to a residence. It also damaged trees and power poles along Highway 72, Highway 172 and County Road 164. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
A downed tree caused significant damage to a porch in Golden.
A residence was flooded in Nettleton.
Jefferson Street was flooded and impassable. Water flooded yards along the street.
A residence was flooded on Old Highway 78 in Fulton. Two cars were flooded as well.
Straight-line winds damaged a home in Chickasaw County.

Several roads were flooded across Monroe County especially from Amory to Smithville. Up to 30 roads were flooded and some were washed out and damaged across Monroe County. Firetower Road in the Parham area suffered the worst damage and Smithville Road was also damaged. Ten apartment units were damaged by flooding in Amory.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding across parts of Chickasaw County. A total of 10 roads were damaged across the county.
A car turned over in floodwaters on Homestead Road in Prairie with passengers inside. Passengers were rescued.
Power lines and trees knocked down across Monroe County. One tree fell on the mobile home.
Trees were knocked down in Parsons. There was also some minor roof damage.
Straight-line winds caused roof damage and downed trees on Highway 178 and County Road 203.
Trees down on Highway 365 between Burton and Cairo.
Straight-line winds knocked down a few trees across central parts of Tishomingo County including the town of Tishomingo.
Straight-line winds knocked down a few trees across southern Tishomingo County including the town of Belmont.
Several roads were closed in the Hatley area due to flooding.
Heavy rain resulted in flooding that closed roads between Okolona and Houston. A sinkhole developed on County Road 215 between Okolona and Houston.
A semi-truck hauling a mobile home was traveling north on Highway 61 just north of Clarksdale and was overturned due to strong crosswinds.
Power line knocked down at the intersection of Highway 6 and 334.
Bank sign blown over near the intersection of North Main Street and Highway 145.
Nickel size hail fell throughout Jonesboro.
Quarter to golfball size hail fell in the Leachville area.

Damage to homes and mobile homes was observed from just west of Highway 45E to Highway 105 near the Gibson-Carroll County line. Numerous trees were also damaged along this path. The most significant damage was observed along Gann Road between Goosefoot and Belews Chapel Road. Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph.
Straight-line winds knocked over an empty rail car.

The tornado formed just southwest of the Carroll County Airport and moved east, crossing Highway 77 near the intersection with Highway 219. The tornado lifted near Highway 114 near Allen Creek.  Numerous trees were knocked down along the tornado path. Several houses, barns, and grain bins were damaged. The worst damage was on Chapel Hill Road.  Peak winds were estimated at 125 mph.
Power lines were knocked down in McKenzie.

The tornado started in Benton County northwest of Camden and caused a substantial amount of tree damage along the path the extended into the Tennessee River. Several homes and mobile homes were damaged along the path in Benton County. The most damage, in Benton County, was in the Ballard Road area. Peak winds were estimated around 125 mph. The tornado then moved across the Tennessee River and into Humphreys County.
Large tree branches were broken.
Straight-line winds snapped trees on Highway 190.
Half dollar size hail fell at Natchez Trace State Park.
Hail up to the size of quarters fell on Highway 351.
Lee County Road 215 closed due to a washout between County Road 242 and County Road 248.
Nickel size hail reported between Senath and Kennett.

The tornado developed in western Tishomingo County and was intermittently on the ground as it moved through the Paden Overlook Area and crossed Mackeys Creek. More continuous damage occurred as the tornado crossed County Road 118 west of Tishomingo. As the tornado moved through the northern portions of Tishomingo, it caused substantial damage to a retail store.  Several buildings in town suffered minor damage and trees were uprooted. As the tornado moved east, it damaged homes, storage buildings, mobile homes, and uprooted trees along County Roads 116, 116 Extended, 106, and State Highway 30. In total, 55 residential homes and four commercial buildings were damaged in Tishomingo Couty.  Peak winds were estimated at 110 mph in Tishomingo County. The tornado crossed into Colbert County, Alabama, just north of the Natchez Trace Parkway.

This tornado developed just north of I-555 and west of Caraway Road. The tornado quickly intensified and caused EF2 damage near the intersection of Caraway Rd. and Race St. The tornado weakened slightly, but produced EF2 damage again at the Mall at Turtle Creek. The tornado reached its most intense stage as it approached and moved across the Jonesboro Airport. Several large industrial buildings were severely damaged. As the tornado moved through residential areas northeast of the airport, it caused EF2 to isolated EF3 damage to homes. The tornado began weakening after it crossed Highway 49 northeast of Jonesboro, with the final damage observed to the northeast of Brookland. Peak winds were estimated at 150 mph.

This tornado developed south of U.S. Highway 412 and west of County Road 934. The tornado overturned a center pivot irrigation system. As it crossed Highway 412, it damaged an industrial building and a grain bin. West of Highway 119, the tornado damaged trees, storage buildings, and a mobile home. The last damage was observed to trees along Highway 119.  Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.
A few trees were knocked down across eastern Shelby County.
Straight-line winds uprooted trees east of Ripley.
Straight-line winds knocked down a few trees around Fayette County.  The damage was mostly focused on Oakland. Winds broke 12 power poles in Oakland with multiple power lines down.
Power lines were knocked down in Fairview.
Straight-line winds knocked a tree down on to a house on Pleasant Springs Road near Chickasaw State Park. Power lines were knocked down also.
A spotter measured a 65 mph gust. Trees were knocked down on Highway 104 North.
Trees were knocked down in Puryear.
Large hail fell across parts of southern Panola County. Hail up to the size of ping pong balls fell on Tocowa Road.
Several trees and power lines were knocked down in Holladay.
Trees and power lines were knocked down across Henderson County.
Straight-line winds damaged a barn roof and knocked down a few trees on Hobby Coop Road.
Straight-line winds caused significant damage to trees and structures in the Farville curve and Rogers Chapel Road area.
Straight-line winds caused damage near Colt on Highway 306.
Trees and power lines were knocked down.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell in Crawfordsville.
Nickel to golf ball size hail fell in Olive Branch.
Penny size hail fell at the intersection of Hacks Cross Road and Highway 302 in Olive Branch.
Quarter to half dollar size hail fell along Interstate 40 in West Memphis covering the ground.
Penny size hail fell near Key Road.
Quarter size hail fell 3 miles west of Interstate 55.
Penny size hail covering ground in the Rockford Subdivision near the intersection of Old Brownsville Road and Ellendale Road.
Nickel size hail fell in Shelby Forest.
Nickel size hail fell at the intersection of Old Brownsville Road and Austin Peay Highway.
Penny size hail cracked a picture window and a windshield near Lepanto.

Straight line winds blew trees and 25 power lines down near Robinsonville in the Casino Strip to Casino Center area. Significant damage occurred to the canopies of two gas stations as well as a car wash outbuilding. A tractor was overturned near the Casino Factory Shoppes off of Highway 61. In addition, damage occurred to an irrigation system.
Penny size hail fell in Jacks Creek.
Nickel size hail reported in Sweet Lips.
Large tree was knocked down in Milledgeville.
A brief tornado touched down and damaged a farm building.
The tornado tracked predominately through farm fields. A trailer home was destroyed in the Claypool area and homes were damaged and destroyed on the north side of Harrisburg.
Quarter size hail reported on the south side of Jonesboro.
Irregularly shaped hail up to 2 inches in diameter fell in Knob.
Penny size hail fell near Campbell Street in North Jackson.

Numerous trees were blown down east and southeast of Somerville including Country Club Road, Jernigan Drive, Lagrange Road and Rehoboth Road. A house lost some shingles on Country Club Cove. A few other trees were blown down across portions of Fayette County.
Tree down across County Road 200 in Falkner just off Highway 15.
Multiple trees and power lines were knocked down from Eastview to Michie.
A few shingles were ripped off a house in Corinth. Trees were knocked down in Farmington.
A downed tree fell through a window in a home in Counce.
Half dollar size hail fell near Counce at Highway 57 and Highway 142.
Porch was blown off a home on County Road 238 north of Iuka. A large tree was knocked down on a home along County Road 239.
A tree was knocked down blocking the road near Hendrix Road and Old Jackson Store Road.
Nickel size hail fell near Arp and Lightfoot Luckett Road.
A tree was knocked down on a vehicle in Somerville.
Apartment complex in Como was extensively flooded. Sandbags were required. Depth of water was about 6 inches.
Scattered trees down in New Albany.
A porch was damaged and a metal roof was pulled off a garage in Booneville.
Numerous trees were knocked down from Burnt Church through Pyburns, Counce and Olivet.

Straight line winds caused extensive damage across the Clarksdale area. A car wash suffered significant roof damage.  A large section of the roof of a hotel was ripped off. There was widespread tree damage across the city of Clarksdale and into Lyon. Several homes were damaged by fallen trees.
Trees were knocked down at Friars Point.
Tree down along Highway 261 west of Caldwell.

Straight line winds caused extensive damage across the Helena-West Helena area. Power poles and trees were knocked down across the city. Multiple buildings downtown were damaged or destroyed including Centennial Baptist Church which sustained significant damage.
Straight line winds damaged or destroyed 15 to 20 homes across Panola County. Numerous trees were knocked down. One fatality occurred when trees fell on a mobile home.
A power pole was snapped and a couple of power poles were knocked over along Highway 32 east of Charleston.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down across DeSoto County.
Three homes were damaged across Tate County. Power lines were knocked down near the Looxahoma community.
Multiple trees down across the entire county. Several trees were knocked down on houses and structures. A person was briefly trapped inside a house due to a fallen tree.
Trees were knocked down along Highway 149 south of Earle, blocking the road.
Trees and power lines were knocked down in Banner. Power meter was knocked off a house.
Numerous trees down in the city of Oxford and across Lafayette County as well. Five homes were damaged across the county.
Multiple trees were knocked down in Bruce.
A large tree was knocked down at the intersection of Walnut Grove Road and Highland Street.
Multiple trees down on Highway 336 west of Pontotoc. A half dozen trees were knocked down on Anderson Road in eastern section of Pontotoc County.
Large tree down across Highway 32. Four roads closed due to debris across county.
Multiple trees down in the community of Alpine.
Multiple trees down across the county.
Trees were knocked down on power lines in Guntown.
A tree was knocked down on County Road 814 in Plantersville.
Numerous trees and large branches down west of Greenwood Springs.
A large tree was knocked down on Highway 22 near Hamburg Road.
Lightning hit a house on Penmont Drive. The strike blew out the walls in an upstairs bedroom. The electric sockets were blown out of the walls in another room.
A couple of trees were knocked down on County Road 168 in Dumas.
Trees and power lines down on County Road 552.
Metal outbuilding destroyed and large tree uprooted along Highway 1 south of Forrest City.
Tree knocked down in Senath.
Carport flipped and thrown across the yard.
A large tree was blown into a home on Park Avenue in Jonesboro. Residents were trapped inside with minor injuries.
Straight-line winds ripped a roof off a building and knocked a valve off a 30,000-gallon propane tank located at Front Street and Pecan Street in Wynne.
Several trees knocked down in Palestine.
Power lines down near WJ Freeman Park and Stage Road in Bartlett.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down across the county.
A large tree fell into a house due to lightning. The tree knocked several windows out of the home.
Straight line winds blew debris down on a roadway near Tulane Road and Fogg Road.
Straight line winds blew down power lines near the intersection of Highway 61 and Star Landing Road in Lake Cormorant.
Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down on Sawmill Road outside of Winborn. In addition, several trees were knocked down on Highway 5 between Pine Grove and Ashland.
Penny size hail fell in Hernando Town Square.
Straight line winds blew trees down on the west and south side of Hernando.
Quarter size hail fell near Highway 51 and Interstate 69.

Straight line winds destroyed T&T Grocery on Highway 4 West in Jumpertown.  A barn received damage when debris from the T&T Grocery fell on the barn's roof. Crossroads United Methodist Church also sustained damage to the church's front porch and steeple. Several trees were knocked down near Jumpertown as well.
Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down along County Roads 7350 and 7000.
Straight line winds damaged the roof of the Mississippi Cabinet Company on Highway 145 North near Frankstown. In addition, trees were knocked down in the area.
Straight line winds blew trees and power lines down on County Roads 3011 and 3321.
Straight line winds blew power lines down near Potts Camp.
Quarter size hail fell in Jumpertown covering the ground.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding at the intersection of Raleigh-LaGrange Road and Sycamore View Road. In addition, 2 to 3 inches of water were over the roadways in the Sycamore View Apartment Complex.
Utility pole snapped along County Road 140.
A tree was knocked down on power lines on SW 3rd Street in Corning.
Trees were knocked down across Malden.
Numerous trees were knocked down across Piggott.
A few trees were knocked down in Rector.
Tree down on Highway 141 near Ebenezer.
A carport was damaged four miles northeast of Jonesboro.
A wind gust of 60 mph reported in Bono.
Tree down on Sage Meadows Golf Course.
Large tree branches were broken in Tiptonville. Winds estimated near 70 mph.
Uprooted trees damaged six homes in Caruthersville.
Straight-line winds caused roof damage and trees down three miles southeast of Holcomb.

The roof was ripped off a real estate building and landed on the post office. There was debris collected around and between buildings at Washington Avenue and South 2nd Street. Trees were knocked down with one large tree blocking South 4th Street and Church Street.
Several trees down.
Trees down across South Fulton.
Numerous trees down and a shed damaged outside of Martin.
Trees damaged and power lines down near Mockingbird Lane.
Mulitple trees and powerlines down in Martin.
Power lines were knocked down at the intersection of Highway 18 and Highway 312 between Dell and Gosnell.
Tree limbs down and shingles ripped off a roof north of Martin.
Thunderstorm wind gust measured on a home anemometer.
Straight line winds blew three trees down in Paragould.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Sharon.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down in Dresden. An office building in Dresden suffered roof damage.
Tree knocked down across the road in Ripley near Highway 51.
Numerous trees down in Greenfield.
Power lines knocked down and blocking roads near a car dealership.
A tree fell on a house on Mt. Zion road near Gleason.
Trees knocked down at Highway 54 and Highway 190 near Como.
Multiple trees knocked down in McKenzie.
Tree knocked down across Highway 152 and Christmasville Road.
Four trees were knocked down in Three Way.
Numerous trees and power poles snapped between Paris and McKenzie. A tree fell on a house in Paris.
Several trees and power lines were knocked down in Huntingdon.
A tree fell on a house near JMC General Hospital.
A spotter measured a 62 mph gust in Big Sandy.
Trees and power lines were knocked down in the Bruceton and Hollow Rock area. A power pole fell on a house on Lankford Lane in Bruceton.
Multiple trees down and power poles snapped in the Camden and Big Sandy areas. Trees down across the county.
A large tree was knocked down in Brownsville.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down across the northern half of Henderson County. A carport was blown into power lines on Highway 412 near Lexington.
Multiple trees were knocked down in Cedar Grove.
A tree was knocked down across the road on Highway 22 near Edge Road on the eastern side of Chester County.
A utility pole was snapped on Highway 641 north of Parsons and trees were knocked down across town.
Part of a metal roof was pulled off a home in Decaturville and numerous trees were knocked down across town. A portion of the roof was removed at Fisherdale Marina.
A tree was knocked on to a vehicle.
Trees were knocked down on Barker Drive.
A large tree was uprooted on Lonesome Pine Road near Olive Hill.
Penny size hail fell near Germantown Road and Old Brownsville Road.
Quarter size hail fell on Perry Switch Road.
Half dollar size hail fell along the Gibson and Crockett County border.
Golf ball size hail fell at Tigrett Grocery in eastern Dyer County.
Nickel size fell near Rocky Springs Road and Ed Moore Road.
Ping pong ball size hail fell near Crockett Mills.
Quarter size hail fell near Glendale Road and Shae Lane.
Ping pong size hail fell in Oakfield.
Hail sized from quarters to golf balls fell on the south side of Jonesboro.
Hail up to the size of quarters fell just southeast of Lepanto.

A macroburst struck portions of Dunklin County with widespread wind damage from Campbell to Clarkton. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. There was significant damage to a building in Campbell.  A warehouse suffered major damage in Clarkton and a center pivot irrigation system was overturned. The Lynn Oak Church also suffered damage.  A train was derailed along Highway 62 near the Arkansas state line, closing the highway.

The macroburst that struck Dunklin and caused widespread damage in southern New Madrid County then spread into northern Pemiscot County causing widespread damage in Wardell. Trees fell on houses. Numerous power lines were knocked down. A mobile home was blown over and several buildings were damaged.  Several homes suffered roof damage.

A macroburst struck eastern Clay County with damaging winds.  Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down from Pollard to Piggott continuing to the Missouri state line.  A commercial building roof was damaged near Piggott. Several homes suffered roof damage.
Straight-line winds caused widespread damage across the Caruthersville area. Trees and power poles were snapped.
Wind-driven hail caused significant damage to structures and roofs in Caruthersville.

A macroburst spread from eastern Clay County into Dunklin County causing widespread damage, especially in the Kennett area.  Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. Several awnings, carports, and sheds were blown down.
Large trees were knocked down.
Trees were knocked down in Bogata.

A macroburst struck southern portions of Lake County causing widespread damage. Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down. A mobile home was destroyed in Ridgely. Many homes in the Cottonwood area suffered roof damaged.
Quarter size hail fell on Christmasville Road near the Madison County line.
Trees uprooted south of Dyersburg.
Large tree limbs were snapped in Newbern and a church steeple blown off.
A large tree fell on a house.
Quarter size hail fell in northeast Madison County.
A tree fell on a house on Sand Ridge Bargerton Road near Highway 412 west of Lexington.  Twenty-eight trees were knocked down on one property west of Lexington.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding in southern Gibson County.  Intersections were flooded in Humbdolt and water was high enough to stall cars. Significant street flooding occurred in Medina. Pleasant Hill road was flooded.
Narrow Gauge road was cracked and partially washed out due to flash flooding.
Trees were knocked down in Fair Oaks along Highway 49. A power pole was snapped along Highway 49 near Fair Oaks.
Attached carport was destroyed along Highway 193 South.
Numerous trees were knocked down in Wynne.
The public measured a 58 mph gust near Highway 64 and County Road 401 west of Parkin.
A grain bin was damaged along Highway 64.
Damaged occurred across Earle. The roof was partially torn off the high school. Trees were uprooted and snapped. Power lines were knocked down across town. A large tree fell on a trailer and car.
A camper was flipped over near mile marker 12 on Interstate 55.
A roof was taken off a barn near Dacus Road in West Memphis. Grain bins were also damaged.
Trees were knocked down along Central Avenue in Memphis.  A tree landed on a car on Holmes Street.
Trees were knocked down near Shelby Forest. A couple of houses were damaged by fallen trees.
Trees and power lines were knocked down on Shadowlawn Road in Bartlett near the Bartlett Freshman Academy. Trees were uprooted and snapped near Lakeland and shingles were blown off a roof.
Numerous trees down around Arlington. Some homes had shingles removed. Power lines down across Airline Road.
Power poles were broken with numerous trees down.
A large tree fell on a home on Forked Deer Road.
A weak tornado knocked down numerous trees northeast of Trenton. Peak winds were estimated at 70 mph.
Penny size hail observed in the Fisherville area.

A weak tornado touched down on Leach Road and traveled southeast crossing Purdy Road and Poplar Springs Road near the Thousand Lakes Community. The tornado continued southeast toward Highway 114 where two homes suffered roof damage. Trees were uprooted and snapped along the path, but overall damage was intermittent along the track. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down along Highway 178 southeast of Myrtle.
Straight-line winds damaged the roof of a gas station at the intersection of Poplar Avenue and Collierville-Arlington Road.
Trees and powerlines knocked down across the Memphis area.
Trees and powerlines knocked down on Plantation Way.
Quarter size hail fell between Earle and Parkin.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down near I-55 south of Hernando.
Several trees knocked down in Senatobia. One fell on a home causing minor damage.
Powerlines knocked down at Sebastian Street and Plaza Avenue. Tree knocked down on Park Street.
Extensive tree damage across the city of Batesville. A tree fell on a house in Batesville near Court Street.
Straight-line winds damaged a storefront in Oxford.
Trees knocked down between Blue Springs and Sherman.
Part of a roof blown off a convenience store at Enid Lake.
A house suffered roof damage and a large tree was uprooted in Sherman.
Roof damage at a grocery store on the Union County line along Highway 348.
Numerous trees down in Saltillo.
Trees knocked down across Pontotoc County.
Trees and powerlines down at County Road 931 and County Road 885.
Numerous trees and powerlines knocked down.
Several large trees down in town.
Trees down across Shannon, Brewer, and Auburn.
An oak tree was knocked down across a back yard in Amory.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Charleston. Water was deep enough on North Market Street to cover the hood of a car.
One to two feet of water covered parts of the Hamlet subdivision in southeast Oxford near Lamar Boulevard and Mimosa Drive.
Miller Road was closed between Bethel Road and Highway 178 due to flooding.
Fleming Road flooded between Shelby Drive and Collierville Road. Shelby Drive flooded between Houston Levee Road and Quinn Road.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down on Springdale Road.
Vehicles were stranded in floodwaters. Water rescues were necessary.
Multiple trees down in Benton County near Sulphur Creek Road and Hicks Road south of Big Sandy.
Straight line winds knocked over a large bank sign near Wal-Mart in Paragould.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines near the Greene County Technical Institute along Highway 412 west of Paragould.
Straight line winds turned over a Cessna airplane at the Paragould Airport. Power poles were also knocked down in the area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on roads in Egypt.
Straight line winds damaged a few transformers near Interstate 55 about 4 miles south of Holland.
Straight line winds knocked down several telephone poles and damaged a few transformers in Yarbro.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines in Wynne.
The roof and carport of a house located on Red Haven Drive in Forrest City were damaged by straight line winds. Numerous power lines were knocked down across the city as well.
Straight line winds broke several large branches off several trees in Brickeys.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Osceola.
Straight line winds knocked down trees along Highway 306 in Coldwater.
Straight line winds blew a tree onto a home near Edith. A convenience store on Highway 51 sustained damage to an awning from the winds as well.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding and as a result Highway 69 was closed about 3 miles west of Trumann.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding around the Jonesboro Airport. The Airport Road, Neil Road, Aggie Road and Stadium Road were all closed due to flooding.
Straight line winds knocked trees down across Henry County. One tree fell on a house on Myatt Road. A roof of a barn was also blown off near Paris.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Senatobia. Highway 51 and Norfleet drive were flooded. Minor flooding was reported at the Northwest Mississippi Community College Campus.
Straight line winds knocked down trees in Westport.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on many streets in Tiptonville.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Imboden. Highway 62 and Highway 63 were closed due to flooding.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding in northwest Clay County. Highway 211 from Old Highway 67 to the Missouri state line was closed due to flooding. Numerous county roads were flooded in the Success area.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 63 between Portia and Ravenden. Three feet of water covered the road in spots.

Significant flooding near the intersection of Highway 69 and Highway 226.
Christmasville Road was completely washed out between Oakfield and Watson Roads. Up to one foot of water covered Christmasville Road near Bermuda Road and Northeast Middle School.
Highway 45 is closed at Ozier Road near Pinson due to flooding.
State Route 198 closed in both directions between Hillcrest Circle Drive and Paul Coffman Drive due to flooding.
Part of the road in the 800 block of Simmons Road caved in. The road was closed to all traffic.
Several feet of water covered Forty Forks Road near Bethel Springs.

A levee broke outside of Selmer toward Purdy which, when combined with very heavy rainfall of up to eight inches, resulted in widespread flash flooding.  Twenty people were rescued. Ten homes and 50 businesses were flooded and damaged.  Roads and bridges were also damaged.
Homes were flooded in Okolona.
The White Rock Road and Egypt Road area was flooded.  Water rescues were needed to evacuate residents from their homes.
County Road 506 under the Natchez Trace Parkway was flooded. Two vehicles were stalled in the water.
A house on County Road 152 was flooded with a family trapped inside. The family was rescued safely.
County Roads 102, 103, and 47 were flooded in southern Union County.

Flash flooding occurred in Ecru. A woman was rescued from a residence while another woman was stuck in her residence due to a flooded driveway. Several cars were stranded in the water.  Water was over the hood of vehicles in some areas.
A brief landspout tornado touched down in an open field with no damage.

Straight-line winds knocked down trees and powerlines on the southwest side of Jonesboro. A large tree fell on a house on Anne Street trapping people inside. Sanderson Street was blocked by a fallen tree.
Minor siding damage and several tree limbs down in Marked Tree.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down south of Millington from South Lucy Road to Pleasant Ridge Road.
Trees and power lines down from Kossuth to Hinkle.
Straight-line winds caused significant tree and power pole damage on Highway 45 near Kenton. Upwards of 25 power poles were knocked down or were significantly leaning. A barn was destroyed.
Trees knocked down across northern Madison County. A tree fell on a home off Old Humboldt Road.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in Benton County.  Water and debris from Little Sulphur Creek flooded the bridge on Sulphur Creek Road. Danville Road was completely covered in water near Big Sandy.
Tree limbs and debris on I-55 near Jericho and one power pole snapped in half.
Straight-line winds knocked down a tree on a home and caused roof damage to outbuildings near the intersection of Highways 9 and 334. An additional 15 to 20 trees were knocked down nearby.
Nickel size hail reported just south of Savannah.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding across portions of Craighead County. Highway 91 along with county roads 328 and 361 were closed due to flooding.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Pocahontas. Several roads in and around Pocahontas were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Lynn. Several roads were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Ravenden. Several roads were flooded.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in Oak Grove Heights. Several roads were flooded.
Straight line winds knocked down power lines in Steele.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in parts of Southaven. Several yards were flooded at State Line Road and Millbranch Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in midtown Memphis. Belvedere Boulevard was flooded along with some roadways in Overton Park.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding in southwest Fayette County. Highways 194, 57 and 196 were flooded.

Heavy Rain produced flooding along the Black River and the river's tributaries in western portions of Clay County. Arkansas 211 was closed due to flooding from U.S. 67 to the Arkansas-Missouri Border near Success. Arkansas 280 near Brookings was also closed due to flooding. Clay County was declared a state disaster area.

Heavy rain produced flooding along creeks and tributaries that feed off the Mississippi River in Mississippi County. U.S. 61 Northbound was closed in a section near Luxora. In addition, Arkansas 120 from O'Donnell Bend Landing also near Luxora was closed. Arkansas 158 was closed from the intersection of Highway 77 to near Milligan's Ridge.

Heavy rain produced flooding along the Black River and it's tributaries. County Roads 933, 960, 911, 520, and 435 were closed as a result of the flooding. Many residents were forced to evacuate due to the rising flood waters. Two houses and several roads received major damage. County road 520 was washed away. Greene County was declared a state disaster area.

Heavy rain produced flooding along the Black River and it's tributaries. The flooding provided intense pressure on the county's levees. Two breaches occurred, one of them on the Scaggs-Ferry Levee. Numerous roads were closed from the high water including Arkansas 90, U.S.Highway 62, Arkansas 166, Arkansas 93, Arkansas 328, Arkansas 304, and U.S. Highway 67 South from Pocahontas into Lawrence County. Over forty buildings including some houses and a senior citizen complex received damage from the flooding. Of those, ten houses were destroyed, thirty-four houses had major damage, and twelve had minor damage. Randolph County was declared a state disaster area.

Heavy rain produced flooding along the Black River and it's tributaries. Numerous roads were closed due to the high water including Arkansas 115, Arkansas 117, U.S. Highway 63 from Hoxie to the Sharp County line, Arkansas 25, and U.S. Highway 412. County Roads 106 and 107 received damage from the flooding as well. Twenty-five homes were destroyed and forty received major damage. Many cabins and other dwellings received damage as well. Lawrence County was declared a state disaster area.

Heavy rain caused flooding along the Cache River and Big Creek ditch. Arkansas 226, County Roads 212 and 204 were closed due to flooding. The Windsor Landing Subdivision on U.S. 49 at Farville was flooded as well as the Cottonwood Subdivision near Jonesboro. Many streets in the city of Jonesboro were flooded as well. Wheat fields were damaged by high water.
Lightning struck a transformer at Arkansas State University outside of Kays Hall. 400 students had to be evacuated due to smoke from the transformer.
A 7 year old boy drowned when he fell into a rain-swollen creek near Steamboat Bend in Northaven.
Two homes near the intersection of Union Hill Road and Highway 348 caught fire due to a lightning strike.
Downed trees and power lines were reported on Route 306 west of Colt.  A tree fell on Pine Tree Baptist Church.
A tornado developed and crossed Highway 70 between Forrest City and Palestine.
Strong winds blew a power pole down on Dundee Road, approximately 3 miles northwest of the Dundee community.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in the Marvell community.
Thunderstorm winds blew down several trees in Lexa.
A large tree was blown down on a home on Prichard Road in North Tunica.

A tornado developed southeast of Hickory Ridge and moved north-northwest through town.  An airplane hangar was damaged west of County Road 259.  The tornado damaged trees and several roofs and awnings as it moved through Hickory Ridge.  The tornado dissipated just northwest of town.
A media field reporter observed a tornado west of Lepanto, just north of Highway 14.  The tornado was in open field and no damage resulted.
A tornado developed west of Lake City and crossed Highway 18.  The tornado damaged a church along Highway 18.  The tornado moved into open field and dissipated south of Lester Road.

A tornado developed north of Cash and moved northwest.  The tornado pulled metal panels from an airplane hangar west of Highway 18.  The tornado damaged the roof of a home and uprooted trees along Highway 91 southeast of Egypt.  Trees were uprooted in Egypt, and the tornado dissipated as it moved through the community.

A tornado developed near County Road 940 and moved northwest across County Roads 967 and 964.  The tornado damaged three homes in this neighborhood, partially unroofing one home.  The tornado dissipated just after crossing Highway 49.
Power lines were blown down along Nettleton, Matthews, and Airport Roads.
Thunderstorm winds downed a power pole and lines near Commerce Drive and I-555.
A large tree fell on a mobile home off of Duncan Road.
Strong winds downed a large tree across County Road 118 near Bono.
Reports via social media of a large tree down on West Thompson St. in Paragould.
Thunderstorm winds downed a large tree on Pine Knot Rd. and County Road 715 west of Paragould.
A tornado touched down in northern portions of Oxford, northeast of the Oxford Airport.  The brief tornado damaged trees west of Old Highway 7, but no structural damage was reported.
Thunderstorm winds damaged a store front and a radio tower.  A large tree was blown down onto a home in Corinth.
Reports from social media of a large tree split by thunderstorm winds in Houlka.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding near Verona.  Several roads were flooded in the area.
Flooding occurred near Main Street and L and N Roads in Mason.  A few homes were evacuated.
Heavy rain caused flooding along Highway 59 at Mason-Malone Road, Highway 14 intersection, and in the Cannon Grove area.
A lightning strike occurred near the NIDEC plant in northeast Lexington.  One injury resulted.
Flooding reported along County Roads 5011 and 5111.  Ditches overflowed and contributed to the flooding.  CR 5111 was almost impassable.
Heavy rain caused flash flooding in central and western Jonesboro.  Several cars were stranded, and roads had water up to a foot deep.
Heavy rain produced flooding along Turkey Creek, south of Camden.  A foot of water was reported over Gobbler Drive near Highway 192.
A tornado developed west of Wynnburg and moved northeast across open farmland, lifting before reaching Highway 78 south of Tiptonville.  No structural damage was observed.
A tornado developed just south of Deering. The tornado moved east northeast on an intermittent path.  The tornado moved across open fields, and no structural damage was reported.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees near Nesbit.  One tree fell across a road.
Thunderstorm winds downed trees north of Lewisburg.  A large tree fell across the road near the intersection of Bethel Road and Highway 305.
Trained spotters reporting flooding along Shiloh road and nearby areas in northeast Corinth.
Thunderstorm winds downed several trees and caused minor damage to one home in the Light community.
Flooding from heavy rains washed out a portion of the 5000 block of Marshall Drive, north of Savannah.
Heavy rain from thunderstorms produced flash flooding northeast of Booneville.  Tuscumbia Road was flooded and impassible near the intersection of County Road 1129.

Power poles were bent and a section of roof was blown off in Blytheville.

Very cold temperatures settled over the region in mid-February. Temperatures dropped to around zero degrees on the morning of February 16th and wind chills dropped as low as 15 degrees below zero. Thin ice formed on area ponds. A young girl drowned when she fell through the ice on a small pond while sledding.
A large tree knocked down. Wind speed measured at 67 mph with a handheld anemometer.
Lightning struck the Dyer Central Control Communications Center. Some electronics were damaged.

Straight-line winds caused minor damage to Belmont High School. Various trees and power lines were knocked down on the property as well. Three houses were damaged. A tree fell on one house and two had roof damage. The tin roof of a church was partially removed.
Small hail was reported in the Shelby Forest area.
Multiple trees were knocked down north and northwest of Oxford. Trees were down on Highway 314 near FNC Park, County Road 101 at Highway 7, and County Road 103.
Straight-line winds knocked a large tree onto a house at Brown Avenue near North Evergreen. A child was rescued after being trapped.
Flooding occurred across Tiptonville. Several inches of water flooded one structure.

Over four inches of rain fell in Union City since midnight. Several roads were washed out in Union City. Several roads were closed across the county. Cleve Duke Road was flooded southwest of Hornbeak. Water was up to the car doors in some areas.
The Highway 45 Bypass and other roads around the county were flooded.

Several roads were closed in Henry County due to flooding. Paschall Cemetery Road northwest of Puryear was washed out. Other closed roads include Dale Cemetery Road and Freeland Road near Buchanan. Highway 69 South and Bethesda Road were flooded in Paris.
Straight-line winds tore the metal roofing off of a barn.
A portion of Highway 79, northeast of Forrest Avenue, in Marianna is closed due to high water. It has been reported that the railroad underpass is underwater and not safe for travel.
Stewart Road completely underwater near the intersection with Brunswick Road. Car was stranded in the water.
Heavy rain caused flooding in southwest Memphis. Water went right up to the front door of one house on Oakshire Cove and several inches of water-covered roads in the Nutbush area.
Brantley Road between Wilson Mill Road and Highway 61 was closed due to flooding.
Holly Springs Road was flooded in DeSoto County.
Flooding washed out several culverts across Madison County. Culverts were washed out on Hopper Road, Bowman Collins Road, and Wilde Road.
A large tree fell on a home on Bensontown Drive in Walnut Grove causing significant damage to the roof and a broken window.
Quarter size hail fell at the Moore's Plantation subdivision.
A tree fell on a house causing minor rood damage.
Highway 15 flooded more than 6 inches deep south of Walnut.
Three homes were struck by lightning within a one-hour period in the Bruton Branch and Pickwick areas. Two homes had a fire in the wall and received minor damage and the third smelled of smoke.
Sassar road was closed due to flooding.
Motorists stranded in floodwaters at Cass Street railroad underpass.
Peavine Road flooded between Buster Road and Breezewood Lane.
Lightning struck a home on Killough Street causing exterior damage and blowing out an interior wall.
Trees and power lines were knocked down along Riverside Road and Rochell Road in Medon.
A large area was flooded including roads in the Quito Estates subdivision north of Millington.
Watson Road was closed due to flooding.
A large area was flooded at Belvedere Boulevard and Poplar Avenue.
