Many streets were flooded and closed off in southeast Jonesboro. Several cars were stalled and stranded. Timms Street was flooded and water rescues from vehicles occurred on Red Wolf Boulevard south of Nettleton Avenue.
County Road 425 was flooded south of Valley View.
Roads and streets were flooded around the intersection of Highway 163 and Highway 158. Water reached the front doors of a few houses.
County Road 959 was washed out between County Road 960 and County Road 931.
A large tree snapped at the trunk near the Eygpt community.
Straight-line winds caused minor damage to a mobile home.
A few trees were knocked down on County Road 1411 between Nettleton and Richmond.
Several trees were knocked down in Richmond.
Trees and power lines were knocked down in Amory.
A few trees were knocked down in Fulton on South and North Cummings Streets.
Flooding in Paragould caused cars to stall.
County Road 590 was flooded near Shannon.

The tornado developed west of County Road 410 to the southwest of Okolona. The tornado damaged a barn and uprooted trees. After crossing County Road 410, the tornado uprooted additional trees and broke large limbs. The tornado dissipated in an open field east of County Road 410 and south of County Road 150. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.

The tornado developed near the intersection of Highway 41 and County Road 413, where the tornado downed trees. The tornado���s path was intermittent, as no damage was observed on the north side of Highway 41. The tornado reached its peak intensity as it approached County Road 142. Several trees were uprooted, and an outbuilding was destroyed. The tornado uprooted additional trees on the north side of County Road 142. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

The tornado developed just southwest of Nettleton, where it damaged a few trees. The tornado path was quite intermittent,  with gaps between damage areas. The tornado then moved into Nettleton and crossed into Lee County. Peak estimated winds were around 65 mph.

This weak tornado crossed from Monroe County and moved north-northeast.  The tornado path was quite intermittent, with gaps between damage areas. A few trees were uprooted on the northeast side of Nettleton. Additional tree damage was noted along County Road 1205. Near the end of its path, the tornado uprooted a tree that fell on a house and damaged the roof of a stable.
A few trees were knocked down near the intersection of Highway 76 and Highway 23. A few cones and road barriers were also knocked down.
A tree was knocked down on power lines on Byrd Road.
A large tree was knocked down near Cherry Road and Park Avenue.
Central Avenue was flooded near the Liberty Bowl and impassable.
Elm Road was flooded and impassable.
Glendale Road was flooded near Highway 69 just northwest of Savannah. Road was impassable.
Cobblestone Drive just north of Savannah was flooded and impassable.
Selmer City Park was flooded.
Several large trees were knocked down between Henderson and Jacks Creek. Reports of minor roof damage and multiple sheds and outbuildings damaged.

The tornado developed near the Chester/Henderson County line. The first observed damage was uprooted trees along Mifflin Road. The tornado moved east, and crossed Boss Wadley Road. Trees were uprooted, and some trunks were snapped in this area. The most significant damage occurred near Highway 22A and Middlefork Road. A home lost part of its roof, several storage buildings were damaged or destroyed, and a tree fell on another home damaging its roof. Last observed damage occurred east of Highway 22A. This tornado was broad and relatively disorganized for much of its lifetime. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
Golf ball size hail fell in the Pine Lake area.
Golf ball size hail fell in the Shady Hill area.
A brief tornado uprooted trees along Highway 104 northwest of Reagan.
Video of a weak tornado over open country south of Perryville.
Power lines were knocked down on Highway 1 in Vanndale.
A brief tornado was observed by a storm chaser.
Straight-line winds knocked down some large tree limbs on Highway 22A just south of Middlefork Road. Minor roof damage occurred to a house on Laster Road.
A tornado uprooted trees and broke a power pole cross member near the intersection of Highways 77 and 118. Peak winds were estimated at 70 mph.
Straight-line winds south of the tornado track knocked down large tree branches on Highway 77 and damaged a power pole on Highway 118.

A tornado uprooted trees and blew down a sign as it approached Interstate 55. As it crossed I-55, the tornado blew over a semi-tractor-trailer. The tornado broke tree limbs just east of I-55. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.

This tornado broke several power poles along Highway 14 south of Marie. A mobile home was heavily damaged along County Road 447. Further to the northeast, a storage building was destroyed along County Road 471. The last observed damage was tree limbs along County Road 860. Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph.

Tornado developed just west of the Mississippi River. The tornado broke power poles next to an industrial facility near the Sans Souci Landing. The tornado crossed the river into Lauderdale County, Tennessee. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph in Mississippi County.

The tornado crossed the river from Mississippi County, AR into Lauderdale County, Tennessee. The tornado destroyed a barn along Crutcher Lake Road and continued to the northeast before dissipating. Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph in Lauderdale County.
A few trees were knocked down and large branches were broken in the southern section of Osceola.
Golf ball size hail fell near Marianna.
MPING report of quarter size hail near Jacks Creek.

Penny size hail fell in the 7000 block of Highway 200.
Numerous roadways were flooded in northern parts of Decaturville.
Quarter size hail fell between Henderson and Mifflin.
Flooding resulted in a water rescue on Perryville Road near Parsons.
Metal roofs were peeled from outbuildings along Highway 20 west of Elaine.
A lightning strike resulted in a structure fire in Gibson County.
South College Street in Covington was flooded.
Five cars and one person were blown off Highway 61 about 2 miles northeast of Lula. Scrap metal debris on road.
Several streets in Brownsville were closed due to flooding. Flooding also occurred at exit 52 on Interstate 40 and the intersection of Highway 70 and Highway 179.
Mobile homes flipped in the Como area.
A large tree fell and knocked down power lines near the Collierville Town Square.
The tornado caused tree and roof damage. Three mobile homes were destroyed as well as outbuildings. Approximately seventeen structures were damaged. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
A mobile home was rolled and heavily damaged east of Coldwater on Highway 306.
A few outbuildings along Mays Road suffered minor damage.
Trees knocked down in Moscow.
Heavy rain flooded many roads and back yards near Olive Branch.

Several trees were down on houses and mobile homes in Grand Junction. Trees were knocked down across roadways. Power lines were knocked down. A mobile home was blown off its foundation on Zinnia Lane and four kids were temporarily trapped inside. A nearby mobile home sustained roof damage.
Highway 22A near Jacks Creek was flooded and impassable.
Trees were uprooted.

Two occupied vehicles were swept away by floodwaters. One vehicle was swept away on Bowman Collins Road and the other on Mandy Road. They required swift-water rescues. These roads suffered culvert washouts. There were multiple road closures across the county due to flooding including Chester Street which was flooded with 2 to 3 feet of water near the uptown area of Jackson. Culverts were also washed out on White Fern Road and Meadon Malesus Road.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down across Selmer.
A porch was blown off a mobile home. Numerous trees were knocked down or uprooted. A power pole was knocked down.
A few trees were knocked down at the Goat Island Recreational Area.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down along County Road 430 between Paris and Tula.
A large tree fell on a house on Denton Street.
Straight-line winds damaged the soccer complex on the west side of Tupelo. A portion of the roof was removed from a building.
Part of a metal roof was removed from a home in Shannon.
A large tree fell on a home in Amory resulting in significant damage to the roof.
Numerous trees were knocked down at the country club on the west side of Aberdeen.
Several trees were knocked down and the roof was blown off an outbuilding.
Trees were knocked onto a home along Highway 341. Trees broke windows and caused damage to the roof and siding.
A large tree was knocked down in Mooreville.
A large tree was knocked down, crushing a large pet kennel.
Twenty-two residents were rescued from near flooded homes on Hidden Valley Circle in Lexington. Eight roads were closed around the county due to washed-out culverts.
Several trees and large tree branches were knocked down along Yager Road.

The tornado developed south of Highway 8, and downed trees along and east of Dobbs Street. Some trees fell onto homes and vehicles. The tornado crossed Highway 8 and damaged the Vardaman school complex.  Awnings were damaged, trees blown down, and a portion of brick veneer was removed from a building. The last observed damage was to tree limbs near County Road 231. Peak winds estimated at 85 mph.

The first observed damage was west of Hatley Road South. Several sheds were damaged or destroyed. As the tornado crossed Hatley Road, it caused minor roof damage and downed several trees. After a brief weakening period, the tornado increased in intensity as it approached Thornton Lane and Weaver Creek Drive. Numerous trees were blown down, some tree trunks were snapped, and power poles were damaged. A permanent home had roof and sunroom damage, and a mobile home lost part of its roof. The tornado damaged homes and downed additional trees along Nash Road. The last observed damage was to tree limbs along Stonewall Road. Peak winds estimated at 95 mph.
A bridge located on Highway 203 near the Burnt Church Community Center was undermined by flooding.
Several trees and limbs were knocked down on Highway 8 between Calhoun City and Vardaman.
Straight-line winds tore the roof off a house on Main Street.
Numerous trees were knocked down at the west end of Phillips Schoolhouse Road near the daycare.
Several roads flooded in Houston. Some rescues occurred in Houston.
Flooding occurred in parts of Hardin County including Burnt Church and Olivehill. Some water rescues occurred.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down across Oxford. Several streets were closed and a couple of vehicles were damaged. A business sign was destroyed.

Flooding occurred across parts of Monroe County. Several inches of water flooded an apartment in Amory. Multiple roads were closed in and around Hatley. Adams road was completely underwater and impassable.
County Road 28 was washed out.
Highway 8 was closed between Church Street and Martin Luther King Drive due to flooding.
Swift-water rescues occurred around Calhoun City.

A few power lines were knocked down just south of Tyronza between Interstate 555 and Highway 322. One house south of town lost some siding and had some windows knocked out by a picnic table. Two center pivots irrigation systems were damaged.
A couple of trees were knocked down near the intersection of Reynolds Road and Country Club Road.
Highway 51 in Coldwater was flooded with over 6 inches of water covering all four lanes.
Multiple trees knocked down on County Road 127 east of New Albany.
Mulitple trees were knocked down on Highway 30 near Keownville.
Ping pong-sized hail fell near the Fox Hills Country Club.
Endville Road flooded with eight inches of water.
Straight-line winds caused significant damage to the awning at Houston Middle School.
A metal shed was destroyed on County Road 17 in Houlka.
Trees down on three houses in Houston. Trees scattered across Highway 8 and uprooted across the Natchez Trace Parkway.
A tree fell on a home on County Road 411 south of Okolona causing major damage.
Highway 178 was impassable due to flooding.
A tree fell on a house near Woodland.
A large tree was knocked down in Nettleton.
A vehicle was stranded in floodwaters in Tupelo.

The first damage from the tornado was observed just west of Shady Grove Road, where large tree branches were broken. As the tornado crossed Buchanan Road, several homes suffered roof damage and a large storage shed was destroyed. The tornado uprooted trees and snapped tree trunks in this area. Further east, along Scarborough Lane, the tornado uprooted trees and removed the metal roof from an event venue. The tornado damaged several mobile homes just west of Log Cabin Road. Two of the mobile homes were rolled on their sides. The injury was reported in one of these mobile homes. The tornado crossed U.S. Highway 79 and appeared to reach maximum intensity in the area of Sulphur Wells Academy Road and Friendship Road. A large metal building was destroyed, and numerous trees were uprooted or had their trunks snapped. The tornado was weakening as it crossed Oak Grove Road, and the last observed damage was east of Antioch Road. In total three mobile homes and two commercial businesses were destroyed. Three homes suffered major damage from trees and 23 homes suffered minor damage. Peak winds were estimated at 95-100 mph.
Branches greater than a foot in diameter were torn from trees.
A swath of straight-line wind damage associated with the rear flank downdraft occurred south of the tornado track. A few trees were uprooted and many large branches were knocked down.
Multiple fire departments called in to extinguish a fire at a business on Mulberry Avenue in Selmer. The fire was believed to be started by lightning.
An apparent log jam developed on the Yalobusha River near Big Creek resulting in some lowland flooding south of the Big Creek Community. At least one home was flooded and County Road 312 was closed.
A weak tornado knocked down trees along County Road 380 in Sabougla. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.

Tornado began just south of Calhoun City and tracked through the east side. Damage to trees was first noted south of town. Roof damage occurred to homes, apartments, and structures due to tree fall and wind force. An older masonry building was destroyed. In total, 43 homes, six businesses, and two public bridges suffered some level of damage. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.
A weak tornado knocked down trees north of New Houlka near the Pontotoc county line before crossing into Pontotoc County. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph.
A weak tornado crossed from Chickasaw County into Pontotoc County and tracked northeast knocking down trees before dissipating southeast of Algoma.  Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph.

The tornado developed in eastern Pontotoc County, causing roof damage to several residences along King���s Highway. In total, 10 homes and one business suffered some level of damage in Pontotoc County. The tornado crossed into  Lee County.  Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.

The tornado developed in eastern Pontotoc County and crossed into Lee County. The tornado damaged numerous trees along County Road 900. The tornado���s damage path became intermittent, and the last observed damage was just west of Natchez Trace Parkway. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.

The first observed damage was near south Thomas Street in southwest Tupelo. The tornado���s damage path was intermittent through the first part of its track. It caused minor damage to trees and a church roof along Thomas Street and Lawndale Drive. The damage became more continuous as the tornado approached Main Street. Numerous trees were uprooted, with some trunks snapped. Several trees fell onto homes, causing substantial damage. The tornado reached its peak intensity near Veterans Memorial Parkway and Elvis Presley Drive. The tornado damaged several commercial buildings and residences. Two residences suffered partial roof removal. The tornado crossed Interstate 22, and the damage became more sporadic. The tornado uprooted additional trees, with some falling on houses. The last observed damage was near County Road 1451. In total, 76 homes, six businesses, and one public building suffered some level of damage. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
This tornado damaged trees along County Road 1970 and Ita Lee Road then crossed into Itawamba County. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.
This tornado crossed into Itawamba County from Lee County. The last damage observed was near route 363 south of the Ratliff community. Peak winds were estimated at 75 mph.
Straight-line winds tore the siding off a home in Corning and knocked numerous trees down.

The tornado damaged trees and moved a double-wide mobile home off of its piers along Highway 34. The tornado crossed Highway 34 and damaged a shed and a large metal storage building. As the tornado approached and crossed Highway 135, it uprooted numerous trees and snapped the trunks of a couple of trees. The last observed damage was east of Highway 135 along County Road 510. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down on Highway 14 near Dawson Lane.
A large tree was knocked down in Oak Grove Heights.
Straight-line winds knocked several trees in the southern part of Paragould and caused minor damage to a few homes and mobile homes. One mobile home was heavily damaged.
A few homes were damaged on Highway 69 west of Trumann. Several trees were damaged and a few signs were blown down as well.
Trees down in Kennett.
A storage shed was damaged.
Power lines were knocked down in Bragg City.
Straight-line winds caused some roof damage to a few homes and a business. Several trees and large branches were knocked down.
Trees were knocked down in Hayti.

The tornado developed near Interstate 55 where it damaged a shop building and a grain bin. Debris from the shop building was carried approximately one-quarter mile downstream. Along County Road 121, the tornado uprooted trees, one of which fell onto a church. The tornado damaged residences and a grain bin along County Road 321. The last observed damage was to trees east of C.R. 321. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph.
Trees and power lines were knocked down in the Tiptonville area. Highways 78 and 22 were blocked. A power pole was snapped in Tiptonville.
Widespread tree and roof damage in the Samburg area.
Straight-line winds tore the roof off home on Shawtown Road.
Straight-line winds knocked down trees and power lines along US Highway 51. A warehouse suffered roof and wall damage.
Trees and power lines were knocked down at Highway 45 and East Union Grove Road. Three irrigation rigs were damaged in the area.
Straight-line winds damaged a workshop and barn on Polk Station Road. A tractor barn was destroyed on Garrett Saw Mill Road.  Grain bins and farm sheds were destroyed on Crockett Road.
Straight-line winds knocked down several large trees along Hurt Road. A large tree fell on and destroyed a home.

Straight-line winds knocked down numerous trees and power lines south of Dresden.  Trees fell on a total of seven mobile homes resulting in significant damage. A fatality occurred in one of the mobile homes. A metal building was also damaged near Dresden.
Trees knocked down on Highway 22 east of Martin.

Trees and power lines were knocked down across Paris. One mobile home was destroyed at a mobile home park on Memorial Drive. Several businesses were damaged. Most businesses received moderate damage to roofs, doors, and windows. In total 35 homes, five businesses, and a church were damaged across Henry County from this storm.
Trees and power lines down on Evanstown Road north of Parsons.
A weak tornado uprooted trees and damaged a few outbuildings. A few homes and vehicles were damaged from trees falling on them. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
A large tree was knocked down and blocked the intersection at County Road 4101 and County Road 4130.
Numerous trees were knocked down with damage to houses, vehicles, and power lines.
Large limbs and some trees knocked down along County Road 363 near the community of Ozark.
A few trees knocked down in Mantachie.
A few trees were knocked down in Fulton. Some trees on vehicles and houses.
A large tree was knocked down between Wren and Aberdeen.
A large tree knocked down on a house in Mooreville.
A tree fell and damaged an outdoor gazebo in Ripley.
Trees and power lines down in the residential area of Houston.
Numerous trees down on Seely Drive in Hamilton.
Straight-line winds knocked down trees in Marmaduke.
Straight-line winds knocked trees down around town. A fence was damaged by a fallen tree.

Numerous trees down across the county especially between Trenton, Humboldt, and Gibson. Multiple trees fell on houses and a tree fell on a car. Power lines were knocked down on US Highway 45W between Trenton and Humboldt.
A large tree was knocked down in Jonesboro.
Several trees were knocked down in Toone.
Four trees knocked down on Poplar Road in Corinth.
Several trees were knocked down in Michie.
Straight-line winds knocked down 30-40 trees. Several trees fell on houses while several power lines were knocked down as well.
Trees knocked down in Lafe.
Trees knocked down with power outages.
Trees knocked down in Saltillo. A large tree fell on the porch of a house.

Trees were knocked down across the Tupelo area. Trees fell on Simpson Drive and in the Palmetto Community south of the city. Shingles were blown off a house in the Palmetto Community as well. A power pole was knocked down on Daybright Drive.
Straight-line winds caused shingle damage to a house in Ecru.
Trees fell on houses in Belmont.
Tree snapped at base.
Several trees knocked down in Bigbee.
A large oak was snapped in New Hamilton.
A brief tornado damaged a barn and storage building. It removed metal roof panels from a house and uprooted several trees. Peak winds were estimated at 85 mph.

The first observed damage was east of Dolan Road and west of Glen Springs Road. The tornado uprooted trees and caused roof damage just west of Glen Springs Road. Across Glen Springs Road, the tornado damaged a storage building and additional trees. The tornado crossed Glen Springs Lake and uprooted trees along Slough Road. Evidence suggested the tornado weakened in this area. The tornado strengthened as it approached Campground Road and Munford Giltedge Road. The tornado damaged a barn, large storage shed and caused roof damage to homes in the area. Trees were uprooted, and a couple of tree trunks were snapped. The tornado continued east and uprooted trees along Plantation Road. Several trees fell onto houses. The last observed damage was west of Beaver Road. Peak winds were estimated at 95 mph.
A large tree fell on a house at Kenny Hill Road and Hickory Lane in Tunica.
Numerous trees down and minor damage to a home.
Multiple trees were knocked down and two structures were damaged in the New Town area mainly along Rose Road.
Trees and power lines down along Highway 69 and Handy Corner near Saltillo.
Trees and power lines down across Abbeville.
Trees down on power lines.
A roof and carport were damaged at home along Highway 30 near Etta. Numerous trees were knocked down.
Trees down and a dog run was damaged on Harmony Loop.
A large tree was knocked down in Ecru.
Numerous trees were knocked down.
Trees were knocked down in Troy.
Trees were knocked down in Tupelo. A tree fell on a house.
Trees were knocked down on Highway 336 in the Thaxton area.
Several trees were knocked down in the town of Belden.
Numerous trees were knocked down on Highway 6 near County Road 598.
Numerous trees were knocked down in the town of Tishomingo. Additional trees were knocked down at County Road 127 and County Road 961.
Numerous trees were knocked down in the Evergreen area.
A tree was snapped in half in Amory.
A tree fell on a mobile home causing significant damage in the Tilden community.
A tree fell on a house on Highway 463 south of Trumann. A tree fell on a house on Highway 214 east of McCormick.
A few trees were knocked down in Dyer County.
A home was struck by lightning and caught fire on Country Club Lane near Paris.
A few trees and power lines were knocked down in Lauderdale County. One traffic accident due to a car running into a downed tree.

A farmer was inside a milk barn on Reed Road near Dyer. The farmer was milking cows when lightning struck the barn. He was holding a metal railing attached to the barn. The farmer was transported to the local hospital and only suffered minor injuries.

Straight-line winds knocked down trees from Highway 22 North to Corinth Road in the northeast part of Henderson County. Trees fell on Stanfill Road, Alberton Road near the Mazies Chapel Road intersection. A local CO-OP has their sign damaged and a greenhouse shifted three feet. A local trucking company had several empty trailers rolled. An outbuilding was also damaged and a tree fell on an unoccupied mobile home.
Straight-line winds knocked down trees and damaged several homes in the Puryear area. Several barns and outbuildings were destroyed as well. A parked tractor-trailer was blown over.
Tornado damaged a 500-foot tower and antennas west of Union City.  The tornado downed numerous trees, several of which fell on houses. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
Thunderstorm winds damaged grain bins and storage buildings.
Half-dollar size hail fell along Cedar Grove Church Road and Sawmill Road.
Quarter size hail fell along Highway 641 north of Camden.
Hail up to the size of nickels fell on Old Springville Road.
An unanchored, 40 foot long mobile home, was blown off its blocks at Dry Branch Road and Morgan Creek Road.
County Road 435 was impassable due to flowing water covering the road.
County Road 1021 was flooded north of Booneville.
Trees knocked down in Marks.
A large tree was knocked down on Sees Chapel Road.
Several trees were knocked down in the Love community off Highway 51.
Three-inch limbs were knocked down in the area of Holly Springs and McIngvale Road.

Several cars were stalled in floodwaters due to street flooding in Batesville. Part of Old Panola Road was washed out near the bridge over the Tallahatchie River. In total, 23 roads were impacted across Panola County.
Several cars were stalled in floodwaters due to significant street flooding in Charleston.

A creek running under County Road 224 east of Water Valley eroded the ground under the road. The roadbed was left intact. A vehicle drove over the compromised road, causing the roadbed to collapse. The vehicle fell into the creek and the driver had to be pulled out. Several mobile homes were flooded along Oklahoma Street in Coffeeville. There was significant flooding on Central Street in Water Valley. In total, six homes and three roads were impacted.
Numerous roads were blocked due to significant flooding across Lafayette County.  County Road 381 was closed and there was flooding in the Oaks Subdivision just north of Oxford.
There was widespread flooding in the Tutwiler area. There were eight inches of water in at least two homes on West Street.
County Road 7 and County Road 299 were flooded with more than 6 inches of flowing water.
Several cars were stalled in floodwaters in downtown New Albany. Water was several feet deep in some locations, including Main Street.
Portions of County Roads 102 and 104 were closed due to flash flooding.
County Road 102 was closed due to flash flooding.
Several low-lying roads were flooded in northwest Quitman County.
A 24-hour rainfall total of 6.38 inches was measured.
A 12-hour rainfall total of 5.38 inches was measured.

A weak tornado touched down near Highway 45 and Highway 278. Large drainage pipes were thrown across the highway and a fence was knocked down around a business. A 53-foot trailer was flipped over. Peak estimated winds were 70 mph.
Several trees were knocked down in Palmetto and Verona. A large tree fell on a house in Verona.
Trees and powerlines were knocked down in Mooreville.
A tree was knocked down across Highway 25 in front of Fairview School.

Heavy rain caused flash flooding across Lafayette County. Four homes and six businesses were impacted. There was flooding at Old Sardis Road, Turnberry Circle, Hathorn Road near Jackson Road, and County Road 317. In total 14 roads were impacted by flooding.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Lee County. Several roads were flooded and 18 houses were impacted.
Highway 1 was closed at the intersection of Highway 1B south of Forrest City.
Part of a bridge washed out on Stark Road.
Significant flooding at Highway 4 and House Road. House Road was closed.
State Route 330 near Tillatoba Lake is flooded.
Highway 51 flooded just south of Como.
Impassable roadway due to flash flooding near the intersection of County Road 318 and Highway 85.
Two-day rainfall total of 8.86 inches.
Two-day rainfall total of 8.58 inches in Water Valley.
Two day rainfall total of 8.37 inches north of Holly Springs.
Two-day rainfall total of 6.20 inches in Potts Camp.
One home was flooded in Crowder.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Quitman County. In total, 12 homes and one business were impacted along with 36 roads.
One business and one home were flooded. Ten roads were flooded.

Over 15 inches of rain resulted in widespread flash flooding across Tallahatchie County.  Numerous roads were flooded and washed out.  Several water rescues occurred across the county, especially in Tutwiler. Power outages occurred in Charleston. Some homes were flooded near the confluence of Tillatoba Creek and North Tillatoba Creek. In total, 50 homes were impacted by flooding.
Two-day rainfall total of 15.35 inches.
There was a levee breach on a small flood control lake near Peters Hill Road and Highway 35.
A large tree was knocked down across Highway 30 west of the Philadelphia area.
A large tree fell on a house.
Quarter size hail fell south of Big Lake.
Straight-line winds blew a carport into the road. Car windows were damaged by a falling tree limb.
Numerous trees were knocked down over roads across southern Benton County especially around the community of Holladay.
A downed tree blocked both lanes of Bobbit Road.
A weak tornado touched down near County Road 1479 north of Mooreville. A few trees were knocked down causing minor damage to a mobile home and vehicle.  Peak winds were estimated at 65 mph.
A weak tornado touched down just west of Verona. A few trees were knocked down. Peak winds were estimated at 60 mph.
Heavy rain resulted in flash flooding across Chickasaw County. Ten roads were flooded.
A brief landspout tornado occurred over an open field near Highway 158 west of Luxora.

The railroad underpass on Riverside Drive near Crump Boulevard and Interstate 55 was flooded.
Powerlines were knocked down along the 300 block of Ashport Road.
A store was flooded with ankle-deep water due to a sewer backup.
Nail Road was closed due to flooding between Highway 61 and Honeysuckle Lane.
A family had to be rescued from their mobile home by boat due to flooding. Several vehicles were damaged.
Numerous trees down and one carport damaged in a five-mile swath from northeast of Blackland to northeast of Booneville.
Tree down close to the town of Rector.
Tree down on East Road in Friendship.
Tree knocked down on Key Corner Street in Brownsville.
Tree down northeast of Gadsen.
The intersection of Highway 64 and Airline Road was flooded.
Straight line winds blew two large trees down in Powhatan.
Straight line winds blew several trees down three to four miles north of Marmaduke.

Straight line winds sheared off the upper portion of a pine tree and struck a house on County Road 534. The eve trough was damaged as a result. Some shingle damage was also reported as well. A quarter mile west three barns were damaged at an unoccupied farm. Two were destroyed. The third barn had the front and rear doors blown out. In addition, an irrigation pivot was blown over and a power line was knocked down in the vicinity as well.
Straight line winds knocked over an irrigation pivot along Highway 25 between Malden and Kennett.
Straight line winds blew a tractor-trailer over on Interstate 55 near exit 27. In addition, the Ross Elementary School in Wardell sustained roof damage.
Straight line winds blew trees down on Walnut Street in Tiptonville.
Straight line winds blew trees down on Putnam Hill Road.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding on Highway DD outside of Campbell. The road was closed as a result.
Numerous trees down across the southern part of Pemiscot County.
Tree knocked down on power lines on Rambo Road.
Numerous trees and power lines were knocked down from the Brazil area into Humboldt.
Trees were knocked down along Highway 70 between the Middle Fork of the Forked Deer River and Frye Access Road.
Numerous trees were knocked down across the county.
Trees and power lines were knocked down on Dyers Chapel Road.
Heavy rain closed seven roads across Dyer County due to flash flooding.
Power lines were knocked down in a couple of spots in Jonesboro.
Straight line winds destroyed a trailer and a grain bin near the intersection of Highway 118 and Marlin Swamp Road. In addition, roofs were blown off of two shops in the area as well.
Straight-line winds caused significant damage to a marina on the Tennessee River southeast of Camden.
Power lines were knocked down and five power poles were destroyed on Highway 45W north of Kenton.
Straight-line winds knocked down numerous trees and damaged several businesses and houses in central Union City.

A thunderstorm caused siding to be ripped off a house 2 miles WSW of Malden.
Flash flooding occurred from eastern Jonesboro through the downtown area. Multiple roads flooded and several cars were stranded.
Flash flooding occurred in East Memphis with several cars stranded.
Quarter hail fell along Highway 79, 5 miles west of Marianna.
Straight line winds damaged trailers and knocked down trees along Highway 1, just south of Marianna.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 120 outside of Luxora. The highway was flooded as a result.
Straight line winds knocked down power poles and power lines near Wren.
Heavy rain produced street flooding on Highway 51 in Coldwater.
Heavy rain produced flooded a restaurant in New Albany along Highway 78.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 51, 5 miles south of Hernando. Water covered the road. In addition, standing water occurred in many yards as ponds overflowed their banks.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding near the intersection of Hacks Cross Road and State Line Road in Southeast Memphis.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding along Highway 51 in Covington as a stream overflowed its bank.
Straight line winds blew trees down in and around Fort Pillow State Park.
Straight line winds blew trees down in the Hatchie Wildlife Refuge.
Winds estimated at 60 to 70 mph, just west of Steele.
Penny to nickel size hail fell 5 miles north of Hayti.
Ping-pong size hail fell on Highway 140 between Puryear and Paris Landing.
At least six inches of water covered King Ridge Drive between Six Crowns Street and King Ridge Cove. A foot of water covered Byhalia Road south of West Powell Road.
Heavy rain produced standing water in fields throughout Lee County.
Straight line winds blew trees down near the intersection of Woodlawn Terrace and James Road.
Straight line winds produced structural damage to a church in Union City.
Straight line winds knocked down trees and power lines countywide.

The first observed damage was just west of the intersection of Highway 25 and Business Highway 25. The tornado moved south-southeast, uprooting or snapping numerous trees along its path. Several trees fell onto houses or storage buildings. The tornado was fairly disorganized early in its life but strengthened as it approached the center of Iuka. Several homes suffered roof damage, and storage buildings were damaged or destroyed. The tornado began weakening after it crossed Eastport street, and the last observed damage was south of Highway 172. Peak winds were estimated at 100 to 105 mph.
A brief tornado damaged trees along and near County Road 247 southeast of Iuka. peak winds were estimated at 70 mph.
Strong winds knocked down a few trees across Lee County.
Tree down blocking Highway 30 and County Road 256.
Trees were knocked down across the road in the Liberty Community.

Heat index values reached 105 to 110 degrees in the afternoon and early evening.
County Road 391 was flooded 2 miles north of Water Valley.
Highway 328 near County Road 387 was flooded.
Straight line winds blew trees down in Brookland.
Straight line winds blew a tree down onto a car on Gravel Springs Road.
Straight line winds blew trees down in Sherard.
Straight line winds blew trees down on Highway 6, 2 miles east of the Panola-LaFayette County line.
Straight line winds blew trees down in Tillatoba.
Straight line winds blew trees down on Second Street in Corning.
Penny size hail fell in the Hilltop area of Jonesboro.
Straight line winds blew trees down on Milnor Drive in Raleigh.
A nineteen year old man fell from a bridge near McKellar Lake into a swollen ditch near an apartment complex where he lived and drowned.

A 56 year old tow truck driver was one of two drivers who arrived to help a man who had driven into flood waters off of Holmes Road near the intersection of Reynolds Road after falling asleep at the wheel. The tow truck driver tied an air hose around his waist for safety and climbed onto the car to attach the cable from the tow truck. The car began to float. The water forced the car through the culvert into the raging Nonconnah Creek tributary, with the force of the current snapping the hose that tethered the man to the tow truck. The car sank 75 feet.

Heavy rain produced flash flooding on a few roadways near the Everett Stewart Airport. A 24 year old man drowned when he ran off of Martin Highway into a swollen creek. The vehicle completely submerged.

The Mississippi River rose to 10 year historical levels in Tunica County. The high levels brought flood water into a few homes in the Tunica Cut-Off Lake area. Voluntary evacuations orders were posted for the area. Two deaths occurred from the flooding. A 23 year old drowned when he fell into the flood water when attempting to secure his family's boat. A 63 year old man drowned when he fell into the flood water after leaving a bar.
The Mississippi River rose to 10 year historical levels in Tunica County. The high levels brought flood water into a few homes in the Tunica Cut-Off Lake area.
Excessive rainfall brought levels of the Forked Deer River to high levels in South Dyersburg. A few homes were flooded as a result.
Heavy rain caused the ground beneath a house to fall into Mills Creek. The house was located on Double Bridges-Unionville Road. A large tree on the side of the hill was also uprooted.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding to many roadways and fields across Henderson County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding to many roadways and fields across Carroll County.
Heavy rain produced flash flooding to many roadways and fields across Weakely County.

Heavy rain produced flooding in March along the Black River and it's tributaries. The flooding provided intense pressure on the county's levees. Two breaches occurred, one of them on the Scaggs-Ferry Levee. Numerous roads were closed from the high water including Arkansas 90, U.S.Highway 62, Arkansas 166, Arkansas 93, Arkansas 328, Arkansas 304, and U.S. Highway 67 South from Pocahontas into Lawrence County. By the beginning of April, over forty buildings including some houses and a senior citizen complex received damage from the flooding. Of those, ten houses were destroyed, thirty-four houses had major damage, and twelve had minor damage. Randolph County was declared a state disaster area. One death occurred. A teenager drowned when the boat he was in capsized in a flooded area outside the main channel of the Black River near the Noland community.

Heavy rain in March produced flooding along the Black River and it's tributaries. Numerous roads were closed due to the high water including Arkansas 115, Arkansas 117, U.S. Highway 63 from Hoxie to the Sharp County line, Arkansas 25, and U.S. Highway 412. County Roads 106 and 107 received damage from the flooding as well. By the beginning of April, twenty-five homes were destroyed and forty received major damage. Many cabins and other dwellings received damage as well. Lawrence County was declared a state disaster area.
Strong winds ahead of low pressure system knocked down an awning at U-Neek Tans in Rector onto two cars.
Strong winds ahead of a low pressure system knocked down a few trees in Corinth. In addition, loose garbage cans and loose items were scattered about the city.
A metal flag pole (5 inches in diameter) was snapped by gusty winds in Sardis.
Highway 49 was flooded between Rector and Greenway.
A historic wooden church built in the 1800s collapsed due to strong winds.
Tree down in Keiser.
Numerous high water rescues in Bruce, extending out to surrounding rural areas.
Main Street at the railroad overpass closed due to flooding.
Quarter sized hail north of Monette near Childress.
A few trees blown down across town.
Penny size hail fell in Holcomb.
A fast-moving storm with small hail that quickly grew to 1 inch sized hail struck Toone.
A thunderstorm moved over the Lexington area dropping nickel sized hail.
Tree down blocking one lane on west Goldston Springs Road.
Trees down on the 6000 block of Highway 140 East.
Quarter-sized hail fell four miles north of Dyer.
Nickel-sized hail fell near East Memphis.
Numerous reports of flooding across the Downtown and Midtown areas of Memphis.
Several outbuildings damaged and some damage to home and trees. Tornado started and ended in open fields. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.
The tornado destroyed an outbuilding. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

Tornado developed just southwest of Trumann and destroyed about 70 homes and damaged another 100 homes. Several businesses were damaged or destroyed. There was also widespread tree damage.  The fire station was also heavily damaged. The worst damage was in the northeast part of Trumann with businesses and homes destroyed.  Tornado path ended near the St. Francis River. Peak winds were estimated at 130 mph.

NWS meteorologists surveyed storm damage in the area of Marietta, MS in Prentiss County and determined it was the result of a tornado. The tornado began in a field along HWY 371 just south of MS-4 East. As the tornado tracked northeastward, hardwood and softwood trees were uprooted with a few snapped trunks. The worst damage occurred along CR 4111, where a site-built home had a large section of roof blown off and a carport totally destroyed. Nearby damage consisted of a narrow path of uprooted trees and a few snapped trunks. It is along this portion of the track that the tornado was given a peak rating of EF-1. Just down the road, a mobile home had a section of peeled roof. The tornado then paralleled CR 3401 to the south, with a narrow but visible path of uprooted trees with some snapped trunks as the circulation cut across tree lines between fields. The final area of structural damage was along CR 3461 where a mobile home had a section of roof peeled back. A few nearby trees were also uprooted just northeast of the home with dissipation of the tornado apparent shortly thereafter. Peak winds estimated at 95 mph.

The tornado began on Beech Bluff Road near Ranger Road where a tree was uprooted and a metal outbuilding was damaged. The tornado then moved east-northeast where a home sustained significant roof damage near the intersection of Beech Bluff Road and Willoughby Road. It then moved northeast where a couple of homes sustained roof and siding damage near the intersection of Fowler and Old Jackson-Lexington Road. The tornado then moved northeast where an outbuilding and small building were destroyed. In total, 15 to 20 homes suffered at least some damage in Madison County.  The tornado then moved into Henderson County. Peak winds were estimated to be 100 mph in Madison County.

The tornado moved from Madison County into Henderson County. Damage was observed on Crucifer Road where a shed was destroyed and a home damaged. The tornado came to an end between Crucifer and Wilson Roads. Peak winds were estimated to be 95 mph in Henderson County.

The tornado began just southwest of US-412 off Pine Crest Drive where several trees were damaged. The tornado crossed US-412 and destroyed an outbuilding then moved northeast towards Highway 104 and damaged the roof of a home. It continued to move northeast across northern Beech Lake and produced more damage in the Timberlake community. A couple of metal power poles were bent and a couple of metal buildings were significantly damaged or destroyed in an industrial park. The most significant damage occurred just east of this area where two TVA transmission towers were completely destroyed. The tornado then continued traveling northeast into Natchez Trace State Park snapping and de-barking numerous trees along its path. One injury was reported in the area of Timberlake Wildersville Road. Peak winds were estimated to be 135 mph.

The tornado initially touched down southwest of Inman Ridge and just east of Willow Creek in western Decatur County. It moved due east and hit a mobile home on the corner of Ora Bawcum Lane and Verlie Inman Road. At this location, several trees were snapped at their base, one of which fell onto and demolished half of the mobile home. Insulation and debris from the home were lofted and scattered into a nearby field. The tornado continued along an easterly path through the community of Yellow Springs and crossed over US-641 and into the southern part of Sugar Tree. Intermittent tree damage was noted on high-resolution satellite imagery along its path. The tornado then continues into Benton County. Peak winds were estimated to be 90 mph in Decatur County.
The tornado crossed into Benton County from Decatur County. Tree damage was noted along the path. The tornado lifted near Redbud Lane. Peak winds were estimated to be 80 mph in Benton County.
A weak tornado touched down in rural Fayette County. No damage was observed.
A tornado touched down northeast of Cash, snapping 12 power poles and damaging a barn. Peak winds were estimated to be 105 mph.
A brief tornado damaged trees southwest of Weiner. A tree fell against a house in Weiner. Peak winds were estimated at 65 mph.

A tornado developed near the Poinsett/Craighead County line and damaged trees along County Road 452. The tornado damaged a large rice facility along Highway 1, and destroyed a storage building near County Road 406.  The tornado dissipated as it approached Highway 158. Peak winds were estimated at 100 mph.
A brief tornado caused minor damage to trees and storage buildings just west of Interstate 555, west of Bay. Peak winds were estimated to be 65 mph.
A brief tornado uprooted trees along Marvin Vaught Road northeast of Samburg. Peak winds were estimated at 90 mph.
A brief tornado damaged trees along Highway 22 west of Union City. Peak winds were estimated at 70 mph.
A tornado damaged trees and storage buildings along Shawtown Road. Peak winds were estimated at 80 mph.

The tornado produced its first damage north of Bay, damaging storage and outbuildings. The tornado gradually strengthened and destroyed a farm tractor storage building along Highway 135 northwest of Lake City. The tornado possibly weakened slightly as it crossed the St. Francis River area, but re-strengthened as it approached Monette. Northern and northwestern portions of Monette suffered significant damage. Homes and retail facilities had their roofs partially or completely removed, and the roof of a nursing home partially collapsed. One fatality and at least 5 injuries occurred in the nursing home. After leaving Monette the tornado crossed into Mississippi County. Peak winds were estimated at 145 mph in Craighead County.

After crossing from Craighead County into Mississippi County the tornado struck the northern portions of Leachville, in northwestern Mississippi County. Several homes suffered partial or complete roof loss in northwestern Leachville. A restaurant, store, and cotton gin suffered considerable damage along Highway 77, and numerous power poles were snapped. A fatality occurred in the store. Anchors to the store's metal frame were pulled out of the concrete foundation. The tornado's path was estimated at nearly a mile wide in this area. The tornado approached the Little River area south of Hornersville, near the Arkansas/Missouri state line.  A stand of trees was debarked east of Arkansas County Road 243. Several homes and mobile homes were heavily damaged or destroyed along State Line Road.  Additional debarking of trees was noted. The tornado then crossed into Dunklin County, Missouri. Peak winds in Mississippi County were estimated at 145 mph.

The tornado crossed from Mississippi County, Arkansas into Dunklin County, Missouri near the Little River area south of Hornersville, near the Arkansas/Missouri state line.  Several homes and mobile homes were heavily damaged or destroyed along State Line Road. Several vehicles and a boat were tossed or overturned. Additional debarking of trees was noted. After exiting the Little River area, the tornado damaged six metal electric transmission line towers. Five of the towers had their top sections collapse, and one tower completely collapsed. Several center pivot irrigation systems were overturned. The tornado then crossed into Pemiscot County, Missouri. Peak winds in Dunklin County were estimated at 140 mph.

The tornado seemed to reach its peak intensity as it moved into Pemiscot County, Missouri from Dunklin County, Missouri. A home along County Road 454 was substantially damaged. Further northeast, near Highway J and County Road 407, two homes were completely destroyed with debris carried off to the northeast. A fatality occurred in one of these homes. Several vehicles, including semi-tractor-trailers, were blown off of the road as the tornado crossed Interstates 55 and 155, resulting in another fatality. An indirect fatality occurred when a vehicle struck a downed utility pole. Aerial and satellite imagery showed ground scouring marks in this area across the Mississippi River. The tornado then moved into Lake County, Tennessee. Peak winds in Pemiscot County were estimated at 170 mph.

The tornado tracked along the oxbows of the Mississippi River between Pemiscot County, Missouri, and Lake County, Tennessee. Aerial and satellite imagery showed ground scouring marks in this area across the Mississippi River.

The tornado tracked along the oxbows of the Mississippi River between Pemiscot County, Missouri, and Lake County, Tennessee. Aerial and satellite imagery showed ground scouring marks in this area across the Mississippi River.

After traveling along the Mississippi River the tornado crossed into Lake County, Tennessee southwest of Wynnburg. The tornado significantly damaged trees with debarking southwest of Wynnburg. Homes and shop buildings suffered substantial damage north of Wynnburg. The tornado approached the Reelfoot Lake area and caused significant damage to a hotel, convenience store, restaurant, and camping facilities in the Cypress Point area. Three fatalities occurred in this area. On the southeast shore of Reelfoot Lake, the tornado damaged cabins and numerous recreational vehicles that were parked in a storage area. The tornado then crossed into Obion County, Tennessee. Peak winds in Lake County were estimated at 165-170 mph.

The tornado crossed from Lake County to Obion County. The tornado's width was shrinking as it approached Samburg, however, it was still strong enough to damage homes, businesses, and city buildings in Samburg. Many homes suffered partial roof loss, and several mobile homes were separated from their undercarriages. A recreational vehicle in a mobile home park along Lake Drive in Samburg was destroyed, resulting in one fatality. The tornado continued northeast from Samburg, damaging several homes along Old Samburg Road. The last observed damage was west of Treece Road. Peak winds in Obion County were estimated at 130 mph.

The first observed damage was in Newbern, Tennesee near Washington Street. A convenience store was heavily damaged. Several outbuildings were damaged in Newbern. The elementary school and an auto shop suffered roof damage. The tornado moved northeast, uprooting and snapping numerous trees along its path, and then moved into Gibson County. Peak winds were estimated at 135 mph in Dyer County.

The tornado crossed from Dyer County into Gibson County and continued northeast, uprooting and snapping trees. Several homes had significant roof damage as the tornado moved across rural parts of the county. The tornado strengthened as it approached the city of Kenton causing significant damage to numerous homes. The tornado then crossed into Obion County. Peak winds were estimated at 140 mph in Gibson County.

The tornado moved from Gibson County into the southeast corner of Obion County. The tornado uprooted and snapped trees along its path and heavily damaged a couple of homes on Sidonia Kenton Road. The tornado then crossed back into Gibson County. Peak winds were estimated at 125 mph in Obion County.
The tornado crossed from Obion County back into Gibson County for a brief time causing more tree damage. The tornado then tracked northeast into Weakley County.

The tornado tracked from Gibson County northeast into Weakley County. The tornado passed north of Sharon mainly uprooting and snapping trees. The tornado strengthened as it approached Dresden causing significant damage to several homes along Highway 89. The tornado was at its peak intensity as it moved through Dresden. Numerous homes and businesses were destroyed or damaged in Dresden. In total, 187 homes were damaged in Weakley County with 100 of those being complete losses. Twenty-one businesses were also affected across the county. The tornado continued northeast and moved into Henry County. Peak winds were estimated at 160 mph in Weakley County.

The tornado crossed from Weakley County into Henry County. The tornado damaged or destroyed several homes near Cottage Grove. The tornado continued northeast toward Buchanan mostly uprooting and snapping trees. A few homes and mobile homes were damaged near Buchanan. As the tornado approached Kentucky Lake several mobile homes were significantly damaged. The tornado then crossed into Calloway County, Kentucky. Peak winds in Henry County were estimated at 150 mph.

The supercell that produced the long track EF-4 tornado from Craighead County, Arkansas into western Obion County, Tennessee reintensified and formed another tornado in northern Obion County near Woodland Mills. A home suffered roof damage on Woodland Mills Road and trees were uprooted north of Woodland Mills. The tornado then crossed into Fulton County and eventually intensified into an EF-4 as it approached Mayfield, Kentucky. Peak winds in Obion County were estimated at 75 mph.
Strong gradient winds ahead of an approaching cold front knocked down a few trees across DeSoto County.
Seventeen train cars were derailed near the West Memphis-Marion border off of Mound City Road.
Numerous trees were knocked down from Orange Mound into East Buntyn. Several trees fell onto houses and vehicles. A fatality occurred when a large tree landed on a house.
A tree was knocked down across Alta Vista Avenue in Frasyer.
A tree fell on a home on Broadway, causing significant damage to the structure.
A tree fell on a house on East Shelby Drive and a utility pole was knocked down on Castle Heights Drive.
A tree and utility pole was knocked down on Frank Road near Houston Levee.
A large tree was knocked down in Olive Branch.
A tree fell on a fence in Oakfield. The siding was blown off parts of the house.
A large tree was knocked down on River Road near Mantachie.
Numerous trees were knocked down across Belmont resulting in several road closures.

Powerful straight-line winds destroyed a mobile home on Cottonwood Corner Road west of Osceola. Several power lines were knocked down in Osceola. Trucks were overturned west of Osceola and a truck was blown off I-55. Power lines were knocked down in Luxora.
Straight-line winds caused roof damage to a business south of the EF-2 tornado track in Trumann.
Outbuildings were damaged east of Blytheville.
Trees were uprooted in Natchez Trace State Park south of the EF-2 tornado track.
Straight-line winds caused roof damage to outbuildings on Prospect Road in northwest Decatur County.
Straight-line winds damaged several outbuildings and caused tree damage along West Shawtown Road.
Trees snapped on Cecil Roberts Road in Obion County.
